title: 历史实现参考
text: 历史实现参考 早期实现涉及的同步协议、恢复机制和验证范围，可通过以下文档继续查阅。当前可用能力请以使用指南与当前实施状态为准。 同步与恢复 - 多库、多目标同步配置 - 恢复与一致性 - 消息目标与投递协议 - 数据校验与修复 部署与验证 - 多节点部署与恢复 - 兼容性与能力边界 - 验证记录汇总 - 性能与运行时记录

title: Account management
text: Local accounts, roles, grants and token recovery 中文：账号管理. Related: task grants, audit. Scope and interface Administrators open Accounts and grants to create identities, edit roles/task scopes, disable/re-enable, rotate tokens and delete accounts. VIEWER/OPERATOR cannot call account administration APIs. These are local Bearer-token identities, not password login or OIDC; external providers remain unfinished. VIEWER reads granted tasks, OPERATOR also controls them, ADMIN manages globally. An empty selected list grants no tasks; all current/future tasks uses taskIds: null . ADMIN cannot be scoped. Unloaded task IDs are retained for advance grants; wildcards are rejected. The last enabled ADMIN cannot be disabled, deleted or demoted. Deletion retains audit identity: the token is revoked and the ID cannot be reassigned. Disabled accounts can be re-enabled. The directory supports at most200 identities including tombstones,10000 exact task IDs per identity; this is not an external-directory capacity claim. Configuration and managed authority Default accessMode: CONFIG preserves startup configuration behavior. authToken/users may reference environment variables. The account page initially displays them read-only. Reviewing the list and explicitly enabling managed accounts transfers them into the durable directory. Once activated, controller.json is authoritative, even if configuration still says CONFIG. Restart does not overwrite managed tokens/grants from old configuration. Changing a Secret/environment variable is not automatic managed-account rotation. Startup configuration still undergoes syntax/identity validation. To remove bootstrap credentials after initialization, use platform-managed.yml: accessMode: MANAGED , no authToken/users , same controller/task directories. An empty directory without an administrator fails startup; it never creates anonymous access. Linux/Docker retain the same persistent directory. Helm values-managed.yaml and native Kubernetes manifest omit bootstrap-token Secret injection. They require initialized controller storage and matching audit data; a new empty PVC cannot recover identities. Live Kubernetes/CSI acceptance remains pending. Tokens and uncertain responses The interface generates32 random bytes using browser crypto. Save the token and acknowledge that before submitting. Preview excludes it; lists/audit/responses never return tokens or their digests. New managed tokens require32–4096 visible ASCII characters; imported bootstrap tokens retain the24-character compatibility minimum. Use generated tokens rather than low-entropy strings. Only SHA-256 token digests are durable; authentication compares digests. No new persistent browser credential storage is used. Closing the editor/directory or signing out clears token inputs. Follow existing deployment security guidance for transport and bearer protection. Rotation immediately revokes the old token for subsequent requests. Successful self-rotation updates the page credential; disabling/deleting yourself signs you out. Permissions refresh on subsequent requests. Already accepted asynchronous operations may continue: revoking an identity is not pausing a dataflow. Task mutation commit checks the authorization revision and rejects stale callers with AUTHORIZATION CHANGED . After lost responses, unchanged drafts retry the same request identity/body. If the mutation committed and invalidated the session, sign in again and inspect the current directory. The server retains up to500 account mutation receipts; expired old requests still cannot bypass revision checks. If your self-rotation committed but its response was lost, use the previously saved new token. Do not delete state or modify synchronization checkpoints to fix login. Durability, concurrency and audit Mutations require expectedRevision and X-Request-ID . Concurrent edits return ACCOUNTS REVISION CHANGED ; reload and review. Identical retained requests do not reapply, and identifiers cannot be reused for another actor/body. Unknown fields and invalid scopes are refused. Directory changes, version and audit outbox are atomically saved together. Audit chain and a persistent directory-version anchor follow. Unavailable audit fails management requests; already committed changes recover through the outbox rather than pretending rollback. Events record actor/action/subject/version, never credentials. The audit interface shows the affected task/account. Legacy audit exports preserve original payload/hash bytes. Controller format2 is separate from pipeline configuration/checkpoint versions. Activating managed access upgrades controller state to version2 so old programs refuse it. Missing/older mismatched directory state fails startup rather than restoring bootstrap identities. Coordinate controller/audit/configuration-version backups. A coherent rollback of all stores can restore old permissions; there is no external immutable anchor to detect every coordinated old backup. Review revocations/tokens after restoration. Offline administrator recovery If every administrator token is lost: 1. Stop the controller; retain its storage and audit data. 2. Prepare platform configuration pointing to the same directories. Supply a configured ADMIN/token through authToken ( legacy-admin ) or users ; prefer an environment-provided random token. 3. Run: 4. The command requires the exclusive controller lock, restores only the selected configured administrator, preserves other identities and task intents, records ACCOUNT RECOVER , and starts no workers. It refuses while the controller runs. 5. Start the service, sign in and review identities/audit. Other configured credentials are not all reactivated. Missing/corrupt directory or mismatched audit is not mere token loss. Recovery does not bypass those guards; restore coordinated backups first. Do not manually lower state versions. API ADMIN only. Mutations require JSON, X-Request-ID , expectedRevision . Method/path Other fields --- --- GET /api/accounts Returns mode/revision/redacted identities POST /api/accounts/activate None; explicit durable management activation POST /api/accounts id,role,enabled,taskIds,token PUT /api/accounts/ id role,enabled,taskIds; token is refused POST /api/accounts/ id /token token DELETE /api/accounts/ id None; retained identity soft deletion Common409 codes: ACCOUNT LAST ADMIN , ACCOUNTS REVISION CHANGED , REQUEST ID REUSED , ACCOUNT EXISTS , ACCOUNT TOKEN COLLISION . Revoked tokens return401; account administration without permission returns403; ungranted task routes remain404. FAQ and evidence Will the old configured administrator work after restart? Managed access does not resurrect it. Explicit offline recovery restores the selected configured administrator. Does deleting an account stop its dataflows? No. Task intents are separate; an authorized operator must pause the dataflow. How do I revoke every task grant? Select scoped tasks, clear selections/additional IDs and save. Do not choose all current/future tasks. Can the controller be downgraded? Old programs refuse managed state version2. Synchronization checkpoint formats were not changed by account management, but controller rollback requires a separate migration. Actual Java8 release acceptance covered old-release audit/hash upgrade, SIGKILL persistence, older/missing directory refusal, old-program refusal, offline recovery and exclusive locking. Real MySQL→PostgreSQL verified grant revocation/rotation during CDC and no permission resurrection on restart, preserving stream/snapshot identity; see evidence. OIDC, passwords/MFA, distributed identity storage, multiple writing controllers and live K8s clusters remain unaccepted. See browser sessions for reload recovery, sign-out and invalidation of all sessions after directory changes.

title: Browser sessions
text: Browser sessions and login recovery 中文：浏览器会话. Specification: RM-SDD-001 SE-01/02/03/05. Shared sessions across controllers (SE-04) remain unfinished. Sign-in and recovery Sign in with an existing configured or managed-account token. The page exchanges Bearer credentials once through POST /api/session , clears the input, then authenticates with an HttpOnly cookie. Long-lived tokens are never saved in localStorage, sessionStorage or URLs. Reloading or opening the same site first calls GET /api/session to restore identity, grants and CSRF credentials, then loads tasks. Invalid sessions return to sign-in. Language preference may still use localStorage. A Store interface separates the session authority from HTTP handling. The current implementation is bounded memory: controller restart clears browser sessions and requires sign-in again . Tasks, accounts and audit retain their own persistence contracts. This does not provide session continuity across controllers; putting independent controllers behind a load balancer is not a supported cluster deployment. Sign-out clears UI permissions, drafts and raw differences immediately, then revokes the server session. BroadcastChannel tells other tabs to sign out; without it, their next request/poll discovers revocation. Sign-in and sign-out are serialized within each page so a delayed login response is also revoked. Late API responses cannot revive cleared UI state. If refresh discovers a different cookie session, it clears the previous identity drafts/details before restoring current grants. Failed server sign-out is reported and can be retried; clearing the page alone is not proof of revocation. Configuration PlatformConfig.sessions and the Helm top-level sessions have the same fields: Field Default Meaning --- --- --- enabled true Permit browser-session exchange; disabling it preserves Bearer APIs secureCookie true Production Host-rivomesh-session cookie; requires HTTPS, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Path=/ and no Domain publicOrigin unset Exact external origin behind a proxy, e.g. https://sync.example.com , with no trailing slash, path, query or user info idleSeconds 1800 Idle deadline after the last validated API request, including automatic polling; 30–86400 seconds absoluteSeconds 28800 Hard lifetime since sign-in, at least idleSeconds and at most 604800; polling cannot extend it rememberBrowser false Default session cookie; true adds Max-Age bounded by the absolute lifetime, but restart still invalidates it maximum 1000 Active sessions per controller, 1–10000; expired entries are purged on creation and capacity rejects new sign-ins These are adjustable policies, not throughput claims. Polling extends server idle time; a human-inactivity timeout is a separate future policy. Browser session-restore features may retain session cookies, so closing the browser does not replace sign-out. Production proxy configuration: Terminate TLS at the proxy; the controller remains HTTP. Restrict backend access to authorized networks and provide HTTPS to browsers. publicOrigin declares the external origin; client-supplied X-Forwarded- headers are not trusted. Without it, origin validation expects https://Host . Cookie-authenticated mutations require an exact Origin and matching X-CSRF-Token . The HTTP development preview at http://127.0.0.1:18088 and local examples explicitly set secureCookie: false , using rivomesh-dev-session . Use the HTTPS settings above in production. Helm defaults to Secure; local port-forward preview can explicitly use --set sessions.secureCookie=false . Production can set --set sessions.publicOrigin=https://sync.example.com . Edit the same ConfigMap fields for native Kubernetes manifests. API and revocation contract Request Authentication/result --- --- POST /api/session Valid Bearer only; returns identity, CSRF credential and absolute expiry, and issues Set-Cookie; browser Origin must match configuration GET /api/session Cookie returns identity, scope, csrfToken and expiresAt; Bearer retains its previous identity view and does not issue a cookie POST /api/session/logout Cookie + Origin + X-CSRF-Token; revokes the session and clears the cookie; available to all roles Other APIs Cookie mutations validate Origin/CSRF, then retain role, task-scope, revision, request-ID and audit checks An explicit Authorization header always uses Bearer validation and never falls back to a cookie. Valid credentials for different accounts return 409 AUTHENTICATION CONFLICT . Same-account explicit Bearer uses API rules without cookie CSRF. CLI/API clients need not adopt cookies. Session IDs and CSRF credentials never enter audit records; identity and operation outcomes do. The current strict directory-revision policy invalidates all existing browser sessions on that controller after any managed-account creation, modification, enable/disable, deletion, token rotation or managed activation . This includes the administrator making the change, who must sign in again. After a confirmed self-token rotation, the page can exchange the newly saved token for a fresh session automatically. Bearer credentials are still checked against the current directory on each request. Config-mode identity changes require restart, which clears sessions. Sign-out does not undo already executed task operations; inspect their operation records. FAQ and recovery - Sign-in appears after reload: check absolute expiry, controller restart, directory changes, cookie policy and origin. Requests switching between controllers are not yet supported. - HTTP sign-in does not persist: Secure cookies are not sent over HTTP. Explicitly disable Secure only for local development; configure HTTPS in production. Different hostnames/protocols do not share the session. - Independent deployments on different ports sign each other out: cookies are not isolated by port. Use different hostnames to avoid overwriting same-name cookies. The application uses root paths and does not support multiple controllers under different URL subpaths on one site. - 403 ORIGIN REJECTED: align the browser URL, publicOrigin, TLS and proxy configuration; preserve Origin/CSRF checks. - 403 CSRF REJECTED: reload to recover the current CSRF credential. Credentials from old pages/sessions cannot be reused. - Account edits sign everyone out: this is the current strict revision policy. Sign in again; disabled or rotated old tokens remain invalid. - 409 SESSION CAPACITY REACHED: closing a page does not revoke its session. Sign out unused sessions, wait for expiry, or increase maximum within the memory budget. Restart clears all sessions but is not routine capacity management. - Sign-out was not confirmed: restore connectivity/audit availability and retry sign-out. Another administrator can disable the account or rotate its token to trigger revision revocation. An API failure is not success. Acceptance covers single-controller real HTTP, a TLS proxy, expiry/revocation, Bearer conflicts and DOM races. Full-browser/accessibility and multi-controller acceptance remain separate. Consult this iteration's archived evidence for actual results.

title: ActiveMQ Classic
text: ActiveMQ Classic 中文：Classic 手册. The implementation uses native OpenWire persistent local transactions, an event queue and a separately retained receipt queue on one fixed broker. Independent actual-release Java8 native acceptance passed persistent publication, selected-consumer ACK, invalid-selector/purge refusal, restart and actual old nonempty-backup protection. MySQL8.4+PostgreSQL17 pipeline acceptance also passed snapshot/CDC, process kill, broker outage, SQL constraint repair/retry and purge isolation; this does not establish cluster acceptance. The fixture broker is Apache ActiveMQ 5.19.12. Java8 requires client5.16.8 (class version52); current5.18/5.19 clients require Java11. Client JMS/SLF4J/Hawtbuf packages are isolated from other SDKs. Client5.16 is an inactive line; maintain its dependency/security lifecycle separately from the current broker. See Apache downloads and archived releases. Use config/classic-v3.yml. Product is ACTIVEMQ CLASSIC , endpoint activemq://host:61616 (or activemqs://host:61617 ), explicit messaging.broker , stream prefix and authenticated HTTP(S) messaging.adminUrl ending /api/jolokia/ . Credentials are separate from URLs. check connects to OpenWire and reads broker/JMX capabilities without creating business queues. Wire broker ID/name must match management; persistent, non-slave KahaDB is required. HTTP redirects and ambiguous JSON/JMX responses cannot become confirmations. TLS requires a separately verified certificate and JVM trust configuration; no real TLS acceptance yet. Resources and consumer contract The physical event queue is prefix . 64-character binding hash ; the receipt queue appends .receipts . Both retain a persistent OWNER record with a random shared owner nonce, binding and both queue names. Source journal identity binds the nonce; native progress binds a receipt JMSMessageID and batch content digest. Consumers MUST use exactly: The application reads channel/key/event-ID properties and the ordinary V3 JSON bytes envelope. Deduplicate stable event IDs and stage/validate transaction boundaries, counts and ordinals before business commit. A producer confirmation is not consumer completion. Acknowledge events only after durable downstream commit; multiple consumers still need transactional staging/order handling. Never consume OWNER records or any receipt messages. Queue size includes the retained owner; it does not equal the number of outstanding event messages. Before publication, management checks that event subscriptions have the exact selector and that receipt queues have no subscriptions. External JMS browsers also count; use JMX browsing for administrative inspection. Broker ACLs must deny readers access to .receipts and deny OpenWire accounts permission to create missing queues. Bootstrap uses explicitly authorized JMX addQueue . An operator must retain OWNER/receipt records, disable inactive-destination GC, avoid expiry/discard policies and configure KahaDB journalDiskSyncStrategy=always and enableJournalDiskSyncs=true . The current standard MBeans do not prove all those policy/flush settings at runtime; provision and audit broker configuration. The isolated fixture illustrates the contract and is not a production secret file. Management needs read/search and narrowly authorized addQueue / getMessage ; destructive operations belong to a separately controlled recovery process. Confirmation and recovery One local JMS transaction writes the event batch and a persistent receipt, then native receipt content is read back. Only then can the fenced source journal save transport progress and schema/snapshot/transaction confirmation. Lost responses can replay the same application event IDs; no distributed XA or exactly-once downstream guarantee is claimed. An older owner's in-flight request cannot be revoked by journal fencing; shared pause remains explicitly unconfirmed until quiescence is established. Resume validates both ownership records and the last saved receipt before any resource creation/publication. Missing initialized queues, owner changes, missing or changed receipts require a recovery/rebuild plan. Normal EVENT consumption retains ownership and receipts. Whole-store rollback can retain old owner IDs; the later receipt is still required. Arbitrary selective deletion of historical events is not a complete-history checksum and cannot be repaired by ordinary resume. Receipt retention/compaction is not implemented. Metadata grows per publication batch, and native message lookup can scan retained queue history. Capacity/soak, replication/failover, network connectors, TLS and broader mixed-product pipeline acceptance remain required; do not extrapolate single-broker transport checks to those profiles. FAQ Why separate receipts? Ordinary queue consumers remove events. A durable receipt must survive consumer acknowledgments to verify a later restart/backup. Wrong selector or lost owner? Stop the consumer, preserve remaining history, review the gap and repair/rebuild under a plan. Resume retries the failed source transaction; it never recreates ownership over initialized empty queues. Broker outage? Connection/HTTP transport failures retry from the persisted checkpoint. Authentication, policy or confirmed-history failures pause this target. Other target subscriptions keep their independent checkpoints. Can I use a failover URI or several independent brokers? Not in this first profile. Keep one direct endpoint and management for that same broker; future replicated/failover profiles need separate identity and store acceptance. HTTP403 from a current broker? Classic5.19.12 also defaults Jetty management access to loopback IPs. Authorize the synchronization worker's actual management network using explicit InetAccessHandler include rules, retaining authentication and Jolokia permissions. HTTP403 is not evidence of a missing queue. Queue existence uses successful exact-MBean searches because the server may redact exception types; failed management calls never authorize resource recreation. Strict origin checks with a Java8 worker: Java's URLConnection does not send a manually supplied Origin header by default. The client sends Referer containing the management endpoint's own scheme/authority. Allow that exact origin in Jolokia CORS policy and retain strict checking; no global JVM header override is required. Jolokia explicitly supports Referer fallback in its security manual. Native HTTP200 plus Jolokia status403 remains an access failure, not a queue absence. The accepted fixture policy allows both http://classic:8161 and http://classic:8161/ : this Jolokia version compares the full Referer value, including its trailing slash. For another deployment, allow the exact value management-scheme :// management-authority / , retaining strict checking. Recorded acceptance target/classic-subscription-selector-fixed.log :2 SDK classification tests and 63 core/API tests passed,0 failures/errors/skips. target/ui-classic-first.log :20 DOM passes. target/classic-native-selector-fixed.log : actual release/native Java8 acceptance described above. Release145723459bytes SHA256 1a1945e3f91658e3f666a79af66b5da1d6ec0eb8ea2ff00cd3d9f8242a017115. Earlier native logs failed and are not acceptance. target/classic-pipeline-first.log built successfully but its harness failed because the Maven Java8 image has no Python; it is not acceptance. The corrected target/classic-pipeline-prebuilt.log passed ONE actual release pipeline case, with host verification of fresh source/tests and native inspector classes compiled against that release. Source/MySQL and target/PostgreSQL were real, with LOCAL H2 journal. Both pre/post SHA256 were 6eb2a8bb053fcf777b765713e5c21aeb675e586f53c79098e5dffb2103afb954, 145723578bytes. Snapshot/current rows were reconstructed from received envelopes by stable IDs, row identities and completed transactions. The consumer persists its received batch before ACK. Worker SIGKILL, broker outage/catch-up, PostgreSQL CHECK failure with Classic continuing, removing the constraint/resuming its original error generation, and purging the initialized Classic queue with SQL continuing all passed. Pause reports SQL FENCED and MQ UNCONFIRMED. Run bash tests/classic-pipeline-run.sh ; an unchanged verified release can use RIVOMESH TEST PREBUILT=1 . Python runs on the host for verification, not as a runtime dependency in the Maven/JRE8 containers. All own resources were cleaned. Final package: target/classic-final-unit-package.log 2 SDK +63 core/API passes,0fail/error/skip; UI20 passes. Current145723617-byte release SHA256290adcc746a64c427ccefc6de712b8fbb7bbdc7ed4d48fcd2757485e99b6c2fe. All65091 class files were compared with the accepted pipeline release; only AdapterCatalog.class changed (status text). Runtime protocol resources are byte-identical. See archived evidence.

title: ClickHouse
text: ClickHouse versioned materialization 中文：ClickHouse 手册. V3 supports a direct ClickHouse HTTP/HTTPS destination alongside transactional databases and message destinations. The accepted initial server is ClickHouse 25.8.33.6, using Atomic databases, local MergeTree receipts and ReplacingMergeTree data. The business names are query views using FINAL and filtering tombstones. This profile serves analytical queries; transactional business takeover requires its own database/application compatibility assessment. Configure and start Use the complete example. Set product: CLICKHOUSE , a direct http://host:8123 or https://host:8443 endpoint, separate username/password, an exclusive metadata database and explicit source-database to target-database mappings. Authentication material is never placed in the URL. The endpoint accepts no credentials, query parameters or non-root path. Use the normal V3 multi-target wizard or YAML import; credentials are masked in previews. check reads source/catalog capabilities and checks ClickHouse UInt128, canonical-query formatting and required MergeTree settings. It creates no target database/table. run requires database/table/view creation, INSERT and SELECT permissions, including access to the relevant system catalog. Existing non-Atomic databases and foreign business objects are rejected. A missing initialized object is not silently recreated at an old checkpoint. One deployment can configure several target instances and independently mapped databases. Use a fixed direct server endpoint for this profile. Load-balancing between independent servers, Distributed/Replicated/Shared engines, Keeper failover and ClickHouse Cloud require separate profiles and acceptance. Data and indexes Source representation Initial ClickHouse storage --- --- Boolean UInt8, retaining NULL where allowed Signed / unsigned integers Int64 / UInt64 Decimal Decimal with source precision/scale, up to 76 digits Float32 / Float64 Native binary floating point; nonfinite values rejected Text / JSON String; JSON number text remains lossless Binary / geometry Raw String bytes, decoded from the internal base64 wire value Date / time / datetime / timestamp Lossless String, including values outside native temporal ranges SQL NULL Nullable flag; distinct from JSON literal null Generated columns Source/normalizer-computed values, stored as ordinary columns Temporal text avoids truncating MySQL's wide calendar range and TIME durations. Use explicit analytical conversion expressions where appropriate. Original schema details remain in the owned metadata. MySQL collation, default-expression and generated-expression execution semantics are not installed in ClickHouse. Logical identity keys feed stable row identities; source sequence and row ordinal select the latest version. Identical keyless occurrences retain separate identities, and a delete removes one occurrence. PK moves delete the old identity and insert the new one. Query business views to obtain the logical current rows; underlying physical parts can contain earlier versions and replay duplicates. uniquePolicy: DOWNGRADE BUSINESS is required. Business UNIQUE constraints are not enforced in ClickHouse. Source PK/identity selection is retained through the versioned view. All target writes during synchronization belong to the synchronization service, as agreed for constraint downgrades. Secondary index conversion The new-task wizard and example explicitly set clickhouse.secondaryIndexes: DATA SKIPPING . For backward compatibility, omitted options retain the earlier NONE data-only profile. check returns clickhouseIndexPlans , with each source index, action, reason and physical index names. The accepted table schema record persists that plan. Source secondary index Physical access structure --- --- BTREE, business UNIQUE, simple column GSI/GLOBAL/GLOBAL BTREE One non-unique skipping index per indexed column Numeric/boolean/decimal column minmax , granularity 1 Text/binary/temporal-text column bloom filter(0.01) , granularity 1 Composite or descending index Split into per-column structures; source ordering is not reproduced Repeated column across indexes One shared physical index Expression, prefix, FULLTEXT/SPATIAL or unsupported column type REQUIRES PLAN ; automatic table creation stops Source primary/identity key Retained by stable row identity; never weakened into optional acceleration These structures do not enforce uniqueness, provide a B-tree point lookup, reproduce MySQL collation/order, or retain GSI routing/global uniqueness. They accelerate matching analytical predicates where data distribution permits; a planner may choose not to use them. Temporal String indexes accelerate equality, not native calendar-range operations. Bloom false positives add reads, not rows. See the official skipping-index guide. Generated views explicitly enable use skip indexes if final=1 and use skip indexes if final exact mode=1 . Exact mode expands candidate ranges to include newer versions before FINAL; disabling it can resurrect stale matches. The accepted server's settings source describes that requirement. Do not edit the owned view or query physical history as if it were the current business table. New table creation checks the complete canonical definition, including indexes, before persisting schema confirmation. Index/view alterations after confirmation pause this target. Earlier data-only ClickHouse tasks: omitted options or explicit clickhouse.secondaryIndexes: NONE retain the original configuration fingerprint and existing layout. This is an explicit index omission, recorded as OMIT BY CONFIGURATION , not a completed conversion. Changing from NONE to DATA SKIPPING changes the fingerprint; it does not run ALTER against initialized data. Use a separately planned new generation and snapshot/rebuild. Do not erase journal metadata to bypass this guard. The UI wizard uses DATA SKIPPING for new tasks; importing YAML supports either mode. Omitted fields in earlier task files do not trigger an automatic layout migration. Confirmation and recovery Rows use native RowBinary, bounded requests and synchronous inserts. Each batch groups rows by table; writes precede a durable native receipt, which precedes the fenced application-journal checkpoint. Receipt/data tables request fsync after insert=1 , fsync part directory=1 and min rows to fsync after merge=1 . Actual power-loss and storage-controller behavior still require hardware testing. HTTP 200 alone cannot confirm a ClickHouse query. The client checks exception headers, complete JSON/count/shape and an empty command response; it rejects trailing error bodies and redirects. The HTTP client does not automatically repeat a request after losing its response. The sink replays through stable versions and receipt checks, without claiming SQL transaction atomicity. VERSIONED MATERIALIZATION means rows and tables within one source transaction may become visible in separate batches. Full-copy rows can also be visible before snapshot completion. Monitor the durable target checkpoint and snapshot acknowledgements when deciding whether a dataset has caught up. Each target has independent checkpoints and error generations. Network failures retry automatically; permanent SQL/schema/ownership failures pause that target and retain its original events. Other targets continue until shared journal capacity/backpressure requires intervention. After correcting a retryable plan or permission issue, use the console's generation-bound target resume. Resume retries the original data and never skips it. Shared pause reports UNCONFIRMED IN FLIGHT MATERIALIZATION : it fences the application journal but cannot retract an HTTP write already running on the server. A business cutover must establish quiescence and reconciliation first. Do not infer a transactional target's exact local SQL fence here. Operational FAQ Why are both metadata and physical data tables present? The service owns generation/fingerprint comments, stable object UUIDs, schema records and native batch receipts. Keep them with the data. They are part of recovery, not disposable temporary tables. Their retention/compaction and large-catalog capacity work remain explicit platform backlog. Can consumers read only the business view? The view uses invoker security. Grant the consumer SELECT on that view and its specific underlying physical data table, without INSERT/ALTER/DROP. SHOW CREATE TABLE target database.table identifies the physical dependency. Queries should use the business view's version/tombstone selection. Credentials, grants and user management remain the database administrator's responsibility. The target restored an older nonempty backup. Can it resume? Startup checks the saved native receipt and schema/object identities. Missing or changed confirmed history raises a rebuild-required error, even if old UUIDs remain. Retain the journal and investigate the backup boundary. Reconciliation/rebuild planning is required; deleting receipt rows or creating empty replacement views does not repair a checkpoint. Arbitrary earlier-row corruption is not proven absent by checking the latest receipt. What if journal storage disappears? LOCAL requires its original persistent directory; shared/multi-host operation requires an EXTERNAL transactional journal. Target rows alone cannot reconstruct keyless identities, capture positions and all receipts. Restore coordinated metadata or plan a full rebuild; independent metadata rollback is not an automatic recovery contract. Why does a decimal string omit trailing zeros? ClickHouse formatting can omit them. Verify the numeric value and declared precision/scale; the native acceptance checks both, including Decimal(65,30). Can I edit schemas, clear tombstones or write target rows? Synchronization assumes exclusive service writes. Schema/UUID changes are checked; arbitrary external DML can invalidate materialization. Preserve tombstones and receipt history. Live source DDL, nonempty foreign-target adoption, automatic repair and business takeover remain separate planned workflows. Recorded acceptance target/clickhouse-native-protocol-decimal.log : real server typed boundaries, binary/JSON/NULL, UInt128 version replay, restart identity/history and deletion. target/clickhouse-materializer-release.log : actual release JAR, read-only check, automatic tables/views, PK move, keyless multiplicity/delete, duplicate replay, client/server restart and refusal after restoring an older nonempty target. target/clickhouse-pipeline-first.log : 24 executions passed, including a real MySQL 8.4 → ClickHouse + PostgreSQL release-JAR pipeline with LOCAL H2 journal, JSON/unsigned/decimal/ binary/generated columns, target outage with SQL continuing, automatic catch-up, worker kill/restart, and missing-view isolation. target/ui-clickhouse-first.log : 18 DOM cases passed. These do not establish replicated/cluster/TLS/power-loss, large-catalog/soak or all-JRE ClickHouse acceptance. Final compatibility acceptance: target/clickhouse-index-compat-unit.log 58PASS/0fail/error/skip and target/ui-clickhouse-index-compat.log 19PASS. target/clickhouse-index-native-compat.log actual-release Java8 native acceptance passed explicit NONE create/reopen without indexes plus indexed FINAL/replay/restart/old-volume rollback protection. Omitted config options retain NONE and the old fingerprint; new wizard/example explicitly opt into DATA SKIPPING. Current artifact144098892bytes SHA25695dbdbb462929ed1a262072e80d1db885696fa53007d5315c38c4d951c193212. Earlier28-pipeline acceptance predates this default-only compatibility adjustment. All own test resources cleaned.

title: COMMON_CUT repair
text: COMMON CUT repair: initial CLI The first MySQL8.4/PostgreSQL17 repair profile passed all four real journal modes. Evidence. Broader production/vendor/capacity acceptance remains incomplete. The console now offers authenticated plan review,execution,cancellation and retry;see Managed repair. A completed, sealed SQL row report and its unchanged globally PAUSED cut are required. Initial execution is limited to MySQL/PostgreSQL transactional destinations owned by this task with completed snapshots and matching schemas. Only the synchronizer may write business tables, including during repair. Accepted initial tables are synchronizer-created with no triggers/foreign keys. The executor rejects detected triggers,incoming/outgoing FKs and PostgreSQL row policies/inheritance;MySQL requires verifiable metadata visibility. Full dependency migration planning is not implemented;see the managed handbook. Other vendors, analytical destinations and queues need separate repair protocols/acceptance. A destination blocked on an earlier failed transaction cannot necessarily reach this cut. Fixing the SQL cause and retrying the original transaction remains its recovery path. Failed-transaction before-image compensation, manual skipping and explicit consistency-gap handling are pending; do not change GTIDs/checkpoints to bypass errors. Review and execution Use the effective V3 task configuration and private report directory: Select explicit nonmatching target/table identities from the report, not SQL table names. The first command writes REPORT UUID/repair-plans/PLAN UUID.json and prints its review content/hash. Review exact table scope, schema/data roots, missing/extra/changed counts and budgets before passing its SHA256 to execution. Plans bind source seal, configuration fingerprint, generation, epoch, sequence, error version and physical destination checkpoints; they contain no raw business values. Keep report/plan files private. REQUEST UUID is a UUID generated for this request. CLI actor IDs are trusted host-operator assertions, not Web authentication, dual approval or controller audit. Do not expose this CLI through an anonymous HTTP wrapper. Authenticated managed repair with revision checks/durable jobs is separately implemented in the managed handbook. Defaults:100000 differing identities,1GiB probe budget per table,4MiB row limit,a10minute paused write-phase budget. Report integrity checks and connection preflight take additional time;this is not a10minute whole-job deadline. Plans retain the full certificate with an8MiB file ceiling. Compact certificates/paged planning and UI budget editing remain pending. Logical quotas require filesystem/container hard quotas for physical enforcement. Transactions and recovery Reports are rechecked for source seal, raw-row integrity, historical destination roots and plan identity. A journal job-row lock prevents concurrent resume/ownership changes. Each table keeps one physical destination checkpoint lock/connection through a full live scan, private disk sort, business DML, full post-scan and receipt commit. The live root/count must match the reported before state. Extra/changed rows are deleted first, then missing/changed source rows inserted. Keyless occurrence IDs are preserved exactly, including duplicate rows. Post-scan root/count must equal the sealed source. Business changes and rm3 sink repair receipt commit in the same local transaction without advancing stream sequence, GTID, transaction ID/hash. Receipts contain plan/schema/before/after hashes, unchanged checkpoint, counts, actor assertion, request hash and timestamp; no business values. Explicit preparation creates only receipt metadata, never missing job/schema/ownership metadata. MySQL DDL may implicitly commit, so fences are reacquired before business work; business tables and all three metadata tables must use InnoDB. Existing receipt columns and primary key are checked; do not drop metadata to bypass identity errors. - SQL failure, drift, corrupt report, count mismatch, quota or deadline rolls back the current table and leaves the pipeline paused. Retry the same plan after fixing its cause; changed target contents require a new validation/plan. - Lost commit reply or process restart:retry the same plan/hash. A matching destination receipt returns alreadyApplied=true without repeating DML. - Multiple tables/targets use separate local transactions. Earlier tables may already be committed when a later table fails. Receipts support partial-progress retry; there is no cross-destination ACID promise. - Once every table is committed, historical receipts can resolve even after resume. They do not prove current live equality. No automatic resume occurs. Review receipts/results, explicitly resume with existing controls and obtain a new cut/report when needed. The original report remains historical and retains its differences. FAQ and boundaries Arbitrary nonempty adoption/schema changes, dependency ordering for foreign keys/triggers, constraint restoration and cutover remain separate work. Deleting changed identities before inserts permits same-table UNIQUE value swaps, but does not establish cross-table/vendor compatibility. SQL failures roll back the current table. Normal exit removes owned probe files. SIGKILL may leave private scratch directories; retry creates fresh probes and never accepts incomplete sorted output. Full scratch retention/cleanup remains pending; never remove active directories. The journal and destination are not a distributed transaction. Journal pause locks guard controls, while destination locks/checkpoints and receipts guard local ordering/commit identity. Extended journal-disconnect/network-partition/node-loss matrices remain pending.

title: Configuration revisions
text: Configuration revisions 中文：配置编辑. The console edits configuration, rotates credentials and restores revisions without resetting checkpoints. The actual Java 8 release passed a MySQL 8.4 → PostgreSQL 17 pipeline covering target password rotation, revision restore and controller restart. See the acceptance record for its scope. Only ADMIN can read/edit configuration or its history. GET responses replace passwords, tokens and credential-bearing URLs/options with opaque references; they do not return saved values or ENV references. Retain the reference to keep a value, replace it with a new string to rotate it, or use null/empty where the adapter permits clearing. References are scoped to task, revision, location and target identity. Do not move them between targets. A restart or conflicting edit can require reloading references. No configuration is echoed by a save response. Stop the local task first; a completed PAUSE also permits editing. Pending controls and running workers block updates. Preview reports changed paths and whether migration is required, without old/new secret values. The task ID, synchronization fingerprint and physical journal binding must remain unchanged for this workflow. Changing mappings, products, semantic profiles, databases or journal location requires a separate migration plan. A v2 URL containing embedded credentials is part of its legacy fingerprint: use dedicated password fields for ordinary rotation; this editor does not rewrite legacy checkpoint identity. Save preserves STOPPED/PAUSED intent. Check connections, then explicitly start/resume; shared pause/error generation is never bypassed by a configuration update. Each committed configuration has immutable owner-readable YAML and metadata files under dataDirectory/config-versions/ taskId / . Metadata links its parent hash, editor identity, request ID and time. The controller registry atomically selects one head; staged unreferenced files are not committed history. Canonical task YAML and worker-config files become repairable projections. Workers launch from the committed version, whose content is checked before launch. A missing projection is repaired on restart; a damaged committed version blocks the task and never silently falls back to an older file. Back up the registry, versions, original task files and journal coherently. Existing externally supplied files retain their original startup loading mode until edited through this workflow. UI-created/edited files are controller-managed; editing a projection on disk does not change the committed configuration. Use the editor/API. Independent CLI task files remain ordinary files. Historical versions retain prior credentials: protect the entire private directory, not just current YAML. Automatic version/orphan retention cleanup is not implemented. History is paginated in 20-record pages with signed cursors. Restore previews the paths that change, then creates a new revision linked to the current head; it does not delete history or revert database checkpoints. Old history cursors/references may expire after controller restart or a new configuration head. Fetch history again. Idempotency receipts remain actor/role-bound; their existing bounded retention is separate from configuration history. Version integrity hashes detect corruption relative to the registry. This is configuration provenance, not a tamper-proof security audit against privileged filesystem administrators. Denied/authentication events and asynchronous results now use the separate security audit with retention/export. Exact task authorization is implemented. External immutable anchors and account management remain unfinished. Console workflow 1. Sign in as ADMIN, select a task and open Configuration & history . You can inspect and prepare changes while running; stop the local worker or finish pause before saving. 2. Edit usernames, snapshot chunk rows, poll/retry intervals. For passwords/tokens, choose Keep current value , Replace or Clear . Saved values stay hidden. Advanced JSON supports other fields; newly typed credentials are visible there. 3. Preview changes and review paths. Migration-required changes cannot overwrite the task. Editing again invalidates the preview. 4. Save, check connections/objects, then explicitly start or resume. Saving never starts a worker, clears shared pause or skips a failed transaction. 5. Select a committed revision, preview restore, then save the restore as a new revision. Check connections again: old credentials can fail after a database password change. Closing the editor or signing out clears drafts. Sensitive historical revisions remain in private storage. Load more after each 20 records; the separate 40-operation limit does not truncate configuration history. FAQ Does editing repeat the snapshot? Credential/runtime edits preserve synchronization and journal identity. Actual acceptance retained stream/snapshot identity and continued CDC. Mapping, identity or journal-location changes require migration. What if a task file is edited or deleted? Managed projections are repaired from the committed version. Do not edit projections to change configuration. Damaged versions/registry require a coherent backup restore; removing them is not a recovery shortcut. Why is a revision/history reference rejected? Reload current configuration/history and review concurrent changes. Controller restart or a new configuration head can invalidate old references. What if the old worker cannot stop? WORKER STOP UNCONFIRMED blocks updates. Identify and handle the old process before proceeding; do not bypass confirmation by starting a second configuration. Why are projections pending after save? The version is committed. Repair storage capacity/permissions or conflicting directories and let the controller retry. Keep the registry, versions and journal intact. API - GET /api/tasks/ id /configuration : redacted document and optimistic revision. - POST .../configuration/validate : config, expectedRevision or YAML variant. - PUT .../configuration : same body plus X-Request-ID ; immutable commit. - GET .../configuration/history[?cursor=...] : metadata and restore references. - POST .../configuration/restore/validate : reference, expectedRevision . - POST .../configuration/restore : same body plus X-Request-ID . VIEWER/OPERATOR are rejected before reading mutation bodies or config documents. Version history returns metadata only. Concurrent/stale edits receive 409; malformed or oversized/deep documents receive 400. A successful save can include configurationProjectionPending=true when a non-authoritative file cannot yet be materialized. Preserve the version directory and fix storage permissions/capacity; the controller retries projection repair. It does not pretend an uncommitted file write succeeded or erase previous history.

title: Console & deployment
text: Console, multiple tasks, and deployment Updated: 2026-11-17. 中文：控制台与部署. This page describes implemented behavior; see platform design for the full roadmap. Runtime scope Load independent MySQL task configurations into isolated JVMs with bounded heap/concurrency. V3 supports explicit databases/mappings, SQL/message fan-out, keyless/JSON/supported generated columns and LOCAL/EXTERNAL journals. The wizard supports Gauss/PostgreSQL/MySQL, the eight implemented message products plus ClickHouse and Doris; v2 single-target tasks remain supported. See the V3 manual and messaging contract. Capability entries distinguish remaining adapters. The bilingual workbench provides creation, connection/source-object checks, start/stop, shared pause/resume, progress/backlog, and operation history. Independent VIEWER/OPERATOR/ADMIN tokens enforce access. ADMIN can edit configuration, rotate credentials and restore revisions. Row validation and reviewed repairs at a common paused cut are available; failed-transaction patches/skips, mapping migration and business cutover remain open. See validation and repair. Local task control is the default. Opt in with cluster.sharedAccess=true and cluster.sharedTasks=true for fixed-owner global tasks. Any entry manages authorized remote tasks while distinguishing durable admission, actual outcomes and uncertainty. See global control for private directories/keys, upgrade refusal, Helm and native two-node deployment. Automatic execution takeover remains open. Local startup Open http://127.0.0.1:8080 and enter RIVOMESH TOKEN. Default binding is loopback; tokens require at least 24 bytes and never belong in URLs. Use an appropriate TLS entry point/tunnel for remote access; the embedded server currently serves HTTP. Creation does not start replication. Check connections/objects first, then start. Checks read source definitions and test target connectivity without DDL; startup still validates empty initial targets and DDL/replication privileges. Advanced candidate-node configuration can be loaded from files. Independent configurations Place task YAML files in config/tasks and restart, or use the YAML import button/wizard. Paths resolve against platform.yml. Other directories are not scanned and external edits are not hot-reloaded. Externally supplied tasks not yet edited in the console use private worker snapshots; external reload requires controller restart and identity validation. UI-created/edited tasks use private committed versions and a registry head. Task YAML/worker snapshots are repairable projections; editing them does not change configuration. ADMIN uses Configuration & history to preview/save/restore. See the configuration handbook. Use unique jobIds and distinct replication client serverIds on the same physical topology. Configured destination business/metadata namespace overlap is rejected. Operators must also avoid overlapping physical destinations hidden behind aliases/VIPs. Invalid files are reported independently without blocking valid tasks. Setting Default Meaning --- ---: --- maxTasks 20 Maximum loaded tasks maxRunningTasks 2 Concurrent workers; others wait for capacity workerHeapMiB 256 Maximum worker heap; additionally budget native memory, controller, and databases controlThreads 4 Bound on checks/status/control concurrency pollMillis 3000 Scheduler/status interval autoStart false Initial intent for newly discovered files only; saved intent wins, UI creation always starts stopped Unexpected exits restart with backoff; after five exits CRASH LOOP requires repair and Start/retry. Saved running tasks recreate workers after controller restart using target checkpoints. Changed identity/connection configurations are not silently substituted. Stop, pause, resume - Stop local worker affects this controller's worker only; another deployed standby may take over. - Shared pause persists PAUSED and invalidates owners on initialized tasks. Before initialization only local intent is paused, reported as LOCAL PAUSED NOT INITIALIZED. - Resume after repair is bound to an error generation and retries the original failed transaction. Old requests cannot clear newer failures; restart does not bypass pause. No queues are deleted or GTIDs changed. Database administrators still repair source replication errors. Failed status reads show the last successful time and an explicit stale-data indication. The workbench shows at most 100 tables/task with the total count; other tables continue syncing. Full table status remains available through CLI; paginated search will follow. Durable files and APIs tasksDirectory stores configurations; dataDirectory/controller.json stores intent, revisions, and operation history using atomic replacement. A file lock permits one controller per directory; corrupt state is not silently reset. V2 checkpoints remain in target metadata. V3 stores capture/snapshot artifacts/subscriber ACKs in LOCAL or EXTERNAL journals, transactional checkpoints with target business data, and confirmed message receipts in the journal. LOCAL uses dataDirectory/journals/pipelineId; use EXTERNAL for cross-host HA. Never delete a journal and continue from old target checkpoints. dataDirectory/worker-configs holds the selected startup configurations and must receive the same credential protection as task files. Configuration files may contain credentials and are written with mode 0600. Task status APIs omit passwords, raw JDBC URLs, row payloads and snapshot key values. ADMIN configuration APIs return editable documents with opaque references for credentials and credential-bearing URLs; ordinary credential-free URLs are visible. Protect directories/backups too. Worker logs rotate between two approximately 8 MiB files and are not served by the Web API. API Purpose --- --- GET /healthz, /readyz Process probes without database side effects or authentication GET /api/tasks Sanitized tasks/status/load errors/operations POST /api/tasks Create stopped task using config object or yaml string GET /api/tasks/ id Single-task view POST /api/tasks/ id /actions START / STOP / PAUSE / RESUME / RESUME TARGET / CHECK GET /api/tasks/ id /configuration, /configuration/history ADMIN redacted configuration and revisions POST /api/tasks/ id /configuration/validate, /configuration/restore/validate ADMIN preview edits or restore PUT /api/tasks/ id /configuration, POST .../configuration/restore ADMIN commit/restore a new revision without reverting checkpoints GET /api/capabilities Implemented/partially verified/planned adapters Use Authorization: Bearer. Writes require JSON and X-Request-ID; actions carry expectedRevision and RESUME also global errorCount. RESUME TARGET needs subscriptionId and its independent errorCount. Message pause can leave in-flight publication unconfirmed and does not establish a business cutover fence. HTTP 202 means accepted, with final results under operations. Identical request replays are idempotent. Retain 500 request receipts and 40 operations/task; old requests remain subject to revision checks. One pending operation per task. Docker Compose exposes loopback port 8080, persists control/configuration data, and allows 90 seconds to stop. The image runs nonroot; MAVEN IMAGE/JAVA IMAGE build arguments support prepared internal bases. Images are not publicly published; build/import them. Review bundled driver distribution terms before external release. Linux service Install the JAR at /opt/rivomesh/rivomesh.jar and create a rivomesh account. Copy deploy/linux/platform.yml to /etc/rivomesh/platform.yml and place the token in administrator-readable /etc/rivomesh/platform.env. Install deploy/linux/rivomesh.service, allow the service account to write /var/lib/rivomesh, adjust the Java path, then run systemctl daemon-reload and systemctl enable --now rivomesh. Kubernetes: Helm and native manifests Build and push/import an accessible image first. Prepare a private, untracked .env file containing token=your-private-token: Choose one manager for these resources, not both. Native YAML is rendered from the same Chart defaults. Helm supports existing Secrets/PVCs, storage class, resources, and concurrency, with schema/template validation. Regenerate native manifests using helm template rivomesh deploy/helm/rivomesh --namespace rivomesh. The control plane currently uses one replica, Recreate updates, and persistent PVC. Scaling replicas does not provide controller HA. Existing per-task database lease recovery remains; coordinated multi-controller scheduling is future work. Source outages/paused tasks do not fail process probes. Restart after Secret/native ConfigMap changes under an operational plan while preserving task identity. Manifests include persistence, restricted privileges, read-only root filesystem, temporary storage, graceful shutdown, and probes. Validate actual clusters, CSI, architectures, and OS dependencies separately; rendering is not live Kubernetes acceptance. FAQ Does controller restart repeat the snapshot? Matching task configuration/intact target state resumes existing checkpoints. Controller files do not replace target data/checkpoints. Can another node write after pause? Shared pause uses the same task-row lock as business transactions, so old owners cannot commit new work after pause finishes. Before initialization, local pause has no global effect. Why is a task queued? maxRunningTasks is reached. Stop another worker or adjust configuration/restart within hardware capacity. Why did resume fail? The error generation changed, the target is unavailable, or configuration differs. Refresh/repair rather than editing checkpoints. Do these manifests run every planned target? No. They deploy implemented functionality; planned adapters remain marked unavailable. Development verification Maven verify runs unit/API tests; tests/matrix.sh covers platform and existing failover behavior on MySQL 8.0/8.4 with openGauss. Optionally run npm ci --prefix tests/ui --ignore-scripts and npm test --prefix tests/ui for the actual HTML/JavaScript DOM interactions. Node is a development-test dependency only, not a service requirement. After building, python3 tests/deployment-check.py --image rivomesh:0.1.0-SNAPSHOT checks Helm/native parity, nonroot image, authentication, file permissions, request replay, and volume recovery. It removes only its own containers/volumes and never deploys into user Kubernetes clusters. DOM tests do not replace real-browser visual, keyboard, and accessibility acceptance. Browser automation windows were unavailable here; that acceptance remains pending. Individual access roles Use platform-rbac.yml instead of the shared-token example, set its three token environment variables, then run java -jar rivomesh-app-0.1.0-SNAPSHOT.jar serve config/platform-rbac.yml . Each token must be distinct printable ASCII, 24–4096 characters; unresolved environment references are rejected. At most 32 configured users are accepted, with unique IDs and at least one ADMIN. Tokens are not passwords. Browser sign-in exchanges the token for a revocable short-lived session that survives reload; see sessions, HTTPS/CSRF and sign-out. Role Read tasks/status/catalog Check/start/stop/pause/resume existing tasks Create/import Read/edit configuration and revisions --- --- --- --- --- VIEWER Yes No No No OPERATOR Yes Yes No No ADMIN Yes Yes Yes Yes Roles determine actions; users[].taskIds can restrict VIEWER/OPERATOR to exact tasks. Omission preserves deployment-wide access, an empty array grants no tasks, and ADMIN is deployment-wide. See task grants and revocation. OPERATOR is restricted to CHECK, START, STOP, PAUSE, RESUME and RESUME TARGET; unknown future actions require ADMIN until explicitly authorized. The API rejects forbidden requests before reading a mutation body or invoking the task service. UI buttons reflect those permissions, but the server remains the enforcement boundary. GET /api/session returns the current identity, role, permissions and task scope, never tokens or other accounts. The console refreshes permissions and clears drafts on logout/auth loss; stale responses cannot clear a new login. Default CONFIG uses startup identities. After explicit managed activation, the durable directory is authoritative and restart/configuration changes do not overwrite managed grants. ADMIN account UI/API, rotation and offline recovery are documented in accounts. In CONFIG/bootstrap mode, authToken is the global legacy-admin ; omit it when using only individual accounts. Configured identities require distinct credentials. Managed activation preserves the current identities, after which the durable directory controls changes. Local user/grant UI, rotation and offline recovery are implemented. OIDC/SSO, token expiry and external immutable audit anchors remain unfinished. For Linux use the selected platform file in the existing service command/environment. For Docker or native Kubernetes mount it as the platform configuration and inject the referenced tokens through the deployment secret/environment mechanism. The default Helm/native profile keeps the backward-compatible shared token. For individual roles use the example below; neither profile embeds token values. Do not put literal tokens in committed values or exported diagnostic bundles. For Helm roles, provision Secret rivomesh-accounts with distinct admin-token , operator-token , viewer-token keys, then use helm upgrade --install rivomesh deploy/helm/rivomesh -n rivomesh -f deploy/helm/rivomesh/values-rbac.yaml . For manual YAML use deploy/kubernetes/rivomesh-rbac.yaml instead of the default manifest; choose one manager/profile for the same resources. Both native files are rendered from the Chart and checked for parity. Custom users use auth.users: [ id, role, secretRef: name, key ] , with auth.legacyTokenEnabled: false to disable shared access. At least one ADMIN is required. Duplicate IDs/Secret keys, invalid roles and literal token values are rejected during rendering; different Secret keys with equal actual credentials are rejected by the application at startup. For CONFIG/bootstrap identity only, Secret environment values are read at startup; updating a Secret requires a controlled rollout. Managed identities must instead be rotated through account UI/API. To omit bootstrap credentials use accessMode: MANAGED with matching initialized controller/audit storage; see accounts. New configurations created through HTTP record createdBy , createdRole , createdAt . Task operations record the authenticated actorId and actorRole , including their asynchronous outcome, and retain them across controller restart. The server supplies these fields; request-body identity fields cannot impersonate another account. New idempotency receipts also bind the request ID to that identity/role: matching identity replay is idempotent, another identity receives REQUEST IDENTITY CHANGED . Older receipts without attribution retain their compatibility behavior; old records and direct filesystem/internal API changes are not assigned an invented identity. This is bounded operational history: 40 operations per task and 500 request receipts in the controller registry; the UI displays the most recent eight operations. The independent global store records denied API/security events and asynchronous outcomes, with integrity checks, retention, export and an audit screen; see the security audit handbook. External immutable anchors remain unfinished. ClickHouse V3 targets use native versioned materialization and FINAL query views; transactions can become visible in separate row batches. The wizard defaults to non-unique skipping-index conversion. After Check , expand Check results and operation details in task history to review clickhouseIndexPlans , including unsupported indexes and lost uniqueness/order/global-routing guarantees. YAML import supports explicit clickhouse.secondaryIndexes: NONE for earlier data-only tasks; omitting the new field retains NONE automatically. See the ClickHouse handbook before changing profiles. The Doris wizard configures SQL/Stream Load HTTP origins, redirect allowlist, replicas/buckets and index policy. Default3 replicas; one-BE tests explicitly select1. Expand dorisIndexPlans in check results. Pause leaves materialization in flight unconfirmed, not a cutover barrier. Initial identity checks require a Doris ADMIN account; see the Doris handbook.

title: Development preview
text: Docker development preview The preview uses its own Compose project rivomesh-dev-preview , private state and loopback address <http://127.0.0.1:18088 . The account is admin . Its access token is stored in the owner-only target/development-preview/credentials.json ; enter the token in the login form. The current authentication flow does not require a separate username field. Never commit this file. UI resources are mounted directly from sync-app/src/main/resources/console ; refresh after edits. Responses disable caching. Backend and JDBC updates use a copied complete application JAR, isolated from Maven's output. After a successful backend build, deploy it with: The helper validates/copies the JAR, records its SHA-256, recreates only the preview container and checks health plus administrator authentication. UI and backend may temporarily represent different development stages. The capability catalog distinguishes experimental/planned adapters. This preview does not imply full product or scenario acceptance. Configuration/data formats may change during development and restarts briefly interrupt access. State persists under target/development-preview/state . Updates retain it; removing the entire target directory also removes preview state and credentials. To stop without deleting data: restart: unless-stopped restarts a previously running instance when Docker Desktop returns. An explicitly stopped instance needs start . Use host.docker.internal to reach host databases from this container, not 127.0.0.1 . Source MySQL still requires GTID and ROW/FULL configuration; check a task before starting it. 中文 Temporary acceptance containers are removed after use rather than retained for reuse. The live development console and currently running builds/tests stay available. Cleanup is scoped to this project; it does not globally prune other services. The registry preview now uses two independent controller directories and one shared PostgreSQL control store. The second endpoint is http://localhost:18089 ; credentials match but sessions are separate. Task actions remain local at this stage. See node registry.

title: 达梦 DM
text: DM destination and FAQ 中文：达梦 V3. Example: dm-v3.yml. Scope and instance requirements product: DM is wired into V3 configuration, CLI, bilingual wizard, independent transactional destinations and type plans. Availability remains EXPERIMENTAL . The first DM8.1.4.80 ARM64/vendor Java8 JDBC8.1.3.140 native transaction and actual MySQL8.4.13+PostgreSQL17.12 snapshot/CDC/outage/catchup/worker-kill/separate-SQL-repair/missing-table isolation profile passed; see evidence. Empty-layout guards, text-key case/trailing spaces and four-byte Unicode also passed. PostgreSQL-protocol results do not prove DM support. Use dm.jdbc.driver.DmDriver , jdbc:dm://host:5236 , and pinned Maven Central com.dameng:DmJdbcDriver18:8.1.3.140 . The vendor POM declares Apache-2.0; full distribution license/NOTICE review remains pending. Database installation packages/licenses are not distributed with Rivomesh. The first profile requires COMPATIBLE MODE=0, UNICODE FLAG=1(UTF8), CASE SENSITIVE=1, BLANK PAD MODE=1, NORMAL/PRIMARY and OPEN instance state, and IMMEDIATE/BATCH,WAIT COMMIT WRITE. Each physical connection verifies vendor/version, instance role and these conditions, sets session UTC and checks empty strings remain distinct from NULL. It never changes global parameters or promotes a replica. WAIT is local log-flush durability, not a substitute for storage, replication or fencing policy. Encoding/blank-padding are initialization choices. They protect quoted identifiers, VARCHAR primary keys and trailing-space identities from merging. Other mode/parameter combinations need separate adaptation. Have the DBA assess existing instances and migration/provisioning; do not disguise them as PostgreSQL or reset checkpoints to bypass checks. Configuration and operation Provision the instance and account first. The destination needs mapped-schema/table/index creation, business/checkpoint read/write and directory/instance/parameter read permissions. Apply least privilege in production rather than copying fixture SYSDBA. A successful connection check does not prove every DDL/DML privilege. Each MySQL database maps explicitly to a DM schema; PostgreSQL, messaging and other targets may run independently in the same pipeline. Source GTID/ROW/FULL requirements are in the V3 handbook. Use MYSQL PASSWORD / DM PASSWORD environment references or protected configuration. check returns dmStoragePlans . JSON and precision 38decimals require dm.acknowledgeTextConversions: true ; the wizard explains and requires this acknowledgement. Advanced configurations containing only native types may keep the default false. Acknowledgement does not change layout identity or permit pretending an existing layout is another type. Linux, Docker, Helm and native Kubernetes share the task document; manifests do not deploy DM itself. V2 and the DM Journal backend are not enabled. journal.product: DM is rejected. LOCAL Journal supports same-host recovery; cross-host workers use supported external PostgreSQL/openGauss/MySQL journals. Types and indexes Source model First DM mapping --- --- BOOLEAN / INT64 / UINT64 BIT / BIGINT / DECIMAL(20,0) DECIMAL precision≤38 Declared precision/scale DECIMAL precision 38 VARCHAR(precision+3), lossless decimal text at source scale; acknowledgement required JSON CLOB preserving JSON text/numeric precision; acknowledgement required, not native JSONB STRING Bounded VARCHAR(n CHAR), large text CLOB Bounded binary / large binary VARBINARY / BLOB DATE / DATETIME / TIMESTAMP DATE / TIMESTAMP(6) MySQL TIME INTERVAL DAY(2) TO SECOND(6), preserving sign/microseconds/over24hours Wide decimal text preserves values, not native numeric ordering/comparison/aggregation. Review SQL/types before takeover. JSON text is not equivalent to every vendor JSON type/version. Supported generated expressions follow source support and become ordinary columns. Keyless tables retain rivomesh row id and duplicate multiplicity. Business UNIQUE defaults to ordinary indexes under valid source constraints, complete ordered replication and exclusive synchronization writes. Primary/actual identity keys remain. Simple business GSI can become ordinary indexes, losing global routing/uniqueness. Prefix/expression/descending/fulltext/spatial indexes need plans. CLOB/BLOB indexes cannot be silently copied: DM LOB INDEX REQUIRES PLAN. Existing UNIQUE is never automatically dropped. Arbitrary nonempty adoption, procedures/triggers/foreign keys/partitioning and full DDL evolution still need migration workflows. Transactions, failures and FAQ Business changes and the destination checkpoint commit in one DML transaction, using metadata row locks and increasing epochs to fence old workers. DM DDL may auto-commit; preparation reacquires the fence and never inserts DDL into the business transaction. Targets acknowledge independently rather than using a global atomic commit. - Network/instance outage: recognized transient connection errors back off/reconnect; other sinks continue until journal backpressure. Database operations promote/route primaries. Full primary/replica cluster acceptance is separate. - SQL failure: only that subscription pauses. Repair permissions/constraints/types, then resume in the UI or with resume config/dm-v3.yml dm-business errorGeneration using the current status and the same JAR prefix. Original transactions retry; restart does not skip failures or bypass a pause. - Missing table/owner/checkpoint: refuses an empty replacement under old progress. Preserve evidence and plan a rebuild/reconciliation. - Precision overflow: do not force65digits into38. Review the lossless text plan and business SQL, acknowledge, then recheck. - Character capacity: VARCHAR may default to bytes. Existing layouts check ALL TAB COLUMNS CHAR USED/CHAR LENGTH/DATA LENGTH; byte-based VARCHAR must have worst-case four-byte UTF8 capacity. Binary width is checked and intervals need at least DAY(2)/SECOND(6). Character semantics, large values and page/row limits still need assessment; identical length numbers alone do not prove compatibility. - Case/empty-string/trailing-space differences: check actual initialization/compatibility parameters. Existing custom column rules require separate assessment. - Existing rows/extra constraints: never overwrites rows or silently removes constraints. Normal resume is not the full adoption tool. Reconciliation/repair/cutover workbench remains pending. - Trial expiry: supply a lawfully licensed vendor build. Initialization may report trial limits; no license files/checks are bypassed or modified. Run bash tests/dm-pipeline-run.sh with a locally supplied lawful image, or override RIVOMESH DM IMAGE for the same-layout build. The test creates an isolated project and removes only its own containers/volumes, without privileged mode/host parameter changes. Different images/versions require acceptance; fixture resource limits are not hardware capacity standards. Official references: JDBC, initialization, SQL definitions, storage/commit settings.

title: Apache Doris
text: Doris target, recovery and FAQ 中文：Doris V3. Example: doris-v3.yml. Current scope Native MySQL-protocol DDL/metadata and HTTP Stream Load are implemented. Independent native recovery and the actual MySQL+PostgreSQL mixed failure pipeline passed; see archived evidence. The first environment uses official apache/doris:all-in-one-4.1.3 ARM64, internally reporting doris-4.1.3-rc02-7126cf65d96 . This is not acceptance of every Doris release, cluster or production capacity. Doris is an analytical materializer, separate from transactional relational sinks. It is neither a generic transactional MySQL Sink nor an external Journal. Sources remain MySQL; explicit database mappings and fan-out apply. Layout and visibility Each source table owns a private Unique Key/Merge-on-Write physical table in metadataSchema . A source-named view in the mapped business database projects the original column order, hides internal fields and excludes retained tombstones. Internal names derive from pipeline/subscription/generation/table identity and fit the 64-character limit; full ownership hashes remain checked. The internal key represents source PK/identity or normalized keyless occurrence identity, not business UNIQUE(email). Identical keyless values retain distinct occurrences. Sequence/row ordinal fit a LARGEINT version; older writes cannot replace newer state. Deletions retain a current-version tombstone instead of relying on native soft-delete cleanup. Query business views; never mutate private tables or remove tombstones. A Stream Load has native visibility within its table batch, but source transactions can span multiple table/row batches: cross-table source transaction visibility is not atomic . Incomplete snapshots/backlogs are not cutover barriers. Only the sync service writes; this analytical layout is not an equivalent OLTP write takeover. Types and indexes Source normalized type Doris storage --- --- BOOLEAN / INT64 BOOLEAN / BIGINT UINT64 LARGEINT, still checked against the source unsigned-64 range DECIMAL DECIMAL(P,S), configured range 1–76; decimal256 session enabled; MySQL 65-digit values tested FLOAT32 / FLOAT64 FLOAT / DOUBLE; nonfinite input rejected STRING / JSON / DATE / TIME / DATETIME / TIMESTAMP Lossless STRING text, not native JSONB/temporal semantics BYTES / GEOMETRY Base64 STRING, recoverable to original bytes Within the source adapter’s supported expression set, generated columns copy evaluated source values; target expressions are not recreated. NULL differs from missing fields and full images are required. num as string=true prevents intermediate JSON double conversion; source JSON travels inside a string, preserving its internal numbers. Default secondaryIndexes: INVERTED converts plain BTREE/business UNIQUE/generic GSI metadata to nonunique per-column inverted indexes; composites can split. Business uniqueness, source ordering/collation, composite-prefix and global routing semantics are not preserved. Internal row identity is never downgraded. Expression/prefix/fulltext/spatial and unsupported types require a plan; NONE explicitly omits secondary indexes. dorisIndexPlans in check results records decisions/differences. Changing an initialized index/bucket/replica profile requires migration. Connections and permissions url is the FE MySQL-protocol entry, usually 9030. doris.loadUrl is an HTTP origin, optionally a direct BE, usually 8040. FE 307/308 redirects require exact configured redirectOrigins (scheme/host/port), identical paths, no URL credentials/query, and no HTTPS downgrade. Every entry must belong to the same cluster; receipt checks do not replace correct network configuration. Use separate username/password fields and environment references. Initial metadata identity checks use SHOW FRONTENDS/SHOW TABLETS, requiring a dedicated Doris ADMIN account; a least-privilege alternative is unfinished. Console roles are separate. Business readers should access views only. SQL/HTTP TLS still requires acceptance. Default three replicas requires enough BEs. One-BE tests must explicitly select replicas: 1 ; the service never silently lowers redundancy. Replicas range 1–5; buckets default 4, range 1–64. Compose resource limits describe fixtures, not throughput standards. The Web wizard exposes SQL/HTTP origins, redirect allowlist, replicas, buckets and index policy. Check before starting. Check reads source definitions and probes SQL features/HTTP health; it creates no tables and does not establish LOAD/DDL privileges. SQL enforces finite connect/socket timeouts and disables Connector/J cancellation timers to avoid their disconnect-cleanup null pointer. Arbitrary programming errors are not reclassified as networking. HTTP has independent connect/read/request/response bounds and never silently retries an ambiguous PUT internally. Confirmation and failures Loads require strict mode, zero filtering and exact input-row confirmation. Publish Timeout/running labels do not advance checkpoints. Each attempt uses a new load label: versioned rows/permanent destination receipts provide idempotency, not cancelled/expired labels. Success/finished labels still require native row key/version/tombstone/value verification; metadata content is also read back. After confirming data, the service persists a target batch receipt, then Journal transport progress, then the subscription checkpoint. Ambiguous responses/crashes can replay. Destinations acknowledge independently: relational targets can progress through a Doris outage until journal quota imposes backpressure. Restart checks native tablet identity, ownership, DDL, views and latest confirmed receipt. Initialized missing objects are not recreated empty at an old checkpoint.
