Restoring a coherent older nonempty FE+BE backup while keeping a newer journal is refused when the newest receipt is absent. Restore the right target or plan a rebuild. Coordinate data, metadata and journal backups; arbitrary per-table/incoherent rollback or external tampering requires reconciliation and is not comprehensively detected. Pause reports UNCONFIRMED IN FLIGHT MATERIALIZATION ; already submitted requests cannot be retracted. Relational targets may report FENCED. This is not a Doris business cutover barrier. Deterministic data/schema/permission faults pause that subscription; after repair resume its error generation without skipping the original transaction. FAQ Where are business UNIQUE/GSI constraints? They become nonunique acceleration. Source enforcement and exclusive synchronization preserve caught-up data; external writes are unsupported. Doris internal UNIQUE KEY protects row identity, not business uniqueness. Why views and private tables? They hide occurrence IDs, versions and tombstones while preserving public column order. Do not replace views with unrelated tables or treat private storage as identical source DDL. SQL connects but loading fails? HTTP health does not test LOAD privilege, and SQL/HTTP are separate entries. Verify same-cluster origins, accounts, privileges and explicit FE redirect destinations. Does one SQL fault stop all targets? Deterministic faults pause their target. Repair and use independent UI resume or resume config.yml subscriptionId expectedErrorGeneration ; do not edit GTIDs/checkpoints. Can it adopt existing nonempty objects? Current ownership checks create missing private objects/views and reject conflicting existing data/layout. Adoption, live DDL, layout migration and cutover workflows remain unfinished. Does retained space clean itself? Source journals reclaim by independent ACK. Target receipts/tombstones/indexes are outside logical journal quota and need storage monitoring. Receipt compaction/retention, soak and hardware capacity reports remain unfinished. Primary references and limits Design references: Stream Load, Unique Key concurrency, JSON precision, tablet identity/privileges, official fixture image. Product documentation is not project acceptance; see validation. Complete clusters/compute-storage separation, combined FE/BE faults, TLS, all JDKs, huge catalogs/transactions, adoption/repair/migration and capacity matrices remain pending. SQL modes and text validation Catalog, receipt and row-verification values use binary server-prepared MySQL parameters. The adapter forces useServerPrepStmts=true and emulateUnsupportedPstmts=false ; an unsupported protocol fails instead of silently reverting to literal interpolation. DDL comments contain safe internal identifiers only. Actual Doris4.1.3/Java8 EMPTY and NO BACKSLASH ESCAPES profiles passed quoted/backslash names, Unicode/emoji text, snapshot, CDC and session reconstruction. Malformed UTF-16 fails deterministically with DORIS TEXT ENCODING INVALID , rather than retrying invalid text indefinitely; see additional evidence. Sources: Doris prepared statements, string literals. After the binding change, current release9a087 also passed an actual MySQL8.4.13→PostgreSQL17.12+Doris4.1.3 pipeline with outage catch-up, worker kill, SQL repair/retry and missing-view isolation. The native mode/old-backup case used11667063; all14Doris adapter classes match9a byte-for-byte. See additional evidence for artifact and scope distinctions.

title: Controller and Agent lifecycle
text: Separate management entries and execution Agents 中文 · Global control · SDD contract The protocol4 separated profile passes348app/actual-JAR tests,76DOM and5x152controls,PG/MySQL stores,actual multi-database/two-target CDC,all-controller loss,store outage,pending accepting-entry recovery,nonroot processes and SQL role races.Automatic Agent takeover and complete journal/adapter/JDK matrices remain open. Evidence. Configuration role Registry role Responsibility --- --- --- COMBINED CONTROLLER WORKER Compatible management/local execution in one process CONTROLLER CONTROLLER UI/API,shared login,configuration and durable admission;execution capacity0 AGENT AGENT Fixed-owner execution,Worker supervision,observations and typed reads;HTTP probes only Activation Every member sets cluster.sharedAccess=true,sharedTasks=true,separateExecution=true and an explicit role. Control database,cluster.id,namespace and Base64 task key match; node IDs and private directories/volumes are independent. separateExecution=false keeps protocol3 combined behavior; defaults do not silently become separated deployments. Separation uses protocol4. Stop all old members normally and confirm STOPPED before upgrade; expiry/unreachability is insufficient. Preserve tasks,journals,reports,keys and directory UUIDs. Old programs refuse the new protocol; direct database downgrade is unsupported. An existing combined owner with tasks retains its original nodeId/directory when reopening as AGENT. A controller refuses an execution directory with tasks,including shared ownership hidden behind an empty replacement directory. Legacy local-to-global import remains a separate migration. Controllers cannot receive execution tasks. Create requests specify an Agent; the UI filters controllers and pages to find Agents. Committing transactions recheck role/ownership instead of trusting an earlier directory/role read. Linux The controller example uses8080;the Agent example uses8081. Adjust control connections and supply token,control credentials and task key environment values,then run independently: Use separate configuration copies/directories and distinct ports on one host. Supervise with separate systemd services; management service dependencies must not stop the Agent. Agent termination stops its own supervised Workers. Docker Build the current image first. Supply RIVOMESH TOKEN,RIVOMESH TASK KEY,RIVOMESH CONTROL URL,RIVOMESH CONTROL USERNAME,RIVOMESH CONTROL PASSWORD. The example assumes PostgreSQL control storage: It creates controller-a,controller-b,agent-a with three private volumes. Management ports bind loopback8080/8082;Agent probes bind8081. Browser access still needs HTTPS/proxy configuration for production cookies. Stopping management must not delete/stop Agent state. The file does not create the external control database. Helm and native Kubernetes Use the shared Secrets documented under global control,then install independent releases: Without Helm,adapt/apply native manifests A,B,Agent. Each release has one replica/private PVC. Add Agents with distinct releases/node IDs/volumes. Static rendering/invalid-setting checks exist;live Kubernetes/CSI/node-fault acceptance is separate. Recovery FAQ What if every management entry stops? The Agent independently reads the shared queue. The tested LOCAL/H2 profile continues CDC;management rejoin reads the same owner and authority. This does not relocate execution to another Agent. Does CDC survive control-store failure? In the tested LOCAL/H2 profile,the same Worker continues source capture and independent business writes. Management APIs/registration readiness refuse control without local-account fallback. Recovered storage permits renewed registration and observations. External-journal shared failures,other adapters and production topologies require their own profiles. Why does the Agent have no login page? Its HTTP endpoint serves GET /healthz and /readyz only;administration paths return404 AGENT PROBE ONLY. Use management entries;typed owner queries travel through shared storage. What if the Agent exits or is killed? Its Workers are affected;management shows pending/unknown. Restore original Agent directory,nodeId and keys;queued offline STOP is processed before restoring old RUNNING intent. Expiry does not prove process termination. Automatic takeover/stale-Worker fencing remain CP-04. Are Agent secrets least-privilege isolation? No. Agents remain in the trusted control domain;Workers filter controller environment variables. Roles do not establish tenant/OS isolation. Least-secret/external-identity work remains separately tracked. NODE ID IN USE after restart? SIGKILL leaves an old lease until expiry;never bypass the guard.Supervisors may retry normally;if another member keeps renewing,fix duplicate configuration. VALIDATION BARRIER MOVED immediately after configuration restart? Process liveness and already-equal rows do not establish a new journal claim.Check shared state and actual incremental catchup before retrying.The guard must not accept a moved cut;clearer startup readiness remains CP-06.

title: GaussDB index policy
text: Gauss index conversion, correctness, and application takeover Updated: 2026-11-14. 中文：Gauss 索引策略. See requirements and decisions for scope and open questions. Status: v3 implements ordinary secondary indexes and business UNIQUE downgrade; v2 still creates columns/PK only. IndexPolicy produces explicit actions and JdbcSink executes supported indexes on new tables. Expressions/prefixes/descending/special methods and existing UNIQUE/GSI require separate plans, never blind DROP. Business GSI model entries may become ordinary indexes; identity GSIs are not downgraded. Commercial distributed GaussDB still needs hardware acceptance. See the V3 manual. Accepted synchronization policy MySQL is authoritative. Only the synchronization service writes to targets during synchronization; applications may read them. Validate data and restore required constraints before application writes take over. For newly created Gauss business tables: Source object / target requirement Synchronization policy --- --- MySQL PRIMARY KEY Preserve stable row identity and uniqueness; never downgrade to an ordinary index Business secondary UNIQUE(email) or composite UNIQUE Create a nonunique ordinary index with corresponding columns/order; preserve compatible column definitions and NOT NULL Ordinary secondary index Create an ordinary index supported by the target GSI contemplated for secondary uniqueness or query acceleration Use an ordinary secondary index, without global routing/uniqueness guarantees Unique structure required for PK, row identity, or internal correctness Excluded from relaxation; choose compatible distribution/constraints or fail preflight Metadata transaction deduplication, owner/lease, and checkpoint uniqueness Preserve; business-index relaxation does not apply Existing target UNIQUE, GSI, FK dependencies, etc. Inspect dependencies and produce a difference/migration plan; do not automatically DROP or weaken An ordinary index cannot replace a PK. Replacing a global UNIQUE with UNIQUE(email, distribution key) is not equivalent: it allows duplicate email across distribution keys and still enforces a constraint that may be unnecessary during synchronization. This topic covers openGauss/distributed GaussDB. Other adapters may also relax incompatible business secondary UNIQUE constraints under declared policies. Preserve PK/candidate identity and internal correctness; analytical Unique Key/materialization identity is not an optional secondary constraint. See platform design. What UNIQUE(email) means Example source definition: Logical target example, not current generated output or a universal version-independent script: Omitting target UNIQUE does not itself create duplicates. Final correctness depends on complete replication. At the same fully applied source transaction boundary, each source PK should correspond to the same target row if: 1. Every source transaction is logged and captured completely, with FULL row images, correct ordering, and correct routing. 2. PK mapping is one-to-one; target PK comparisons do not merge distinct source keys. 3. Snapshot/CDC handoff has no gaps, and durable GTID/checkpoints plus idempotent application handle redelivery. 4. Business changes and apply checkpoints commit atomically; retries never skip failed transactions; stale owners are fenced. 5. No external writes, trigger side effects, lossy conversions, or accidental merging of source tables occur. Under these conditions, the source enforces email uniqueness and the target reproduces its rows. The target ordinary index no longer enforces email uniqueness. Retry idempotency relies on PKs and transaction checkpoints, not the email index. Removing UNIQUE is not a recovery mechanism. Preserve multiple NULLs allowed by the source; GROUP BY email HAVING COUNT( ) 1 alone is not a valid constraint check. Case, collation, trailing spaces, empty-string/NULL behavior, and type conversion can change equality semantics. Source uniqueness does not guarantee that a future target UNIQUE constraint will build successfully. Temporary duplicates during snapshot The current snapshot uses online chunks followed by log replay, not one database-wide point-in-time snapshot. For example, the scanner reads id=1,email=a ; a source transaction changes it to b and inserts id=2,email=a ; the scanner then reads id=2. Before catch-up, the target may contain two distinct PKs with email=a even though every committed source state was valid. Temporary secondary-key duplicates are not duplicate PK rows and must not cause data to be discarded. Complete ordered replay must restore the source state at the declared boundary. Snapshot/early catch-up output is not promised to be consistent; consumers requiring consistency wait for an agreed barrier and read protocol. Ordinary secondary indexes permit these intermediate states, which fits the current scan method. Preserving selected target UNIQUE constraints in a future design would require revisiting snapshot/replay semantics and constraint timing, not merely adding UNIQUE to generated DDL. Can GSI become an ordinary index? Yes, an ordinary index can be selected during new-table index planning to retain a basic access path on corresponding columns. This is a replacement with changed capabilities, not a lossless native conversion. MySQL has no Gauss GSI; keyword substitution in source DDL cannot implement it. Huawei documents GSI distribution independent of the base table. Its example contrasts an ordinary index visiting all DNs with GSI routing a qualifying lookup to one DN. This design therefore accepts possible extra cross-node query work and promises no equivalent performance. Verify exact version capabilities. CREATE GLOBAL INDEX, official query-plan example. Design consequences: - Ordinary indexes provide neither cross-DN global uniqueness nor GSI's separate distribution/covering design; changing an index does not redistribute its base table. - Retaining indexed columns does not preserve query plans, covering behavior, or JOIN performance. Validate representative queries with EXPLAIN . - A global structure required to enforce PK identity cannot be relaxed. Prefer distribution compatible with the PK; fail preflight when correctness cannot be preserved. - Existing GSI may support constraints or other dependencies. Migration must inspect ownership, dependencies, validity, and rollback paths before removal. Partition GLOBAL/LOCAL indexes describe partition coverage and must not be confused with distributed GSI. openGauss partition-index syntax is not evidence of GaussDB GSI capability. openGauss index documentation. Distributed business and metadata tables Relaxing business secondary constraints does not remove restrictions involving PKs, distribution/partition columns, or types. Distribution planning must be deterministic, explainable, and overridable, with an explicit write strategy for PK/distribution-key changes. Metadata requires its own design: deduplication keys, task IDs, stream ordering, and lease operations must satisfy distributed constraints, while business changes and local target checkpoints remain atomic. Do not delete UNIQUE(job id, transaction key) to avoid GSI, or infer source ordering from independent CN-generated IDs. The current metadata layout has not been validated on commercial distributed GaussDB and is not a deployment template for it. Planning and resumable execution Implementation requires these steps, not merely removing a UNIQUE keyword: 1. Discover source index metadata: PK/secondary classification, column order, prefix lengths, expressions, sort direction, visibility, and method. Persist a versioned conversion manifest. 2. Generate executable DDL and capability differences for the target product/version/mode, distribution/partitioning, and types. Deduplicate equivalent target indexes; use stable digests when shortening names. 3. Create columns and PKs before snapshot; persist definitions, policy, and fingerprints. Correct row identity comes first. 4. Prefer ordinary business secondary-index creation after initial catch-up, with bounded concurrency. CDC progress and index readiness are separate: streaming does not imply every index is READY. 5. Persist planned/started/succeeded/failed states and definition digests per target/table/index. After restart, inspect catalog definitions and validity before proceeding. Adapter-specific recovery must cover nontransactional DDL and invalid indexes left by online builds. 6. A matching name with a different definition is not success. Retain diagnostics and retry the object without resetting snapshot cursors or skipping business transactions. Pause a target if DDL failure compromises safe writes; a missing acceleration-only index may instead leave CDC running with a failed index phase. Report prefix, expression, FULLTEXT, SPATIAL, invisible, oversized, and unsupported-collation indexes individually. Initially automate only ordinary column-based B-tree-like indexes; explicitly list other objects as unsupported/manual work rather than claiming complete index synchronization. Do not silently expand a prefix index to the full column, which may exceed limits or change plans. Application takeover This is a planned operating procedure, not an existing automated command. Validate each target independently; simultaneous takeover of every target is unnecessary: 1. Freeze relevant source business writes and DDL; record a final source GTID barrier and eliminate dual-write entry points. 2. Wait for the target to apply through that barrier with no failed transactions, missing logs, or unfinished snapshot. Use proven target application progress, not shared capture GTID alone. 3. At the same frozen boundary, compare row counts, PK sets, chunk digests/required row values, and semantics for restored constraints. Retain original UNIQUE definitions in the conversion manifest. 4. Validate duplicates, NULLs, lengths, and dependencies using actual target equality rules; build required UNIQUE/FK constraints. If distributed constraints need GSI or redistribution, plan and validate that separately. Ordinary indexes during synchronization do not justify omitting constraints permanently after takeover. 5. Once all required constraints are valid and checks pass, stop or fence synchronization writes to that target, then permit application writes. Failure blocks takeover; repair and retry without deleting conflicting rows to force success. After application writes begin, the original one-way sync service cannot safely overwrite that target without coordination. Failback or bidirectional replication requires a separate design; GTID retention does not provide it. Other mirror targets may retain their own subscriptions, but after business moves to the new database the original MySQL source does not automatically receive those new writes. FAQ Will retries insert extra rows without UNIQUE? The keyed design uses PKs and transaction checkpoints; an ordinary email index does not deduplicate. No-PK support is now a first-release requirement but remains unimplemented. It needs candidate identity or consistent-baseline/multiset handling, not the keyed guarantee; see platform design. Are repeated email values always errors? No. Distinguish NULLs, comparison differences, and pre-catch-up mixed scan states. Judge against source definitions at a declared boundary; do not automatically delete rows. Are ordinary indexes always faster than GSI? No. They may reduce write maintenance but increase the DNs visited by queries. Measure actual workloads. Will existing target UNIQUE indexes change automatically? No. Current code does not do this; the design first produces an object/dependency migration plan. Constraint-owned indexes are not standalone objects to DROP blindly. Does an interrupted index build restart the snapshot? The design retains data checkpoints and resumes index work after catalog inspection. Implementation and fault validation remain pending. Is constraint restoration guaranteed to succeed? No. Actual validation and constraint creation gate takeover. Incompatible distribution/constraints or inconsistent data must block it. Acceptance checklist - Single/composite UNIQUE becomes nonunique with traceable ordering, nullability, and conversion manifests; PK/internal uniqueness remains intact. - Temporary email duplicates during online scans converge to the frozen source boundary; updates, deletes, PK changes, and transaction redelivery preserve rows. - Validate independently lagging targets; index failure on one target must not corrupt another target's state. - Test process death around index DDL, connection loss, uncertain responses, definition conflicts, invalid indexes, and stale owners. - Use real multi-CN/DN GaussDB to validate distribution compatibility, global row identity, transaction ordering, and ordinary-index plans; validate openGauss separately. - Before takeover, validate collations, empty strings/NULLs, target uniqueness, and the frozen barrier. Deliberate conflicts must block switching without discarding data. The current validation record excludes these new capabilities. It must not be used to claim index conversion or commercial distributed GaussDB acceptance. Doris business UNIQUE/GSI conversion uses nonunique inverted indexes; its internal UNIQUE KEY protects source row identity only. This is not GaussDB B-tree equivalence and does not preserve business uniqueness, collation or global routing. See the Doris handbook.

title: GBase 8c
text: GBase 8c destination GBASE 8C is an experimental adapter using the vendor's com.gbase8c.Driver and jdbc:gbase8c:// . 8a, 8c and 8s are separate product families ; PostgreSQL wire compatibility does not establish support for all three. 8a/8s remain separate planned adapters. The first profile targets V6 S1.3.0B19 ARM64, PG/UTF8; the first actual MySQL+PostgreSQL mixed snapshot/CDC/TIME/keyless/text-key/outage/catch-up/worker-kill/SQL-repair/missing-table acceptance passed. This applies to that profile and is not a full production matrix claim. See config/gbase8c-v3.yml. CLI and the Web v3 wizard share this adapter. Pre-create a PG-compatible UTF8 database and a synchronization account allowed to create schemas/tables/indexes and execute DML. The service does not change global compatibility settings or promote database nodes. Use a separate login. Native tests confirmed that initialization owner omm cannot connect remotely, and CREATEDB alone does not authorize schema creation inside postgres . An administrator can grant the required database scope: Existing schemas/tables need their own permissions or ownership. Synchronization does not require SYSADMIN. The fixture's CREATEDB attribute exists to create a negative compatibility-mode test database; pre-created production databases do not require copying that attribute. See the vendor permission guide. Session and data contract Every physical connection checks the metadata product and actual kernel version before vendor-specific SQL. It requires PG mode, UTF8, preserved empty strings and case/trailing-space-sensitive text comparisons. It sets session UTC, synchronous local commit and standard string escaping. Read-only endpoints raise a retryable connection error. Other compatibility modes require separate semantic and type plans. Quoted identifiers, row tables and primary keys are used. Keyless rows have internal occurrence IDs. JSON maps to JSONB; UINT64 to DECIMAL(20,0), wide decimals retain precision, binary maps to BYTEA, timestamps retain microseconds, and MySQL TIME becomes a signed INTERVAL. Generated values are taken from the source; complete target-side expression reconstruction is not promised. A native probe confirmed VARCHAR(100) holds 100 four-byte Unicode characters. Business changes and the target checkpoint share a local transaction and epoch fence. One unavailable target does not prevent independent targets acknowledging data. This does not imply cross-target distributed atomicity or protection against arbitrary physical backup rollback, split brain or external business writers. Index and distributed scope DOWNGRADE BUSINESS turns non-identity business UNIQUE into ordinary indexes. Simple business GSI conversion loses global uniqueness and routing. Primary, identity and internal uniqueness cannot be downgraded. Existing UNIQUE is not automatically dropped; expression/prefix/full-text/spatial indexes need a reviewed plan. Only the synchronization service may write destination business tables; validate and restore constraints before takeover. Distributed tables add distribution-key and unique-constraint restrictions: see the vendor SQL reference. A single-instance PG acceptance cannot establish CN/DN, DSS shared-storage, HA failover, cross-shard transaction or redistribution compatibility. Distribution-key changes, metadata/ownership placement, preserved UNIQUE and global indexes require independent planning and native verification. Recovery and FAQ - On downtime/network failure, retain journal/checkpoints and wait for the same writable destination. Size retained logs and source binlog retention for the outage. - SQL errors pause the affected subscription. Inspect/fix the cause and resume the original transaction. Manual skip/compensating data editing is not implemented. - Missing business tables isolate the affected target. Do not edit checkpoints; rebuilding or resnapshotting requires a separate plan. - Arbitrary nonempty adoption is rejected. Empty existing tables still need column/key/trigger/FK/index/ownership validation. - Unsupported live source DDL pauses safely; complete online schema evolution is pending. - The vendor filename is gbase8c-jdbc-3.0.0B02.jar , its embedded Maven version is 3.0.0 , and runtime DriverVersion contains an unresolved placeholder. Exact input identity uses fixed filenames and SHA-256, not that version string. Reproducible inputs Vendor downloads. Driver ZIP SHA-256: 3c2645993cd2e20a19941fc4d4bb5aba0f02ca378766543b6dd259a50c382721 ; JAR SHA-256: fe115f05124f6b9f37e49c829a0def28f7d09a6d871dd62a0c9f856b0aaa7e91 . The build verifies both, preserves vendor classes and a dedicated license resource, and checks Java 8-compatible bytecode. Native fixtures use separately obtained lawful vendor binaries. No database binaries/licenses are distributed in the repository. The local base image in tests/gbase8c/Dockerfile supplies Linux userland; the actual executable is verified vendor gbased , not openGauss pretending to be GBase. 中文 Native fixture reproduction / 原生夹具复现 Use Python 3.12+ and a lawful matching ARM64 vendor installer: Installer SHA-256: 6946abaa7666cbfadea3957682020262a102e52c6f7b4632d1f93fee9d3400b7 ; extracted B19 kernel SHA-256: 69663acfbb786c3f05cc434fb9f6d42806609b69c818c6e6ce0c4234748ad582 , matching its vendor checksum. The unified installer also contains a B10 kernel; this fixture explicitly selects B19.

title: Global task control
text: Global task control: activation, recovery and limits 中文 · SDD design 2026-11-17: an optional fixed-owner global profile now wires public HTTP, UI, shared configuration, durable commands and remote reads. Local control remains the default. CP-02/03 remain PARTIAL: legacy task import, complete business workflows, capacity and fault matrices are not fully accepted. Automatic owner relocation is separate. Activation Members share the control database, cluster.id, namespace, sharedAccess=true, sharedTasks=true and taskKey. Each has a distinct stable nodeId and private persistent task/data directories. taskKey is canonical Base64 text encoding 32 random bytes, supplied through protected environment configuration. Keep it out of task YAML. Never share controller.json. First activation requires empty task directories; existing registered tasks or YAML fail with GLOBAL TASK IMPORT REQUIRED. There is no automatic legacy import tool yet. The platform example supports Linux. Back up the control database, private directories and keys first. Old members must stop normally and register STOPPED before the shared protocol upgrade; expiry or loss of contact does not establish that they stopped. After upgrade, old local/registry-only members refuse admission. Disabling sharedTasks, changing nodeId, losing directory identity or using the wrong key does not fall back to local authority. Supply database credentials, token, key and node ID through the deployment environment. The example enables Secure cookies: expose HTTPS and configure the correct publicOrigin at the proxy. Helm and native Kubernetes The global Helm values reference existing Secrets: token in rivomesh-auth, and username/password/task-key in rivomesh-control-store. task-key contains the same Base64 key text on all members. Use separate releases, private PVCs and stable node IDs: Alternatively adapt and apply the native manifests A and B with kubectl apply -f. Independent controllers must not share a private directory. Static Helm/native parity and invalid-configuration checks exist; live Kubernetes/CSI, node-fault and rolling-upgrade acceptance remain open. Docker uses the same independent persistent-directory and key requirements. Acceptance fixtures leave no persistent preview. UI and configuration The session field taskControlScope=GLOBAL identifies this profile. Any entry lists authorized tasks with cursor pagination, owner/node state, global revision, Worker state, desired/active configuration and command results. Creation/import forms select the execution node; form import creates a new task and does not migrate old checkpoints. Unavailable owner execution is UNKNOWN, not stopped. Create/edit/restore/actions return 202 for durable admission only. Configuration history separates desired/active; the active pointer advances after successful owner application. Failed proposals preserve the old active configuration. Masked secret references work across entries. Connection previews, raw differences and repair-plan reads use expiring owner queries and cannot complete while the owner is offline. Complete filtering, log aggregation and real-browser visual/accessibility acceptance remain open. Global maximumTasks/maximumCommands differ from per-node maxTasks/maxRunningTasks. Defaults are 10000 global tasks and 1000 active commands; configuration ranges are resource guards, not hardware throughput promises. Queries are limited to 512KiB requests, 1MiB responses, 1–60 second lifetime, bounded readers and retained capacity. Admission and recovery PENDING is durable queueing. DISPATCHED saves the exact original local request/revision before invocation. ACCEPTED is local durable admission. SUCCEEDED/FAILED come from actual operation receipts. UNKNOWN requires reconciliation, not a success claim or reissue under a new revision. Startup restores receipt protection and validates local configuration against shared authority before scheduling. The latest startup fix scans all outstanding command pages, including undispatched STOP/PAUSE. Corresponding Workers cannot restore old RUNNING intent before local durable admission; older local operations may finish and stop commands receive priority retries. Rejection after authorization changes releases the block; uncertainty retains it. Focused tests and the application build pass; native business acceptance remains candidate-specific and does not retroactively change earlier evidence. TASK BUSY/OPERATION PENDING retain the original request. Outstanding receipts bypass ordinary 500-entry pruning. Cancellation has a parent and reserved capacity: cancel undispatched work atomically, reconcile uncertain delivery first, and perform actual cancellation after local admission. Success does not imply all targets rolled back. Offline STOP waits for the original owner. Restore its private directory/volume and keys; an empty directory cannot impersonate it. Default combined controllers stop their local Workers on exit. The explicit separated profile is covered by execution lifecycle; relocation, drain, scheduling and cross-Agent fencing remain separate work. Source MySQL primary promotion is a separate fault scenario from controller-owner takeover. Operations FAQ How do I distinguish accepted from executed? Inspect deliveryStatus, status, code and actual Worker/target checkpoints for the same request ID. HTTP 202 is not business commit evidence. Does refresh or another entry preserve login? Shared sessions restore identity subject to cookie domain, Secure, SameSite, expiry and revocation. Different domains require correct proxy/session configuration. Can A stop an offline owner? A durably queues STOP. It stays pending/unknown until the original owner supplies an actual receipt. Heartbeat expiry does not prove process termination. Can I edit owner fields, delete root tables or use an empty directory? No. Authenticated metadata, counts, private-directory identity, receipts and configuration projections reject missing/substituted authority. Does control-store failure fall back to local accounts? No. Management refuses control without shared authority. Existing data-process behavior follows its journal/lease/target protocol; management availability does not establish complete data-plane fencing. What belongs in backups? Coordinate the control database, every private directory, logs/reports/local journal, external journal if selected, and original keys. Restoring just a cursor or old control snapshot is insufficient; automated coordination and old-backup fault matrices remain open. What is already evidenced? Earlier candidates cover real PostgreSQL/MySQL control stores, two independent JVMs, HTTPS/shared login, A creating B-owned tasks and offline commands. Configuration fixtures also invoke real TaskService with fixture Workers. The startup fix and real cross-node business CDC are under additional acceptance. These do not establish all cluster, adapter or hardware profiles. Why is no persistent preview running? The user requested temporary fixtures only. They remove their own containers/volumes and leave unrelated resources untouched. Multi-target maintenance receipts and upgrade recovery Intermediate candidate463994bca812 exposed inconsistent Set normalization during real two-target validation: comparison completed and remained PAUSED, while receipt inspection recorded UNKNOWN/OWNER RECEIPT MISMATCH. The fix applies the same input validation/sorting as local admission and retains the original request,revision,actor and report identity. Candidateb2b9a078 passes339actual-JAR-first tests,5x143maintenance controls,actual two-target validation/repair and original-report recovery from old UNKNOWN; see evidence. Never edit shared phases or issue another validation to hide uncertainty. The explicit controller/Agent profile now has scoped acceptance; see execution lifecycle. Default combined deployment remains coupled, and additional profiles need independent verification. 2026-11-17: explicit protocol4 controller/Agent separation is accepted for the declared profile;default combined mode remains coupled. title: Apache Hive
text: Hive destination, recovery and FAQ 中文：Hive V3. Example: hive-v3.yml. Status The first independent native and actual mixed recovery profiles passed; the catalog retains an experimental label. CLI/Web V3 configuration, isolated JDBC, native HiveServer2 checks, ACID ORC history and latest-version views are implemented. Hive4.0.1/Java8 independent acceptance covered PK moves, keyless multiplicity, precision, lost-confirmation replay, case-folding, restart and older nonempty backup refusal. Actual MySQL8.4.13→PostgreSQL17.12+Hive passed snapshot/CDC, independent Hive outage and catch-up, worker SIGKILL resume, SQL constraint repair/retry, missing-view isolation and truthful pause fences. The final artifact/worktree-assets gate passed too; see evidence. This does not accept every Hive version, cluster or production capacity profile. The first fixture is official apache/hive:4.0.1 ARM64, one HiveServer2, persistent embedded Derby and local warehouse. It is not a production/HA deployment. HDFS/S3, external Metastore, Tez, Kerberos, TLS, clusters and other JDKs remain unverified. Layout and consistency Hive is a versioned analytical destination, not the transactional JDBC sink or a Journal. Each source table has a managed ACID ORC history table in metadataSchema . A view with the source table name in the mapped database selects the latest internal identity/version, filters tombstones and exposes source columns only. A primary-key move writes an old-identity tombstone plus a new row. Identical keyless rows retain separate normalized identities. Retries may leave duplicate physical versions; the business view should expose one current row per identity. History row count is not source row count. Only Rivomesh writes this layout; do not edit history, ownership properties or tombstones. One source transaction can span multiple Hive statements/tables: cross-table source transaction visibility is not atomic . JDBC commit is not an atomic business-data/checkpoint boundary here. An unfinished snapshot or backlog is not a cutover barrier, and this layout cannot directly take over OLTP writes. Types Normalized source type Hive storage --- --- BOOLEAN / INT64 BOOLEAN / BIGINT UINT64 DECIMAL(20,0), bounded to unsigned 64-bit DECIMAL precision ≤38 DECIMAL(P,S), refusing overflow or rounding DECIMAL precision 38 STRING preserving digits and declared scale FLOAT32 / FLOAT64 FLOAT / DOUBLE; non-finite values refused STRING / JSON / DATE / TIME / DATETIME / TIMESTAMP STRING; not native JSON/temporal semantics BYTES / GEOMETRY base64 STRING preserving decoded bytes Generated columns retain evaluated values for expressions already supported by the source adapter; expressions are not recreated in Hive. Reassess comparison, ordering and query functions for the destination types, especially wide decimal strings. Full row images and explicit missing-vs-null checks remain required. First-profile names use ASCII letters/digits/underscore, cannot start with a digit, and are at most128 characters; mapped databases also follow common configuration length limits. Unsupported source names are not silently rewritten. rivomesh columns are reserved. UNIQUE, GSI and ordinary indexes Hive removed its old indexing feature from3.0; there is no equivalent ordinary B-tree conversion here. Official index documentation. Business secondary indexes are explicitly omitted. Review the differences and set acknowledgeIndexOmission: true ; initialization refuses secondary indexes without that acknowledgement. Source business UNIQUE is not enforced in Hive. GSI global routing, uniqueness, covering layout and performance are not retained. ACID/ORC/bucketing are not substitutes. Internal identity/version correctness is preserved. Convergence assumes an authoritative source, exclusive destination writes, complete catch-up and identity-preserving conversions; see index policy. Connection and deployment Require hive.txn.manager=org.apache.hadoop.hive.ql.lockmgr.DbTxnManager , hive.support.concurrency=true , hive.query.results.cache.enabled=false , and managed full-ACID ORC tables/views. Operate Metastore, warehouse, transaction cleanup and compaction; session flags alone are insufficient. Hive transactions. Only direct binary jdbc:hive2://host:port/database is accepted, with optional auth=noSasl none and ssl=true false . Discovery, HTTP, Kerberos, URL credentials, initialization scripts and arbitrary session options are refused. Credentials use separate fields/environment references. noSasl is a matching-server option, not the production security default. TLS is configurable but not accepted by native testing yet. queryTimeoutSeconds is1–1800 (default300). Binary socket timeout is bounded to5–120 seconds and internal connect retries are0. A timeout does not prove the statement was absent. Default SQL/response limits are4MiB/16MiB, at most10,000 returned rows; overflow fails rather than confirming truncated results. Events also obey maxMessageBytes . Use a dedicated writer with private metadata-table DDL/read/write and property/description/definition access, plus mapped view DDL/read. Minimum grants depend on the authorization plugin and remain to be verified. Readers should access business views only. check is read-only and cannot prove write permissions. Its hiveIndexPlans entries expose per-table index actions, required acknowledgement and columnStorage types; omission is never reported as an ordinary-index conversion. A pinned standalone Hive SDK runs in a private classloader without replacing core logging/Jackson/Guava. First use extracts and verifies about42MiB under a private java.io.tmpdir cache. Read-only Docker/K8s filesystems need a restricted writable temporary volume; do not share an untrusted cache. Confirmation and recovery Implementation writes versions, reads back actual identity/version/tombstone/values, writes and reads a target receipt, saves Journal transport progress, then advances the destination transaction checkpoint. Physical row count alone cannot confirm an uncertain write. Reconnect checks ownership, layout, view definition, resource properties and the latest receipt. Established missing objects are not recreated at old progress. Resource UUID is a Rivomesh Metastore property, not independently authenticated storage identity. Coordinate Metastore, warehouse and Journal backups. Arbitrary partial-table/file rollback, forged metadata or partial history loss are not claimed to be fully detected. The first independent native case passed server restart and refusal of an older nonempty Metastore+warehouse backup while Journal retains newer progress; see the exact release and scope in evidence. Connection failures retry by classification; deterministic structure/permission/data errors pause this destination. Resume retries original data, without changing GTIDs or silently skipping. Pause cannot establish that every in-flight Hive request has been cancelled. Journal ACK-based reclamation does not reclaim Hive history. Monitor history, tombstones, receipts and ACID delta files separately. Receipt compression, safe history GC, compaction soak and hardware sizing remain unfinished. FAQ Why append versions instead of ordinary UPDATE/DELETE? History, versions and tombstones support snapshot replay, uncertain requests, PK moves and keyless identity under one layout. Read the view rather than the physical table. Can Hive take over the application? This analytical layout has neither source cross-table atomicity nor enforced business UNIQUE. Takeover needs a separately designed data model, reconciliation, barrier and constraints. Does Hive block other destinations? Delivery threads are independent; other destinations can progress while Hive is unavailable. Unconfirmed data retains shared Journal space and eventually causes capture backpressure at quota. The first mixed profile passed; Journal exhaustion and the wider fault matrix remain unverified. Can an existing nonempty table be adopted? Arbitrary adoption/overwrite is not implemented. Ownership or shape mismatch is refused. Live DDL, nonempty adoption and repair require later workflows. How is the native case reproduced? After building, run bash tests/hive-materializer-run.sh . It operates only its own named volumes and stops the server before coordinated Metastore/warehouse backup/restore. Failed raw logs stay in target/ ; inspect actual scenario coverage rather than relying on a marker alone. The fixture uses HIVESERVER2 PID DIR on a dedicated ephemeral runtime mount to avoid a stale PID matching a new process after container restart. Metastore and warehouse remain persistent volumes. This fixture correction is not a production Hive HA implementation. Query cache and consistent reads The mixed fixture returned three detail rows but a cached COUNT0. A fresh session with only query-results cache disabled returned COUNT3 while stats optimization remained enabled. This observation does not establish the same problem for every Hive release/deployment. The first supported profile requires the server default and all reader sessions to use hive.query.results.cache.enabled=false ; the writer session must also disable it. Read-only preflight and write-time checks refuse enabled cache with HIVE QUERY CACHE DISABLED REQUIRED , without silently changing global settings. Disabling cache only on the writer cannot protect other readers. Do not re-enable it in application connections or manually add rows based on stale cached counts. Correct server/reader settings before check/resume; this does not require resetting data, task identity or checkpoints. The original cache-enabled mixed run was explicitly aborted and is not accepted complete recovery. The cache-disabled profile passed independent materialization/restart/older-backup refusal; the frozen-release complete mixed run passed too; see evidence.

title: 金仓 Kingbase
text: Kingbase destination and FAQ 中文：金仓 V3. Example: kingbase-v3.yml. Scope and connection V3 configuration, CLI, explicit mappings, independent fan-out workers and the bilingual wizard accept product: KINGBASE . The first profile targets PG compatibility mode and remains EXPERIMENTAL . The first Java8/Kingbase V009R001C001B0025 PG/UTF8 native transaction and MySQL8.4.13+PostgreSQL17.12 mixed recovery profile passed; see evidence. Existing PostgreSQL results do not prove Kingbase compatibility. Other modes, RAC/distributed products, all versions and capacity remain pending. The pinned Java8 driver is cn.com.kingbase:kingbase8:9.0.1 , with com.kingbase8.Driver and jdbc:kingbase8:// , normally port54321. The vendor namespace coexists with PostgreSQL. Maven Central's vendor POM declares Apache-2.0; a complete distribution license/NOTICE review is still required. Every physical sink connection checks the actual product, version() , SHOW database mode , UTF8 encoding, empty-string preservation, case/trailing-space comparisons and writability before metadata access. It sets UTC, standard strings and synchronous commit=on . Only pg passes. The service never changes compatibility mode, global settings or database roles. Local synchronous commit still requires reliable server storage and suitable replication configuration; it does not prove multi-node failover durability. Have the DBA provision a UTF8 database, account and writable endpoint first. Each MySQL database explicitly maps to a schema within that Kingbase database. Rivomesh may create mapped schemas/tables/indexes and its metadata, but does not install the database or provision accounts. Provide metadata access and relevant schema/table/index creation plus business/checkpoint read/write privileges. A connection check does not prove all DDL/DML privileges. Use MYSQL PASSWORD / KINGBASE PASSWORD environment references or protected configuration. In the UI choose V3 and KingbaseES(PG), then explicit mappings. V2 does not enable this adapter. Linux, Docker, Helm and native Kubernetes use the same task document; deployment manifests do not deploy Kingbase. Data, indexes and recovery Business changes and the destination checkpoint commit in one local transaction, with metadata row locks and epoch fencing. An uncertain commit is resolved by rereading the destination checkpoint. Other targets acknowledge independently; this is not a distributed atomic commit. LOCAL Journal supports same-host recovery; cross-host worker takeover requires an already-supported external PostgreSQL/openGauss/MySQL journal. An unverified Kingbase journal backend is explicitly rejected. Keyless tables gain rivomesh row id to retain duplicate multiplicity. Supported generated expressions follow source-adapter support and their values become ordinary destination columns. UINT64 uses DECIMAL(20,0), decimals retain declared precision, JSON uses JSONB, binary uses BYTEA, microsecond times use TIMESTAMP(6), and signed/over24hour MySQL durations use INTERVAL. Procedures, triggers, foreign keys, partition layouts and arbitrary generated expressions are not automatically reproduced. DOWNGRADE BUSINESS turns business UNIQUE into ordinary indexes; primary/actual identity keys remain unique. Plain BTREE/simple business GSI can use the ordinary-index plan, losing global routing/global uniqueness. Expression, prefix, descending, fulltext and spatial methods require a separate plan. Downgrading assumes valid source constraints, complete ordered replication and exclusive synchronization writes. Reconcile and rebuild required constraints before takeover. Existing UNIQUE constraints are never silently dropped. Nonempty/incompatible targets require an adoption plan; the complete automated takeover workflow remains pending. Transient connection failures back off and reconnect; other sinks continue until journal backpressure applies. Deterministic SQL failures pause only that subscription. Repair the cause, then resume in the UI or with resume config/kingbase-v3.yml kingbase-business errorGeneration using the current status value and the same java -jar ... prefix. This retries the original transaction. Restart does not skip a pause. Missing tables/ownership/checkpoints refuse reuse of old progress; normal resume cannot repair lost data. TIME and native acceptance scope MySQL TIME is a signed duration, not a java.sql.Time/LocalTime wall clock. V3 snapshots and binlog events normalize it as [-]HH:MM:SS.ffffff . The pinned0.30.3 SDK uses duration overrides for ordinary/extended INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE row events; other fields retain its existing codecs. Native tests cover TIME2 precision0..6, negative fractions, over24hours and keyless identity. V2's accepted type range is unchanged. The real pipeline compares integer microseconds for positive/negative25hours, every fractional precision and negative1microsecond. Boundaries/malformed binary have unit coverage. Source reference SQL uses TIMESTAMPDIFF(MICROSECOND,...,ADDTIME(...)) ; this environment's integer TIME TO SEC result and default four-place SQL division are unsuitable microsecond oracles. This Kingbase version returns float8 from EXTRACT(EPOCH), so readback first casts to NUMERIC(20,6), then compares integer microseconds. A generic duration-text mapping does not imply native TIME acceptance for every other adapter. The same actual release also passed cross-schema business/checkpoint rollback, replay, alias ownership, old-epoch refusal, writable checks, PostgreSQL masquerade refusal, snapshot/CDC, target outage while PostgreSQL continues and subsequent catchup, worker SIGKILL preserving generation/snapshot, separate SQL constraint repair/retry on both targets, persistent SQL pause through restart, missing-table isolation and final transactional fences. Other versions/modes, primary/replica clusters/routing, TLS, other JDKs, old nonempty physical backup restore, power loss, soak and hardware capacity remain pending. Existing custom column collations and application takeover require separate assessment. FAQ - Other compatibility modes? They need separate semantics, catalog/type adaptation and native acceptance. Changing an existing instance's mode is not an automatic compatibility fix. - Product/mode mismatch? Check the actual endpoint and SHOW database mode . Do not disguise it as a PostgreSQL target to bypass validation. - SQL ASCII or other encoding? Older vendor images may initialize SQL ASCII. Have the DBA provision a UTF8 database or migrate encoding, then recheck; Rivomesh does not rewrite database encoding in place. - Read-only endpoint? A retryable connection error waits for a writable primary. Database operations perform promotion and endpoint routing; do not reset checkpoints. - String comparison rejected? Check case/trailing-space settings. This profile requires distinct comparisons and never changes global comparison rules. - Existing rows/constraints? Use an explicit adoption plan. Do not clear metadata or drop constraints to continue an old task. - Concurrent business writes? The downgrade profile requires exclusive synchronization writes. Bidirectional conflict handling and the takeover workbench remain pending. - Database installation/license? Supply a properly licensed vendor build for the architecture. Rivomesh does not distribute database binaries/licenses or bypass authorization. Test containers do not require privileged mode. Reproducible native fixture and references With a lawful compatible image available, run bash tests/kingbase-pipeline-run.sh ; override RIVOMESH KINGBASE IMAGE for the same-layout build. The test uses actual release-JAR workers with isolated MySQL8.4/PostgreSQL17/Kingbase services and removes only its own project/volumes. Initialization explicitly selects PG/UTF8 without case-insensitive initialization, running the native server as the image's kingbase user, without sudo/systemd/privileged. Different image layouts require fixture changes; replacing a version tag alone is not acceptance. - Official JDBC guide - Official Docker guide - Official parameter guide - Pinned JDBC POM

title: Managed repair
text: Managed data repair The first managed workflow passed real HTTP/Worker/database acceptance across LOCAL/H2 and external MySQL/PostgreSQL/openGauss journals,with MySQL8.4/PostgreSQL17 business destinations. Evidence. Full vendor,cluster,capacity and security acceptance remains incomplete. Workflow 1. Complete V3 row validation, keep the task paused and open its differing report. 2. Explicitly select differing destination/table pairs and create a plan. Initial profiles are MySQL/PostgreSQL,with a200table selection ceiling. Nothing is selected by default. 3. Open Review repair plan. Check destinations,tables,missing/extra/changed counts,creator and budgets. Explicitly check confirmation and execute. The browser sends the exact server-read plan hash rather than constructing business changes. 4. Inspect job results/target commit receipts. After failure/cancellation,review and retry the same plan;committed tables resolve from receipts without repeating DML. 5. Explicitly resume only after review and obtain a fresh validation when appropriate. Repair does not resume replication,change historical differences to MATCH or authorize cutover. Only authenticated ADMIN may create,review,execute or cancel. The server derives actor identity from authentication. Task/config revisions,request identity,plan hash,report seal and physical checkpoints constrain execution. Durable work and cancellation Admission persists the explicit scope,report and predetermined plan UUID before queuing. Restart reuses that identity. A saved plan with an unfinished controller operation is loaded and checked against its original creator,time and scope. A bounded maintenance queue is separate from normal controls;each task has at most one pending operation. Cancellation persists first,then interrupts the worker. Checkpoint/dependency waits and target scans/DML observe interruption. The current uncommitted table rolls back;previous commits remain. A cancellation can race a successful commit,so a cancelled result does not prove that nothing changed. Review/retry the same plan to resolve native receipts. Completion records per-table counts,original checkpoints and whether a prior attempt committed. Controller audit links authenticated actor,request and plan hashes. Raw business values never enter operations/audit. CLI actor assertions retain their separate host-trust model. The controller data directory contains operations,plans and sealed row reports;an external journal does not replace it. Persist/back up this directory for Linux,Docker and K8s. Local disk loss,multiple controllers on a shared PVC and live K8s node faults require separate acceptance. Never bypass identity/hash checks while restoring older files or metadata. Dependency refusal Plan creation and each table mutation check dependencies. Initial execution rejects incoming/outgoing foreign keys and triggers. PostgreSQL also rejects row security,partitions/inheritance and extra rewrite rules,and takes a table lock during these checks. Nothing is automatically disabled or dropped. MySQL trigger metadata requires TRIGGER privilege;an empty result with insufficient privilege cannot establish absence. See the official MySQL8.4 documentation. Initial visibility checks conservatively require direct global SELECT and TRIGGER grants and reject observed partial revokes. Role-only/schema/table-level combinations are not resolved yet and may return REPAIR METADATA VISIBILITY REQUIRED. Use an organization-reviewed migration account/profile rather than bypassing inspection. The synchronizer must remain the exclusive business writer. Arbitrary concurrent DDL/external writes are outside this contract. Changed roots produce REPAIR TARGET DRIFTED and require a new validation/plan. These checks do not establish arbitrary vendor/procedure/dependency coverage. API Use existing authentication,X-Request-ID and current expectedRevision with POST /api/tasks/TASK ID/actions: The202response already persists operations[].repair.planId. Wait for REPAIR PLAN READY,then GET /api/tasks/TASK ID/validations/REPORT UUID/repairs/PLAN UUID. This review projection contains counts/budgets,no raw rows or guarantee of current eligibility. Execution requires controller desired PAUSED. Cancel with REPAIR CANCEL and no repair payload. Idempotent replay uses the original request ID,body,revision and identity. A new request with a stale revision is rejected before creating another job. FAQ and boundaries A reviewed plan can become ineligible:execution rechecks current data,schema,configuration and pause cut. Wrong hashes are refused by the executor;stale revisions are refused at admission. Retry the same plan to resolve commits after cancellation. A complete real-time progress catalog,independent receipt browsing,report/scratch retention and cleanup remain pending. This mode requires a common cut. Failed-transaction before-image compensation,manual skip/consistency gaps,nonempty adoption,constraint restoration and cutover are separate pending workflows. Plans display default CLI repair budgets;UI budget editing is not implemented. Full vendor/version/cluster/capacity/security/controller-HA matrices remain incomplete. COMMON CUT foundations · Managed validation Development note:the existing general shape guard initially rejected triggers before the repair-specific check,producing a generic console failure. The guard remains intact;repair dependency checks now run first to return the explicit refusal. The corrected specified profiles pass;the failure and correction remain in the evidence.

title: Managed validation
text: Managed data validation The first management workflow supports SQL destination selection, time/staging budgets, durable background jobs, cancellation, sealed-source target retries and per-table summaries. Validation does not change business rows; see managed repair for the subsequent reviewed workflow. Manual skip, constraint rebuilding and cutover remain open. Managed HTTP/database acceptance is separate; earlier CLI/barrier acceptance cannot establish it. Use the console 1. Complete V3 snapshots, run the local Worker and verify shared RUNNING state. Selected destinations must be able to reach the common cut; unselected destinations can be paused/offline. 2. As ADMIN, select transactional SQL destinations under Data validation. Messaging/analytical destinations are excluded. First native row profiles cover MySQL/PostgreSQL; other SQL product versions/modes require separate acceptance. 3. Set source-gate, source-read and per-target-table deadlines plus logical/per-row budgets. Gate maximum is120seconds, reads24hours, rows32MiB. Total logical budget must be at least four times the row budget and includes source, destination and keyless identity records. Physical storage is additional. 4. Start comparison. After checking the current configuration revision, scope, report ID and budgets are persisted before execution in a separate background queue. Establishing the cut briefly blocks MySQL instance writes; business writes can continue after gate release while replication retains its durable pause. 5. Follow operation history, then open the report. Results show source/target counts and missing/extra/changed rows per table,50table results per page. A historical result does not establish current equality. 6. Inspect results/shared state and explicitly resume using the current error version. Validation never clears/repairs business tables, rebuilds UNIQUE or transfers write ownership. Cancel and recover Cancel is a durable request, not resume. Owned read connections/locks are aborted and complete sealed source data is retained. The response does not guarantee release at an exact millisecond:driver/connect/network timeouts also matter. Observe task state and database sessions. Cancellation before establishing a barrier can leave shared RUNNING state; the controller stops its local Worker and displays actual shared state. Once a barrier is established, cancellation never bypasses PAUSED. A sealed source allows Retry target comparison after loading the report. Original configuration/positions/epoch/physical target checkpoints and source integrity are checked; partial destination scans are discarded and reread, even with the source offline. The report's staging budget is retained; retries default to ten minutes per target table. Existing-report quota expansion and richer retry planning remain pending. An incomplete source MVCC view cannot survive process loss. Keep the failed report, inspect/explicitly resume as appropriate, and establish a new cut. Never mix source views or rewrite report hashes/GTIDs. Controller restart can reuse a report ID when complete source data survived but the operation completion did not; without a complete source view/local Worker, it fails explicitly rather than resuming the shared pipeline. One validation runs at a time; ordinary controls use a separate pool. Access, audit and storage ADMIN starts/cancels/retries; OPERATOR/VIEWER read summaries only for granted tasks. Cross-task access is hidden. Mutations require current revision and request ID; replay does not create another job. Previously accepted asynchronous work can continue after authorization changes; subsequent requests use current grants. Audit records actor, task, report ID, request hash and acceptance/completion/cancellation/read events. Corresponding audit writes are required before the HTTP response. Raw business values are excluded from summaries/history. Reports live under platform.dataDirectory/validations/ taskId / reportId . Private plaintext H2 files need protected persistent disk/PVC and coordinated backup; no encryption/external immutable anchor is provided. The console retains approximately40recent operations per task. Older files remain and known report IDs are readable through the API; full report catalogs/retention, large-directory pagination and controller HA remain pending. Local file locking is not cluster HA. API POST /api/tasks/ taskId /actions with X-Request-ID and current expectedRevision : Retry uses VALIDATE RETRY and validation: "reportId":" UUID ","targetMillis":600000 . Cancel uses VALIDATE CANCEL without validation input. GET /api/tasks/ taskId /validations/ reportId reads a summary. VALIDATION REPORT NOT CREATED means inspect the operation failure; VALIDATION REPORT BUSY means retry after the active scan. Core contract and FAQ / 中文 Job recovery paths First native managed acceptance passed LOCAL/H2 and external PostgreSQL/MySQL/openGauss journals with MySQL8.4/PostgreSQL17 destinations, including cancellation during an actual relation-lock wait, sealed-source retry and report/audit persistence across controller restart. See evidence and failure corrections. Administrator difference details For a completed report, ADMIN can open differences per target/table, page by identity hash, then explicitly reveal raw values. Stored source column names/types accompany expected/actual cells. An absent row is distinct from a present SQL NULL cell. Keyless source/target occurrence IDs are displayed without generating replacements. POST /api/tasks/ taskId /validations/ reportId /differences with "target":"postgres","tableId":" table ID ","after":"","limit":25 returns items/next; maximum limit is100. POST .../values with the target/table and identityHash returns columns and expected/actual cells. Null for an entire side means absent row; cell value:null means SQL NULL. OPERATOR/VIEWER remain limited to summaries. Before releasing values, the server checks difference hashes, raw-row checksums and row identity and requires report/scope-linked audit. Business values never enter audit/controller operations. The API checks total UTF-8 raw JSON lengths before fetching CLOBs and refuses more than1MiB with VALIDATION DETAIL TOO LARGE; it never truncates or substitutes an empty row. Large-row chunking/streaming export remains pending; complete private report data is retained. Values remain in page memory and are cleared on logout. These are historical cut values, not live queries or repair. Repair is separate from read-only validation. The new managed repair workflow requires plan review and explicit confirmation;validation itself never changes destination data.

title: Messaging targets
text: Messaging targets: configuration, consumption and recovery 中文：消息目标. Example: messaging-v3.yml. Source/journal operations: V3 manual. Implemented scope V3 implements Kafka, RabbitMQ AMQP 0-9-1, NATS JetStream and Redis Streams publishers. Pulsar transport and pipeline wiring are implemented; mixed recovery acceptance passed. Each destination has its own delivery thread, publication/snapshot checkpoint and error generation. They can run alongside MySQL, PostgreSQL and Gauss targets. A stalled destination does not occupy another delivery thread; all subscriptions still govern journal retention. RocketMQ native TCP has a separately accepted initial transport profile below; snapshot/CDC and three mixed broker restart rounds passed. Artemis Core transport and pipeline wiring are implemented; the focused seven-message-product recovery case passed; see the latest evidence below. ActiveMQ Classic remains required work. The contract is confirmed at-least-once publication . The broker and journal database do not share a transaction. Lost confirmations, or a crash between confirmation and receipt persistence, can cause duplicates. Retries retain event IDs and content; consumers must deduplicate durably. A publisher checkpoint means broker confirmation, not completion of downstream business processing or readiness for cutover. Configuration and UI Choose a message product in the V3 wizard, map each source database to a message namespace and add other SQL/message destinations. The UI provides topic/stream, Kafka security/SASL mechanism, Pulsar admin/cluster, RocketMQ prefix/cluster/broker/retention, token, replica count and size limit, masks credentials, and saves a stopped configuration. Import YAML for multiple endpoints or advanced deployment settings. Namespaces start with a letter and contain only letters, digits and underscores, up to 63 characters. url and messaging.endpoints reject embedded credentials and query parameters. Use separate username/password fields or messaging.token for NATS. Passwords/tokens support $ ENV NAME references and are excluded from events/status. Check opens connections and reads capabilities; it creates no business queues, streams or replication connection. Artemis uses a temporary non-durable management reply channel. Destination cards expose only product, mapping, consistency and consumer topic/stream names; connection URLs and credentials are excluded. A broker confirmation and the downstream consumer's business checkpoint are distinct. Setting Meaning --- --- autoCreate Create resources before first publication. False requires pre-provisioning. Previously initialized missing resources are never recreated automatically replicas JetStream/Kafka replicas, Redis total copies (primary included), or the initial quorum queue member count; does not provision broker nodes maxMessageBytes Complete UTF-8 JSON envelope limit, default 1 MiB; broker limits also apply connectTimeoutMillis / requestTimeoutMillis Connection and confirmation/management timeout, 100–120000 ms endpoints Additional entrances to the same broker cluster, never independent replacement clusters Kafka topic Dedicated topic for this subscription; all mapped databases/tables share it Kafka securityProtocol / saslMechanism PLAINTEXT, SSL, SASL PLAINTEXT, SASL SSL; SASL supports PLAIN and SCRAM-SHA-256/512 For Rabbit's default / vhost use amqp://host:5672 or amqp://host:5672/%2f . amqp://host:5672/ selects an empty vhost name under the AMQP URI specification. Additional nodes must use the same scheme/vhost. amqps:// and NATS tls:// use JVM trust configuration. Username/password or token authentication is implemented; NKey/JWT files, certificate wizard and a complete TLS acceptance matrix remain pending. Resources and confirmation Each namespace uses namespace. schema , namespace. transactions and namespace.table . Names containing routing syntax, excessive length, or a / rm prefix use rm followed by SHA-256(table ID) for the table channel. The envelope/schema retain the original database/table names. Control channels are reserved. Kafka writes all logical channels into messaging.topic , retaining the channel in the rivomesh channel header. A dedicated single-partition topic is required, with acks=all, enable.idempotence=true and max.in.flight=1. This is not a native transactional Kafka producer; the same at-least-once contract applies. Replicas match configuration, min.insync.replicas is replicas/2+1 , unclean election is disabled, retention.ms/bytes are -1 and cleanup.policy is delete. Plan consumer archival/retention; compaction must not silently evict history. Partition growth or policy changes require a plan. One partition has hardware throughput limits. Every broker must disable auto.create.topics.enable ; explicit first-time Admin creation remains available. Otherwise producer metadata refresh could recreate a deleted empty topic and conceal lost history. Preparation checks every broker and requires the relevant DescribeConfigs permission. Topics need Describe/DescribeConfigs/Write and initially Create. Existing replica/ISR/size/retention mismatches block rather than being overwritten. The stable Kafka clusterId is bound in the journal; reconnecting to another cluster raises BROKER IDENTITY CHANGED . Rabbit uses durable, nonexclusive, non-auto-delete queues, direct routing through the default exchange, persistent messages, publisher confirms and mandatory/return. Returns/nacks never advance the receipt. Quorum is the default; classic is selectable. Created queues use reject-publish overflow. Broker policies must not silently discard old/expired messages or dead-letter redeliveries without a recovery consumer. Production quorum requires multiple nodes and appropriate replicas. Single-node tests do not establish majority-loss or power-loss guarantees. NATS uses JetStream publish ACKs and Nats-Msg-Id , never volatile Core NATS. Streams require File storage, Limits retention, Discard New, no age expiry, exact namespace. subjects and configured replicas. The description binds pipeline/subscription/generation; incompatible existing streams are rejected rather than altered. Finite capacity rejects new publication. The publisher does not automatically delete consumer history: plan capacity, archival and consumer checkpoints. Broker fsync, replication and disk determine power-loss durability. Pre-provisioned streams with autoCreate: false must match the same properties and binding. The binding is rivomesh: plus SHA-256(pipelineId + ':' + subscriptionId + ':' + generation) . Read generation from initialized status; prefer service creation for a new task rather than guessing it. Redis Streams The first Redis profile supports a direct standalone primary running Redis 7.2 or newer . Use redis://host:6379/0 or rediss://host:6379/0 , a database number, separate ACL username/password and messaging.stream . Additional endpoints, Sentinel, Cluster routing and proxy failover are not implemented in this profile. rediss enables hostname verification and JVM trust configuration; actual TLS acceptance remains pending. All logical channels share one physical stream. Each entry contains body , rivomesh event id , rivomesh channel , optional rivomesh key , and transport headers. Redis-generated entry IDs are transport positions, not event identities or MySQL order. Consumers use the same envelope staging/deduplication rules as other message targets. The reserved marker consumer group rivomesh stream marker v1 creates an empty stream without a fake business event; it is not a consumer checkpoint. Preparation requires AOF enabled, maxmemory-policy=noeviction , no TTL on either stream or ownership keys, and a writable non-cluster primary. Ownership is bound per stream in rivomesh publication owners v1 . Existing unowned streams require an adoption plan; another binding is rejected. Previously initialized missing resources are not silently recreated. XADD NOMKSTREAM prevents accidental recreation after deletion while connected. Administrators must not purge/trim/expire these keys; same-name replacement or an old storage backup still requires reconciliation. Each batch uses XADD followed by WAITAOF on the same physical connection . Both returned fsync counts must satisfy local =1 and replicas = replicas-1 ; a timeout alone is not confirmation. The socket factory forbids SDK socket reopening: retries construct a new authenticated client with the configured database, preventing accidental writes into database 0. Server run ID and client ID are also compared around publication to reject hidden connection replacement. AOF write failure, insufficient replicas, OOM under noeviction and disconnection preserve the receipt and retry. replicas: 1 confirms only local AOF, without Redis failover durability. Higher counts require the corresponding live replicas with AOF; they do not provision replication or prove lossless promotion. RDB alone and volatile Pub/Sub are insufficient. The publisher ACL needs connection/auth/select as applicable, INFO, CONFIG GET maxmemory-policy, CLIENT ID, EXISTS/TYPE/PTTL, HGET/HSETNX, XGROUP CREATE, XADD and WAITAOF, limited to the selected stream and ownership hash. Consumers need their own read/group permissions. check reads capabilities without creating keys. WAITAOF and fsync can affect latency; measure against the actual storage and replication topology. No automatic stream trimming is performed; capacity and consumer-safe archival remain an operator responsibility. Pulsar Pulsar uses a dedicated persistent, non-partitioned topic for all mapped namespaces. Configure url: pulsar://host:6650 , messaging.adminUrl: http://host:8080 , cluster , and topic: persistent://tenant/namespace/topic . The tenant/namespace must already exist and belong to exactly the configured cluster; geo-replication needs a separate plan. The first profile uses one service endpoint with native broker discovery; extra endpoints and username/password authentication are rejected. Token authentication uses messaging.token . TLS requires both pulsar+ssl:// and HTTPS admin access with hostname verification. Actual token/TLS and multi-broker/BookKeeper-failure acceptance remain pending. Every active broker must disable automatic topic creation and inactive-topic deletion and enable topic-level policies. Namespace overrides must not re-enable automatic creation. The publisher reads these settings through advertised admin endpoints, requiring cluster/broker/namespace management-read permissions as well as topic operations. Native reconnect must not recreate a deleted empty topic. Restrict administrative policy changes during publication; existence/binding checks cannot detect every purge or restoration of an old backup. Initial creation atomically binds rivomesh.owner to the common pipeline/subscription/generation binding and marks rivomesh.provision=BUILDING V1 . Only that unfinished owned topic is provisioned: infinite retention in both time and size, TTL 0, inactive deletion disabled, BookKeeper persistence, and backlog policies that reject producers rather than evict consumers' history. Applied policies are verified before marking READY V1 and opening a producer. Asynchronous policy propagation retries without publishing. Existing READY policy mismatches, unowned topics or another binding require a plan and are not overwritten. Pre-provisioning with autoCreate: false requires matching ownership, READY V1 and all policies; missing initialized topics never get an empty replacement. replicas means minimum BookKeeper ACK copies for this profile. Fresh topics use ensemble/write/ACK quorum all equal to this value. An existing compatible topic may use a larger ensemble/write quorum if its ACK quorum meets the configured minimum. This setting does not provision bookies, broker replicas or failure domains. Confirmations rely on BookKeeper's durable journal/replication configuration and recoverable metadata. A single-bookie test is not a production HA or power-loss guarantee. Retention is infinite, so plan capacity, archival and consumer-safe history removal. Publication sends bytes synchronously with batching/chunking disabled and bounded pending requests. Message properties carry immutable event ID, logical channel and transport headers; the Pulsar key carries the logical row/transaction key. BookKeeper-confirmed send completion precedes the journal receipt. Pulsar message IDs and broker-side deduplication are not substitutes for event-ID deduplication and transaction staging. Native Pulsar transactions are not used; the common at-least-once contract applies across producer replacement and source lease handoff. The Java 8 client is pinned to Pulsar 4.0.14 behind rivomesh-pulsar-transport . Its logging, crypto, Jackson annotations and protobuf are isolated from core dependencies. This is deliberate: later Pulsar client branches require newer Java, while the 4.0 branch retains Java 8 support. Build the reactor with mvn verify so the private SDK is packaged before the application. The transport test runs with the core JAR first on the classpath and verifies both dependency sets coexist; it also verifies read-only check, ownership, send/read, broker restart, retention refusal and lost-topic protection. Full mixed-pipeline recovery acceptance is recorded separately in validation. Broker startup and source catch-up are different measurements. The failure harness first verifies that SQL continues while stopped brokers report automatic retry, then waits for broker health, then measures catch-up without manual Resume. A broker whose admin service or storage is still starting cannot be treated as a ready destination. Recovery diagnostics include safe error codes such as PULSAR ADMIN HTTP 503 ; no row data or credentials are copied into status.
