Active-active conflict merging and cross-environment global transactions are separate advanced projects, not implied first-release guarantees. 14. Delivery sequence and completion Phase Delivery/acceptance --- --- P0 Foundation Rename, source-neutral events/positions/SPI, capability matrix, configuration versions, task/subscription isolation; preserve existing recovery regressions P1 Correctness/UI foundation Keyless/JSON/generated columns, baseline/DDL recovery, relational targets, wizard/incidents; object/transaction/fault matrix P2 Storage/distribution Three journals, fan-out, all in-scope MQ, ClickHouse/Doris/Hive; lost ACK/duplicates/reordering/partial batches/quotas P3 Migration closure Existing targets, validation/repair, constraint restoration, cutover gates/audit, Linux/Docker/Helm/native YAML, full bilingual manual P4 Performance/product acceptance Hardware benchmarks, soak/fault/upgrade matrix, security configuration/offline delivery; truthful status per target Later source milestones PostgreSQL/Oracle connectors and snapshot/long-transaction/failover acceptance before verified reverse paths Phasing does not demote in-scope message targets or objects to optional suggestions. Every stage delivers runnable functionality, matching UI, bilingual documentation, and fault tests. Do not mark design-only adapters available. Apache preparation separately includes name review, community/governance, ownership/dependency terms, LICENSE/NOTICE, reproducible builds, and test infrastructure. Rivomesh is not currently an Apache project. ASF naming.

title: Reconciliation workflow
text: Data reconciliation, repair and a common cut The common barrier, MySQL consistent view, private disk staging, transactional SQL row comparison and CLI are implemented. The LOCAL/H2 and external PostgreSQL/MySQL/openGauss barrier profiles passed native acceptance; the newer row-comparison scope is recorded separately. The first COMMON CUT repair CLI is now accepted in the linked repair handbook; the first managed repair UI is separately accepted;other compensation modes and cutover remain incomplete. Implemented foundation SourceAdapter.ConsistentRead represents one view across tables. Source-specific covers interprets position coverage; generic SourcePosition does not order GTID/LSN/SCN strings. MySQL uses GTID-set coverage. PipelineValidationBarrier.open(config, selectedTargets, maximumGateMillis, maximumReadMillis) checks the existing journal identity/running state/completed snapshots, obtains a bounded MySQL global read lock, establishes one REPEATABLE READ view and pins declared table metadata across configured databases. It records the source cut, waits for capture/normalization and selected target ACKs, then rechecks generation/epoch/position/sequence/snapshot acknowledgments under the journal job lock before persistently pausing and incrementing the epoch. Selected SQL targets acquire local transactional fences and must report the same sequence. JdbcSink.existing never creates lost checkpoint metadata. The source write gate is released while its MVCC view remains available for table reads. Unselected targets can be paused or offline; they are not presented as validated. The certificate contains source/capture positions, configuration fingerprint, generation, epoch, sequence, error version, schema hashes and selected target checkpoints. It proves a synchronization boundary, not row equality. Concurrent control or checkpoint changes invalidate eligibility. Source writes may continue after gate release; the task stays paused until explicit recovery processes later binlog events. Bounds and recovery The explicit source-gate limit is1–120seconds; the read session has a separate limit, at least as long and at most24hours. Deadlines abort owned connections, with session wait timeout as an additional cleanup measure. No global settings are changed. Network failures prevent an exact millisecond guarantee of server-side unlock; monitor database sessions as well. The source MVCC transaction holds table metadata locks and old row versions, which can delay DDL and grow undo. Native tests observe actual lock waits and release. Early closure of an unfinished cursor aborts the entire validation view instead of draining an unbounded result or treating a partial scan as complete. SIGKILL releases connections; durable pause cannot be bypassed by restart. Lost MVCC views cannot be reconstructed from files; incomplete source scans need a new cut. Fence failure retains the persisted pause. The protocol assumes a consistent writable destination endpoint and does not replace database HA routing/old-primary isolation. Selected destinations currently use transactional SQL. MQ producer acknowledgement is not downstream data validation; analytical visibility/materialization requires product-specific support. Primary MySQL references: consistent snapshots, FLUSH, session timeouts. Row comparison and CLI The synchronizer must be the only writer of destination business tables. Begin with a RUNNING pipeline, completed snapshots and selected targets able to reach the common cut. Establishing the cut briefly blocks writes across the MySQL instance. After releasing source writes, the pipeline stays PAUSED until explicitly resumed. CLI defaults:30second source gate,1hour source view,10minutes per destination table,1GiB logical staging budget and4MiB per row. Java callers can set explicit limits. Source rows, target rows and keyless identity records all consume the budget; it is not a1GiB source-data allowance. Physical-file checks run at batch commit boundaries; H2 pages/indexes/temporary data can require additional space. Use filesystem/container quotas for a hard physical limit. Large-scale capacity remains unaccepted. The source scan uses the original MVCC view. Keyless occurrence IDs are paged from the durable journal and matched against the complete canonical source multiset. Only complete source scans are sealed. Supported POSIX systems use0700directories/0600files, with same-process and cross-process writer locks. Staging is not encrypted; place it on appropriately private storage. Each destination scan holds the physical checkpoint row lock on the same connection used for reading. Ownership, schema, completed snapshot and exact checkpoint are checked without recreating metadata, advancing sequence or modifying business rows. Types share the synchronization canonicalization contract. Keyless internal identities are compared as well as values; equal data with wrong identities yields missing and extra differences. MySQL TIME expressions are explicitly cast to CHAR for source snapshots, consistent views, virtual-generated evaluation and target validation. This avoids JDBC temporal formatting losing a negative subsecond sign: -00:00:00.000001 must remain negative one microsecond. MySQL FLOAT32 targets explicitly use FLOAT; default-mode REAL aliases DOUBLE, as documented in the official numeric type reference. Existing incorrect table types need an explicit migration plan; validation never alters them automatically. Per-target/table results contain counts, content roots and missing , extra , changed totals. Equal results produce VALIDATION MATCH , otherwise VALIDATION DIFFERENCES . The Java store supports identity-hash keyset pages of up to200differences. Summaries omit business row values; raw values in private staging remain sensitive. Recovery boundaries: - An interrupted incomplete source scan cannot resume its lost MVCC cursor. Inspect the durable pause, explicitly resume as appropriate and establish a new cut. Never mix source views. - Once source data is sealed, validate-compare checks configuration/generation/epoch/error version/positions and physical target checkpoints, validates the source seal and row checksums, discards partial destination scans and rereads them. The source database need not be online during this phase. - Resuming/reconfiguring the pipeline or changing checkpoints invalidates continued comparison. Historical reports remain readable and do not prove current equality. - Success, failure and timeout all retain the pause. Use the current error version with the existing status / resume-pipeline controls to resume explicitly. The first end-to-end native comparison profile uses MySQL8.4 sources and PostgreSQL17/MySQL8.4 destinations. Other transactional adapters share the reader interface but their vendor/version/mode/distributed acceptance remains separate. Messaging and analytical destinations do not yet implement this comparison protocol. FAQ - Why did replication stop advancing after validation? Establishing the cut durably pauses it. Review the report/task state and explicitly resume using the current error version. Monitor source binlog retention and journal capacity while paused. - Can a longer timeout resume an incomplete source scan? A lost MySQL MVCC transaction cannot be reconstructed. Keep the failed report, follow explicit task recovery and establish a new cut with an appropriate read budget. - Why can equal keyless business values still produce missing/extra rows? Incorrect occurrence IDs break later UPDATE/DELETE processing. Counts or business-value-only comparison would miss this. - Can I rewrite hashes after VALIDATION SOURCE SEAL MISMATCH ? Do not alter the summary/H2 contents to force acceptance. It can indicate corruption, changed data or a development-era report format difference. Retain evidence and establish a new validation run; historical summaries remain useful for diagnosis. - Did validation repair rows or rebuild UNIQUE constraints? No. It only reads destinations. Reviewed repair and pre-takeover constraint restoration require subsequent workflows. Remaining workflow The first management jobs, cancellation, summaries, task grants and report audit now have bilingual UI/API. ADMIN raw difference-row details are now implemented; complete report catalogs/retention, richer retry/quota planning and job/controller HA remain pending. Keyless repair must retain journal occurrence IDs. Additional vendor/type/mode/fault profiles remain to be verified. Reviewed repair plans must show affected objects/counts/boundaries, enforce authorization/configuration versions/idempotency/audit, commit business repair and native receipts locally without rewriting the synchronization GTID/sequence, and resolve lost responses. Arbitrary nonempty adoption and failed-transaction compensation/skip need separate consistency-gap handling. Final cutover needs a fresh final source barrier, target visibility/data checks, restored constraints and write handoff; an earlier historical cut after source writes resumed is not a current takeover permit. 中文 The first managed workflow now supports destination selection, background jobs, cancellation, target retries and table summaries. See Managed validation. ADMIN raw difference-row UI is now implemented. Managed repair UI is now separately accepted;cutover UI remains pending. The first COMMON CUT repair CLI now has four-journal native acceptance for MySQL/PostgreSQL. It is separate from validation-only operations and has a separately accepted authenticated managed workflow;failed-transaction compensation and cutover remain pending.

title: Recovery & consistency
text: V2 recovery, primary failover and consistency 中文：恢复、主库切换与一致性. This document describes the v2 single-database, single-target core . V3 uses MVCC snapshot artifacts, a separate journal and independent destinations: follow the V3 manual and message contract. V2 state cannot be adopted simply by setting formatVersion: 3 . Service ownership Processes create v2 metadata idempotently, handling concurrent catalog creation separately. Initial task configuration and discovered-table manifests are inserted atomically. Conditional updates claim the owner and lease; a separate heartbeat renews the lease, and data/progress transactions check the same owner. Each new work session uses a new owner identity so callbacks from an older replication connection cannot commit into the new session. The task-row lock serializes capture, snapshot and application commits. After ownership transfers, the old owner is rejected before business writes and cannot pause or release the new owner's task. Standby nodes do not open binlog connections; a healthy task normally has one replication client. Persistent GTID state - capture gtid : the initial baseline plus committed source transactions durably queued or irrelevant to the selected business database. - required gtid : the union of captured transactions and the GTIDs required by source state already read during snapshot/discovery. - applied sequence : the queued transaction sequence already applied to business tables. Physical UUIDs and file positions support diagnostics and backend validation; cross-server recovery uses GTIDs. A complete source commit is persisted before adding its GTID to capture gtid . The connector's possibly earlier in-memory GTID is never copied directly over persistent progress. Duplicate GTIDs are checked under the task lock and do not enqueue the same durable transaction twice. Primary failover during a snapshot After recording baseline B0, capture FULL row images while scanning by primary-key cursor. Every chunk records a source GTID watermark after reading; its business rows, last key and read dependency commit together. Discovery and initial scan-upper-bound reads also contribute to required gtid . A snapshot may have read a transaction from the former primary before the capture connection persisted it. Validating only capture gtid would miss that dependency. A failover candidate must therefore include required gtid . After all chunks complete, record B1, wait until capture gtid includes B1, then replay the queue in source commit order. The scan imports unchanged rows; the final full row image or DELETE establishes the result for changed rows. Primary-key changes remove the old key and write the new key. Logs cover inserts before the scan cursor and beyond the initial upper bound. During snapshot and early replay, the target is not a consistent image of one source instant. During continuous incremental application, every source transaction, including cross-table changes, is applied in one destination transaction. This v2 cursor approach differs from v3's restart/rebase of an incomplete MVCC snapshot. Primary discovery and selection 1. Probe candidate addresses for UUID, server id, read-only state, GTID mode, executed/purged sets and replication health. 2. In ordinary primary/replica topologies, select only a writable node without active upstream threads or residual replication errors. 3. For Group Replication, require ONLINE, PRIMARY, writable and single-primary mode. 4. Multiple writable primaries require external isolation; the service does not arbitrarily choose one. 5. Require required gtid ⊆ candidate.gtid executed ; otherwise wait for catch-up. 6. Require candidate.gtid purged ⊆ capture gtid ; otherwise necessary uncaptured history may already be unavailable, so block progress. 7. Reconnect with persistent GTID auto-positioning. Automatic fallback to the purged set is disabled. JDBC queries validate physical UUID and writability; the replication connection validates its handshake server id before processing events. If a router/VIP sends these connections to different backends, abandon the session and rediscover. Heartbeat expiry, disconnection or source role changes also establish a new session from persistent GTIDs. Operators must ensure candidates belong to the same logical topology, replicate all selected data, and have no filtering or forged GTIDs. Equal GTID sets cannot detect every manual data modification. CDC cannot reconstruct permanently lost asynchronous transactions that never reached a surviving candidate. Rivomesh does not promote MySQL nodes. Transaction boundaries Operation Contents committed in one destination transaction --- --- Create task Configuration fingerprint, B0, table manifest, scan upper bounds and discovery watermark Snapshot chunk Business rows, cursor, row count, completion state and read-dependency GTIDs Capture commit Complete ordered row events, origin, GTID, capture/required sets Apply commit All row changes, applied sequence, phase changes and queue deletion Record failure Error history, shared run state, safe context and owner release An uncertain commit ends the current work session. The new session rereads persistent progress instead of reusing an old in-memory cursor/GTID. Business tables, queues and state tables must be backed up/restored as one recovery unit. SQL errors and shared pause Connection/serialization SQL states 08/40, lock waits and recoverable resource failures retry with backoff. Data, constraints, permissions and syntax errors pause. Safe error context includes table, source GTID, queued transaction sequence, SQLState and vendor code; row payloads and SQL literals are excluded. A failed destination transaction rolls back completely and retains the queue head. Capture may already have safely persisted later commits; application does not pass the failed transaction. PAUSED is shared database state: restarting or adding standby processes cannot bypass it. Repair the cause, then resume the original transaction. Resume does not skip rows, alter GTIDs or empty queues. Database operators repair source replication SQL errors. The service does not execute SQL SLAVE SKIP COUNTER, inject empty GTIDs or RESET. A failed replica does not interrupt capture from a healthy primary; promotion of that unhealthy replica is rejected until repaired and caught up. V1 file-position tasks lack complete GTIDs and read dependencies. Automatic in-place upgrade is refused and old state is preserved. Consult validation for accepted versions and fault profiles; manual repair/skip, v2-to-v3 migration and automated business cutover remain unfinished.

title: Rename migration
text: Rivomesh rename and existing-task migration Updated: 2026-11-14. 中文：更名迁移. This change migrates project identity/build references without changing replication algorithms, v2 state formats, configuration fingerprints, or SQL-error handling. Names Object New value --- --- Project / root Maven artifactId Rivomesh / rivomesh Directory rivomesh , alongside canal Maven groupId / Java base package io.rivomesh Executable artifactId / entry point rivomesh-app / io.rivomesh.Main Relocated driver artifactId / JDBC class rivomesh-gaussdb-driver / io.rivomesh.gaussdb.jdbc.Driver Source module directories Retain sync-app and gaussdb-driver ; directory names need not equal artifactIds Technical naming does not establish domain/trademark ownership or Apache acceptance; review separately before public release. Existing installations 1. Stop every old service node for the task; do not mix driver-package versions on one task. 2. Back up configuration and business/management data as one recovery unit. Preserve jobId, logical clusterId, source database, target URL/schema, and metadata schema. Never delete state or clear business tables for a rename. 3. Change any explicit target driver to io.rivomesh.gaussdb.jdbc.Driver ; omitting it selects the new default. Do not substitute the test PostgreSQL driver for the relocated Gauss driver. 4. Update working directories, classpaths, JAR paths, monitoring/log references to sync-app/target/rivomesh-app-0.1.0-SNAPSHOT.jar . Recompile custom code using renamed entry/model classes. 5. Run check/status, verify existing state, then run. PAUSED remains paused; repair and resume rather than bypassing errors through renaming. Moving the root does not update external file contents. Check relative paths against the new working directory. Private local.yml is not rewritten automatically; repository examples/defaults are updated. Recovery boundary The rename introduces no multi-source/multi-target/new-journal state format. Those changes require separate migrations, compatibility checks, and rollback plans; package changes alone cannot make incompatible checkpoints reusable. See README and validation for current operation, and platform design for planned capabilities.

title: Requirements & decisions
text: Rivomesh requirements, decisions, and implementation boundaries Updated: 2026-11-16. 中文：需求与决策. This document records scope and implementation status. Accepted requirements are not released features. See the README for current operation and platform design for capabilities and scenarios. New/clarified scope and gaps use SDD baseline RM-SDD-001:48traceable requirements,tasks and acceptance contracts. Current behavior remains governed by implementation status and evidence. Confirmed decisions ID Decision Current implementation --- --- --- D01 Each independent task configuration binds one logical source, initially MySQL; the platform may manage multiple configurations/independent sources, with standalone task deployment retained Web/CLI support v2/v3, multi-database/target wizard, independent recovery and journal selection D02 Select multiple databases per topology with explicit target instance/database/schema mappings Web/CLI v3 implement databases and per-target mappings ; see V3 manual D03 Fan out one source to multiple targets/products Web/CLI v3 implement independent target ACKs, fault isolation and recovery D04 Support MySQL5.7/8.0/8.2/8.4 sources;accept standalone/GTID ASYNC/single-primary MGR per profile Basic5.7,historical8.0 V2/HA and representative8.4 V3 evidence exist;8.2 dedicated acceptance and the full matrix remain D05 Broad MySQL,PostgreSQL,openGauss,distributed GaussDB,DM,Kingbase,OceanBase and GBase product/version/mode scope Specified initial MySQL/PG/openGauss/DM/Kingbase/GBase8c profiles exist;distributed GaussDB,full OceanBase recovery,GBase8a/8s and more modes remain D06 Relax Gauss business secondary UNIQUE to ordinary indexes, avoiding GSI solely for those indexes; permit relaxation for compatibility issues on other targets V3 ordinary secondary indexes/business UNIQUE downgrade implemented; GSI has model plans; distributed hardware acceptance pending D07 Only the synchronization service writes subscribed target tables; validate and restore required constraints before takeover Exclusive writes currently required; takeover workflow planned D08 Automatic recovery does not skip;manual skip/compensation requires review,original evidence and gaps;database promotion stays external Some ASYNC/MGR/worker takeover and original-transaction retry pass;manual skip/failed-transaction compensation are not implemented D09 Linux manual, Docker, Kubernetes Helm Chart and native manifests, comprehensive bilingual manuals/FAQ Deployment files and bilingual operations manual provided; live K8s/full-platform acceptance remain D10 Final name Rivomesh, directory rivomesh , Java package/Maven groupId io.rivomesh Renamed in this change; no claim of domain/trademark clearance or Apache status D11 Include no-PK tables, JSON, and STORED/VIRTUAL generated columns in first-release scope V3 keyless multisets, JSON, STORED and whitelisted VIRTUAL materialization implemented/tested D12 Optional independent log storage; deployment with or without it V3 H2 local and PostgreSQL/openGauss/MySQL external journals with independent ACKs/safe reclamation implemented D13 Broad support for existing nonempty targets, object differences, and takeover Initial targets must be empty;COMMON CUT repair exists while nonempty adoption/merge remains pending D14 Publish reproducible hardware/workload/performance standards instead of universal TPS promises Benchmark tooling and small SQL/JDK smoke evidence exist;representative capacity standards and soak remain D15 Complete bilingual UI,wizards,diagnostics and guided recovery Local workbench,grants,configuration,validation and MySQL/PG COMMON CUT repair exist;global control,persistent login,skip/patch and cutover remain D16 Government/enterprise domestic-database migration, staged switching, and parallel environments One-way mirroring is the foundation; ownership/takeover/failback boundaries in platform design D17 ClickHouse,Apache Doris,Apache Hive and extensible analytical destinations All three have initial materialization/recovery profiles;cluster/security/capacity/all-JDK gates remain without relational-transaction promises D18 Kafka,Pulsar,RabbitMQ,RocketMQ,ActiveMQ Classic/Artemis,Redis Streams and NATS JetStream All have initial transport/recovery evidence;complete cluster/TLS/capacity and new skip/compensation protocols need per-adapter acceptance D19 PostgreSQL and Oracle sources are committed implementation scope,with neutral SPI/events/positions retained Actual sources remain MySQL;PG/Oracle SOURCE is PLANNED and native snapshot/CDC/recovery remains D20 Unified multi-node inventory/control;any entry manages remote tasks Worker lease/owner foundations exist;global registry,remote command plane and control HA do not D21 Login survives reload with logout,expiry,revocation and cross-controller policy Current token is page-memory-only;server sessions/reload restoration remain D22 Reviewed transaction skip,controlled source-gap recovery and guided manual corrective data COMMON CUT repair is not failed-transaction compensation;new modes,gap ledger and UI/API remain D23 Java8/11/17/21/25 require real current-release profile evidence Java8 baseline and an older ten-profile SQL matrix exist;complete current-platform/driver/recovery matrix remains D24 Use SDD specification/design/task/acceptance tracing and complete bilingual docs RM-SDD-001 v0.2 closes4single-controller session requirements;44remain tracked The platform boundary is one source per task, multiple tasks per platform . No implicit source merging or cross-source transactions. Isolated workers may run under one console or as separate deployments. source.nodes still lists candidates in one topology. Isolate task IDs, state namespaces, quotas, and replication client server IDs; reject overlapping target tables by default. Multiple databases and targets This example expresses product intent. For runnable configuration see the V3 manual and config/pipeline-v3.yml : Task MySQL database Target instance Target namespace --- --- --- --- sales orders gauss-a app / orders sales crm gauss-a app / crm sales orders doris-b analytics / orders legacy finance dm-c Explicit product-specific namespace Version mappings and check case rules, reserved words, shortened names, and collisions. New subscriptions establish their own baseline rather than reusing another cursor. Independent configurations capture separately by default; sharing requires explicit association and compatible source identity, filters, security, and storage policies. Within a v3 task, the runner shares ordered logs and routes events with independent snapshot, delivery/application/visibility positions and errors per target. One target's SQL failure should not pause others; shared decoding failures may affect all targets in that task. Apply complete source transactions atomically where the relational target supports that scope. No cross-target XA is introduced. Probe Doris single/multi-table transaction support per version; use dedicated batch/materialization protocols for ClickHouse/Hive. Reject unmet task consistency requirements, or require an explicit weaker mode explained by the UI. Recovery and log storage Preserve atomic data/local-checkpoint commits and owner fencing for transactional sinks. Other sinks require replayable batches, resolved commit acknowledgments, deduplication/versioning, and visibility watermarks. Advancing an external checkpoint first is not a substitute. Mode No extra independent store Failure boundary --- --- --- Local durable journal Yes; persistent directory/volume Process recovery; permanent disk loss is not guaranteed lossless; cross-node takeover requires original logs and reliable fencing Target-hosted journal Yes, for targets with required transactional/state capabilities Failure of that target can block capture; arbitrary analytics engines cannot host the current Gauss metadata unchanged Independent shared journal No; an explicitly supported HA backend Enables cross-node worker recovery, subject to journal availability/capacity Persist logs before capture GTID advances. Reclaim only after all active subscriptions and baseline dependencies permit it. Alert/backpressure at quotas rather than silently discard unconsumed data. Per-task quotas must prevent one offline target from exhausting the platform. Failover verifies captured and all relevant snapshot-read dependency GTIDs. CDC cannot recover permanently lost source transactions; editing GTIDs must not bypass gaps. Distributed metadata needs compatible keys/constraints and a durable stream sequence, not CN-generated IDs, timestamps, or lexical GTID ordering. Compatibility and index policy Broad support means capability detection and a matrix identifying product/version/mode/engine/driver, objects, and consistency level. Distinguish verified, experimental, unverified, and unsupported. JDBC connectivity does not prove replication support; a feature in one release cannot be assumed for older versions. Other targets may relax incompatible business secondary UNIQUE constraints into ordinary indexes or supported access structures, with an explicit difference manifest. Report the absence of an equivalent structure honestly. Candidate identity keys on no-PK tables, technical keys, and Doris/ClickHouse materialization keys are not optional business secondary constraints. See Gauss index policy and platform design. Decisions no longer blocking design Broad product coverage, hardware-based performance standards, optional storage, no-PK/JSON/generated columns, existing targets, conditional UNIQUE relaxation, Rivomesh naming, independent configurations, and Web UI are confirmed. Do not repeatedly ask whether these features are needed. An onboarding wizard obtains actual versions, modes, namespaces, volumes, and privileges and produces compatibility/sizing reports. Listing every future customer environment now is unnecessary. Conflict priorities for existing data, destructive changes, and production switching still require task-specific choices; broad compatibility does not authorize arbitrary overwrites/deletions. Classify DDL by operation/capability: additions, compatible changes, destructive changes, generated-expression changes, and partition changes, with automatic, planned-migration, or blocked outcomes. Including the three requested object types does not imply every MySQL engine/function/DDL is automatically compatible. Delivery and acceptance Suggested order: rename → capability/task isolation → identity/JSON/generated columns/DDL → optional journals/adapters → UI recovery/validation → takeover → full benchmark/delivery matrix. Deliver UI operations alongside core features rather than waiting for every adapter. Test task isolation, cross-database transactions, target-specific recovery, journal GC/backpressure, duplicate counts on keyless tables, historical generated expressions, JSON precision, existing-target reconciliation, analytics retry/visibility, source failover, and stale owners. Validation separately records v2 HA, v3 three-target/two-journal, HTTP/DOM and broker tests. Repeated executions are not summed as distinct cases; remaining scope needs dedicated acceptance. FAQ Can configurations connect to independent MySQL sources? Yes. The platform now loads independent configurations and manages isolated workers/checkpoints. Standalone CLI remains. See console manual for boundaries. Do parallel environments imply writes to the same table on both sides? No. Start with one writer/multiple readers, shadow validation, or explicit domain ownership. Independent writers require additional source capture, conflict resolution, loop prevention, and application routing beyond current one-way MySQL CDC. Can every target share identical DDL/write SQL? No. Reuse the event model; adapters own types, indexes, transactions, batch commits, and reading semantics. Are all new features available now? No. Renaming, v3 fan-out, keyless/JSON/supported generated columns, optional journals, Web and Kafka/RabbitMQ/NATS/Redis Streams/Pulsar/RocketMQ are implemented. Complete DDL, remaining adapters, permissions/repair and business switching remain in development. Enable features according to the implementation/validation matrices.

title: Security audit
text: Security audit, retention and export 中文：安全审计. This records management API/controller events separately from the 40-operation task history and configuration revisions. Scope and permissions Only ADMIN can read/export or open Security audit . VIEWER/OPERATOR attempts are denied and audited. API requests record HTTP BEGIN / HTTP END : authenticated actor/role, fixed route category, known task ID, direct peer IP, HTTP status and safe error code. Authentication failures have no actor and status 401; authorization/Origin denials record 403. Health probes/static files are excluded. Raw URLs/queries, Authorization, bodies, credentials, rows and exception text are excluded. Client request IDs are SHA-256 hashes for correlation, not raw arbitrary headers. Forwarded IP headers are not trusted. HTTP END means response prepared, not delivered. A 202 is not successful execution. OPERATION COMMITTED records durable PENDING and SUCCEEDED/FAILED outcomes, actor and operation-request hash; configuration edit/restore outcomes are included. Startup/orderly shutdown have separate events. Internal calls without HTTP attribution and older history are not assigned invented identities. CLI replication, business SQL and OS activity are outside this controller audit. Durability and failures dataDirectory/audit/events.mv.db uses H2 transactions, synchronous writes, contiguous sequences and a SHA-256 chain. The private audit directory is 0700 and database 0600 where POSIX permissions exist; protect other platforms with ACLs. Startup verifies the retained chain/tail. The controller registry binds the audit store identity: deleting/replacing it with a new empty database refuses startup. Stop the controller and coherently back up registry, audit, configuration revisions and journals; copying a live H2 file is not a consistent backup. An API begin event must persist before the request executes. Failure returns 503 AUDIT UNAVAILABLE , preventing that HTTP management action. Already accepted asynchronous results commit an outbox entry with controller state, then append the event. A crash between append and outbox removal replays by event ID without duplication. If completion was committed but audit/outbox cleanup failed, the operation may have happened: inspect/replay its original request ID and revision, rather than blindly submitting a new request. A BEGIN without an END means the result needs investigation. Audit failures do not terminate independent replication workers. Management requests are blocked while process probes can remain healthy. Repair private volume capacity/permissions; restore coherent backups for chain corruption or identity mismatch. Never erase audit files to bypass verification. Retention auditMaxEvents defaults to 1000000, range 1000–10000000. Set it in Linux/Docker platform YAML, Helm --set platform.auditMaxEvents=2000000 , or the native ConfigMap, followed by a controlled restart. The UI/API expose the limit and pruning anchor. Each new-event transaction prunes the old prefix while retaining anchorSequence/anchorHash ; the remaining history never pretends to start at zero. This count is not a physical disk byte quota: monitor H2/backup storage. Status polling also generates events; choose retention from measured request volume. Pages use fixed after/through bounds, oldest first, 100 by default, maximum 1000. after=0 selects the current retained beginning; through=0 fixes the current head. Continue with next and the same through . A cursor overtaken by retention receives 409 AUDIT HISTORY EXPIRED , never silent data omission; invalid rollback/range changes receive409 AUDIT HISTORY CHANGED . Console and exports ADMIN opens Security audit , reviews sequence/time/identity/route/task/result and uses Next page . Refresh retained window starts a new window. Export this page downloads only the current 100 events and proofs, not all history; changed boundaries prevent download. Close/sign-out clears records and fences late responses. For a full streaming export, use a management machine with Python 3 and an environment-supplied ADMIN token: The full exporter fixes one tail, verifies sequence/chain/store identity/tail hash page by page, streams to a 0600 file, writes COMPLETE, then publishes the final filename. Memory is bounded by page size. Existing outputs are never overwritten and HTTP redirects are refused. Failures/expired retention leave .partial , without a successful final file; export to a new path. Events generated during export lie beyond its fixed tail. Successful single-page verification with non-null continuation proves that page, not full-history completeness. API - GET /api/audit?after=0&through=0&limit=100 : ADMIN pages, events/next/storeId and integrity boundaries. - GET /api/audit/export?... : same range/permissions with JSON attachment headers; the streaming tool continues through this endpoint. Only those three nonnegative integer query parameters are accepted; limit is 1–1000. Reads/exports themselves are audited. Security and acceptance boundaries The local chain/registry detects ordinary corruption, missing rows and new empty-store replacement. It cannot resist an administrator rewriting all files/recomputing the chain or coherently rolling back every backup. External immutable/signature anchors, cross-controller aggregation, account management and its audit remain required work; exact task grants are documented in the authorization handbook. Keep exported tails/hashes in independent controlled custody. This is not an external immutable compliance audit service. See validation for tested profiles. Local account changes record ACCOUNT COMMITTED with subjectId and directory version; the UI shows the affected task/account. Directory mutation and audit outbox are saved together, with a separate durable version anchor unaffected by event retention. Legacy export payload/hash bytes are preserved; see accounts. External immutable anchoring remains pending.

title: Shared access
text: Shared accounts, sessions and audit 中文：共享身份. Contract. Acceptance follows implementation status and candidate evidence. Explicitly set cluster.sharedAccess: true in the registry configuration. All endpoints then use one SQL account/session/new-audit authority. Stop old registry members gracefully before the first switch; expiry alone does not prove an old endpoint stopped. Control protocol1 upgrades to2 and rejects registry-only members. All members must enable shared identity. Old memory cookies require one new login; established SQL sessions survive restarts. Task pages/actions remain LOCAL until CP-02/03 connects global task/command authority; route task requests to their owning endpoint meanwhile. Bootstrap imports the selected node's verified managed directory or seeds from configured accounts. Existing shared grants are never overwritten by stale deployment tokens. Start the chosen import node first when migrating existing managed identities. Imported non-administrator accounts are restricted to the importing node to preserve their prior local access. The account editor exposes “All nodes” and selected node IDs; an empty selection grants no node access. Administrators can explicitly expand access after reviewing task-ID collisions. API nodeIds: null means all nodes, an array limits nodes, and an omitted field on update preserves the prior grant. Administrator accounts always cover all nodes. Conflicting independent managed directories are not automatically merged; review/export identities and grants before planning adoption. Back up coordinated local control/accounts/audit/configuration/reports and SQL metadata before migration. Local controller state becomes format3 and binds clusterId/shared-store identity. Old software, disabling sharedAccess and missing/wrong authority refuse startup rather than restoring stale local grants. This is the control-state format, not task formatVersion. Rollback requires coordinated backups and review of revoked credentials, not merely an old JAR. Pre-import local audit history retains its original chain/payload. The shared chain records its storeId/last-sequence/hash anchor. New HTTP/account/task-outbox events enter the shared chain; endpoints see the same storeId. pendingOperations currently counts only the responding endpoint local outbox; other nodes pending diagnostics remain future work. Local outboxes drain only after shared confirmation; duplicate IDs are idempotent and payload collisions are rejected. A login at A resumes at B and survives A shutdown/kill/restart. Logout revokes its session globally. Any directory mutation atomically updates revision, revokes all old sessions and writes account audit. Audit failure rolls the transaction back. Every authentication/grant check reads the SQL identity/policy/content marker and audit anchor; matching immutable verified payloads may be reused without offline authentication fallback; outages return503 without local/memory fallback. Session creation checks current revision and expiry uses database time. Bearer and HTTPS/Origin/CSRF rules remain in browser sessions. Members must agree on enabled/Secure/remember policy, idle/absolute expiry, session capacity and audit retention. publicOrigin can differ by direct endpoint; a common HTTPS frontend uses the same external origin. Limits:200accounts,10000task grants per account and4MiB serialized directory. Capacity rejects a change without changing prior state. Sessions share one global maximum. Audit uses auditMaxEvents; non-HTTP idempotency receipts are retained separately without automatic cleanup yet, so monitor disk growth. Retention governance remains LG-09. Worker JVMs receive essential OS variables and explicitly referenced task variables. Unreferenced parent variables/JAVA TOOL OPTIONS and management/control-store credential variables are withheld; referencing protected names returns WORKER ENVIRONMENT DENIED. Use task-specific source/target/journal settings and explicit approved TLS/Kerberos driver configuration. Workers remain trusted SDK processes under the installation user; filesystem isolation, dedicated containers/Vault and finer task-secret distribution remain CP-05 work. Deployment: enable the field in platform-cluster.yml, keeping independent local directories. Helm has values-shared-access.yaml; native YAML has shared-a / shared-b. Supply dedicated store credentials through Secret. Live Kubernetes/CSI/controller HA remain separate acceptance. Recovery and FAQ - Lost all admin tokens: stop one local controller and use the existing access-recover command with a protected configured ADMIN seed. Shared mode updates SQL authority, revokes sessions and audits recovery atomically. Verify and rotate temporary credentials. - SHARED ACCESS QUIESCENCE REQUIRED: stop all old members gracefully; STALE is not confirmed stopped. If isolation is uncertain, plan/verify it before switching, without editing STOPPED records directly. - SHARED ACCESS REQUIRED: restore the bound cluster/sharedAccess configuration; disabling it cannot revive old local tokens. - SHARED ACCESS STATE REQUIRED/IDENTITY CHANGED: restore matching SQL identity/backup/connection settings. Missing authority is never reseeded from stale configuration; do not delete local bindings. - SHARED ACCESS DIRECTORY CONFLICT: back up/export/review the independent directories before adoption/merge; privileges are not silently expanded. - SHARED ACCESS POLICY MISMATCH: align expiry/cookie/capacity/audit settings across members. - ACCOUNT DIRECTORY CAPACITY: review account/grant volume; rejected changes preserve prior state. - Recovery still shows login: check real expiry/logout/directory revocation. Valid shared sessions recover without the failed controller's memory. - Different local/shared audit sequence: they are separate store chains linked by migration anchors/event IDs. Never rewrite/concatenate historical payloads as one chain. - Can old backups restore revoked access: a consistent old backup can contain old grants. External immutable rollback detection remains unfinished; review revocation/rotation after restore.

title: Task authorization
text: Per-task authorization 中文：按任务授权. Complete example: platform-task-scopes.yml. Roles determine actions. users[].taskIds limits the tasks visible/operable by VIEWER and OPERATOR. IDs match exactly: no wildcard, prefix, database or destination-schema matching. Grants may name tasks not loaded yet. - Omitted taskIds , including older configurations, preserves deployment-wide task access, including future tasks. An explicit empty list grants no tasks. Supply the list when access must be restricted. - VIEWER reads; OPERATOR checks/starts/stops/pauses/resumes granted tasks. Neither can create/import, read/edit configuration or read global audit. - ADMIN is deployment-wide and cannot configure taskIds ; global management endpoints are not task-scoped. Keep at least one ADMIN. The compatible authToken is also a global administrator. - Duplicates, wildcards, paths and invalid IDs are rejected. At most 10000 exact grants are accepted; this does not raise the platform task-loading limit. GET /api/tasks returns only granted tasks; UI counts use that filtered list. Scoped accounts do not receive invalid-file listings, since unloaded files cannot reliably be attributed. ADMIN still diagnoses them. Unauthorized and nonexistent task routes both return 404 TASK NOT FOUND . Rejection precedes body parsing, revision changes and actions. A role-forbidden endpoint, such as OPERATOR configuration/audit reads, still returns 403. GET /api/session returns this account's taskScope : an array is exact grants, null is unrestricted. The console shows a grant count and IDs in the identity tooltip. An account without loaded granted tasks gets a dedicated empty-state explanation. Sign-out clears grant/task data. Server checks enforce access independently of the UI. Deployment and revocation Linux/Docker use the configuration above with environment-supplied tokens. HTTP startup takes an immutable snapshot of grants, roles and token digests. Editing the file/Secret does not affect a running service; perform a controlled controller restart. New grants then apply without resetting replication checkpoints. Every request checks the current snapshot; an old request ID does not bypass revoked access. Helm uses deploy/helm/rivomesh/values-task-scopes.yaml with the existing RBAC Secret references. Manual Kubernetes uses deploy/kubernetes/rivomesh-task-scopes.yaml . Choose this instead of default/RBAC manifests, not as extra copies of the same resources. Custom auth.users[].taskIds is an array; empty grants render as [] . Native YAML comes from the same Chart. Restart under an operational plan after changes. Live Kubernetes/CSI acceptance remains pending. Denials enter the global audit for ADMIN review. Local account/grant UI is implemented; see accounts. OIDC/SSO, groups and individual-action grants remain unfinished; private configuration is still administrator-managed. This protects console task access, not database accounts, OS files or cross-deployment tokens, and does not establish multi-replica controller scheduling. Default CONFIG retains startup snapshots. Explicit managed activation makes the durable directory authoritative; restart does not resurrect configured tokens. Changes affect subsequent requests; accepted async operations may continue.

title: Validation records
text: Validation and recovery evidence Updated 2026-11-15. 中文：故障与恢复验证. Counts below are test executions, including repeated regressions , not counts of distinct scenarios. An implemented protocol or Java 8 bytecode does not establish acceptance on every product version, security profile or JDK. OceanBase experimental adapter: full recovery NOT accepted (2026-11-15) Evidence and retained failures: candidate9a087 passed118Java/SDK unit/API tests,116app tests separately against the actual fat JAR, and31DOM checks. Native strong reads, cross-database rollback, ownership/epochs, snapshots/types and partial CDC passed. Four complete mixed attempts still failed administrative-DDL timeout, tenant initialization or OBD resource admission. These are not accepted full recovery; the catalog remains EXPERIMENTAL. Artifact differences, resource probes and all failures are retained for further investigation. Actual release11667063 passed native restart/older-backup guards and new EMPTY/NO BACKSLASH ESCAPES quoted/backslash table, Unicode/emoji snapshot/CDC/session-reconstruction cases. Unit coverage verifies malformed UTF-16 is a deterministic pause. Current release9a087 additionally passed the actual MySQL8.4.13→PG17.12+Doris4.1.3 mixed recovery case; its14Doris adapter classes match the native-mode/old-backup release11667063. Artifact and scope distinctions are retained. Doris native and mixed recovery (2026-11-15) Archived evidence:2 SDK +114 app tests and30 DOM checks passed; the final fat JAR separately passed114 app cases, not additional distinct tests. Final native MoW/index/PK/keyless/precision/restart and older nonempty FE+BE backup refusal passed. Actual MySQL8.4→PG17.12+Doris4.1.3 passed snapshot/CDC, independent target outage/automatic catch-up, worker kill, SQL repair/retry, missing-view isolation and honest pause fences. Comparing all65114 classes with the mixed-case release found only capability text changed; runtime resources match. Clusters/TLS/all JDKs/capacity/adoption/live DDL remain outside this acceptance. Exact task grants and final release (2026-11-15) Archived evidence: Maven passed2 SDK plus99 app tests; the exact final fat JAR separately passed all99 app tests. Repeated executions are not additional distinct cases.29 DOM checks and three Helm/native profile checks passed. Actual Java8 loads a platform file and verifies exact/empty grants, filtered listings, denied direct actions and grants after SIGKILL/restart; this management fixture uses a stub DB backend. The same final release separately passed actual MySQL8.4→PG17.12 configuration rotation/restore/restart CDC, with146 independently verified audit events. Account editing UI, live K8s and external immutable audit remain outside this acceptance. Global security audit (2026-11-15) Archived evidence:98 Java/SDK unit/API,28 DOM and7 exporter checks passed. The same release passed Java8 actual HTTP/H2, native hash verification across exported pages, committed-event persistence after SIGKILL, and deleted-store startup refusal; the independent management fixture uses a stub DB backend. Actual MySQL8.4→PG17.12 credential/config restore/restart CDC also passed, with132 independently verified audit events. Helm/native parity is static acceptance, not live K8s or external immutable auditing. Configuration editing: final-release acceptance (2026-11-15) Archived evidence: 88 Java/SDK unit/API and25 DOM checks passed. The exact final release passed actual MySQL8.4→PostgreSQL17.12 stopped target-password rotation, failed old-credential CHECK, idempotent update, revision restore and controller restart with deleted projections, retaining original stream/snapshot identities. This does not establish visual/browser acceptance, all targets/source account DDL, or complete security auditing. Current accepted profiles Profile Evidence Boundary --- --- --- V2 MySQL 8.0.46 / 8.4.13 → openGauss 7.0.0-RC3 target/platform-matrix-final.log , 44 executions, no failures/errors/skips Includes async promotion, MGR election and platform recovery; commercial distributed GaussDB is not covered MySQL 5.7.44 target/mysql57-base.log , 28 executions Basic snapshot/JSON/CDC/restart; full 5.7 HA matrix remains pending PostgreSQL 17.12 target target/sink-postgres.log , 37 executions Snapshot, transactional data/checkpoint, JSON and restart; other versions need acceptance V3 SQL fan-out, LOCAL/EXTERNAL journals target/v3-final-after-keeper.log , 53 executions Separate MySQL 8.4, PostgreSQL 17 and openGauss 7 targets; HTTP controls and ownership V3 async MySQL failover target/v3-ha-fixed.log Two workers, primary death, externally promoted replica, GTID dependencies and unhealthy SQL-thread rejection V3 three-node MGR target/v3-group.log Primary dies during an unfinished MVCC snapshot; new election, snapshot rebase and catch-up Independent SQL target delivery target/v3-cooperative-stop.log , 31 executions A locked Gauss checkpoint does not prevent PG/MySQL receiving changes within five seconds Journal quota and recovery target/v3-backpressure-recovery-fixed.log , 40 executions Low-quota backpressure, reserved normalization workspace, heartbeat, shared pause, oversized transaction refusal, expansion/replay SQL + four message targets target/messaging-redis-safe-reconnect.log , 42 executions Actual executable JAR, MySQL → PostgreSQL + Kafka 3.9.2 / RabbitMQ 4.1.4 / NATS 2.11.8 / Redis 7.4.2; worker kill and three consecutive broker restart rounds Retry diagnostics target/retry-status-unit.log , 35 executions; target/ui-retry-status.log , 10 DOM tests Automatic retries stay RUNNING with a diagnostic code; no checkpoint/generation change or manual Resume action CLI LOCAL keeper + retry status target/v3-local-keeper-retry-status.log , 43 executions Both journal modes, three actual SQL targets, real HTTP controls and LOCAL pause/restart transitions Redis acceptance additionally injects connection replacement between XADD and WAITAOF, insufficient replica fsyncs, handshake EOF, unsafe AOF/eviction settings, deleted streams and a disconnected non-default database. Confirmations never lead publication receipts; replay retains event IDs. Socket reopening cannot silently write into database 0. Sentinel, Cluster, replica promotion, TLS and power-loss acceptance remain pending. Kafka/RabbitMQ/NATS/Redis tests use single-node broker profiles. Replica parameters, SASL/TLS configuration and hostname verification code do not substitute for real authenticated/cluster failure tests. Pulsar 4.0.14 transport and mixed-pipeline recovery now passed the separately recorded profiles below. RocketMQ initial native single-broker transport acceptance passed; mixed pipeline snapshot/CDC, worker kill and three broker restart rounds passed. Artemis Core has a separately recorded independent transport profile; seven-message-product mixed recovery has not passed. ActiveMQ Classic remains unfinished. The later target/messaging-visible-retry-recovery.log passed 45 executions. Each of three rounds actually stops all four brokers, verifies PostgreSQL continues while every message destination persistently reports automatic retry without PAUSED, starts the brokers, and verifies catch-up plus automatic diagnostic clearing. Workers execute the release JAR; recovery requires no manual Resume. Pulsar transport acceptance passed in target/pulsar-transport-java25-shading.log : the actual shaded artifact coexists with core dependencies, validates ownership/policies, publishes/reads, survives a broker restart and refuses missing initialized resources. target/messaging-pulsar-ready-recovery.log then passed 47 executions , actual release JAR with a 256 MiB worker heap, PostgreSQL plus five message destinations, worker kill, snapshot/keyless/generated values and three deterministic stop/start rounds. Broker readiness is awaited separately (up to 180 seconds); the subsequent catch-up bound stays 60 seconds. That is test orchestration, not a hardware-independent recovery SLO. The earlier target/messaging-pulsar-mixed-first.log failed while the Pulsar admin service was still starting at the test deadline. It is not counted as a pass. Safe typed retries retained the original receipt, and other targets caught up. target/pulsar-transport-first.log failed a compile-time ambiguous SDK type import; target/pulsar-transport-shaded.log failed because old Shade 3.5.1 could not parse the dependency's Java 25 multi-release classes. Shade 3.6.2 fixes packaging while retaining a Java 8 build baseline. These packaging checks are not an actual Java 25 runtime acceptance matrix. Latest DOM tests: 11 pass in target/ui-pulsar-copies.log . Verified behavior - Atomic source transaction/capture positions, independent subscriber ACKs, content receipts, epoch fencing, checksums and gap refusal on H2/MySQL/PostgreSQL-family journals. - Snapshot baseline/manifests/parts, complete-artifact reuse, incomplete MVCC rebase, per-table target confirmations and artifact GC only after every subscriber confirms. - Cross-database source transactions; keyless duplicate occurrences, one-occurrence updates/deletes and persisted normalization reused by slow targets. - Lossless unsigned/decimal/JSON values, SQL NULL versus JSON null, empty text/bytes, DATE/microseconds, logged STORED generation and supported historical VIRTUAL evaluation. - Data/checkpoint atomicity, whole-transaction rollback, primary-key updates, target ownership, protected identity constraints and business UNIQUE conversion. - Source-primary shutdown and external promotion, MGR majority election, SQL-thread 1032 failure rejection, retained GTIDs and fail-closed purged/missing history. The service does not promote database nodes or rewrite GTIDs. - Target SQL/permission failures pause only that target. Stale Resume generations cannot clear newer failures. Temporary failures retry and retain their original transaction/checkpoint. - Low-quota backpressure leaves unpersisted GTIDs unchanged while delivery/GC/heartbeats continue; workspace reservation prevents raw backlog from blocking its own normalization. - Mandatory-return/negative or lost message confirmation does not advance publication receipts. Broker and journal are separate transactions, so duplicates are possible and consumers must stage/deduplicate/commit their own checkpoints. - Shared pause persists before target fencing. SQL fences can be confirmed; in-flight broker requests remain explicitly unconfirmed and cannot be retracted by a journal epoch. Console, packaging and deployment The bilingual wizard, masking, token handling, task creation without automatic start, SQL/MQ mappings, version-bound recovery, retry status and source-versus-target snapshot progress have DOM tests. Real HTTP tests cover authentication, origin rejection, bounded task resources, request deduplication, revision conflicts, corrupted configuration/state refusal, private snapshots and redacted status. The environment has no usable automated browser window; screenshot, keyboard and visual accessibility acceptance are not claimed. The executable JAR has been tested as the worker artifact, with Java 8 entry bytecode and the relocated Gauss driver. Container acceptance previously verified non-root UID 10001, health endpoints, authentication, static assets, private configuration and volume restart. Helm lint/render, native-manifest parity, existing PVC and invalid configuration checks passed in target/deployment-after-messaging.log . A live Kubernetes/CSI deployment, full upgrade/soak tests and Java 11/17/21/25 runtime matrices remain required. Tests create and remove only their own Compose projects. RESET, primary shutdown and test-data repairs apply only to isolated fixtures. Reproduction entry points include tests/matrix.sh , tests/v3-run.sh , tests/v3-ha-run.sh , tests/v3-group-run.sh , tests/messaging-run.sh and tests/ui ( npm test ). Scripts execute sequential Maven builds against shared output directories. Failed runs and limits Failed logs are retained and are not counted as passes. Early H2 concurrent shutdown tests preceded cooperative stop/controller keepers. target/v3-backpressure-recovery.log exposed connect-time EOF during H2 handoff; bounded connection-open retry fixed that path. target/v3-retry-status.log exposed CLI automatic-server churn across PAUSED loops; a keeper spanning those loops is verified by the later 43-execution run. target/messaging-redis-first.log and target/messaging-redis-repeated-recovery.log exposed an unclassified Redis constructor connection failure. The constructor now uses typed retry classification. Later intermediate runs also exposed unguarded test-reader network calls during startup; those readers now retry only known connection/metadata transients. target/messaging-redis-safe-reconnect.log is the passing three-round acceptance. Commercial distributed GaussDB, other vendor/analytics targets, complete live DDL, populated-target adoption, manual repair/skip, migration cutover/failback and full RBAC are unfinished. Async replication can permanently lose transactions before promotion; CDC cannot reconstruct such losses, forged GTIDs or source writes never recorded in binlog. Use the runtime manual and message recovery contract for operational boundaries. title: 恢复与一致性
text: 恢复、主库切换与一致性 本文描述 v2 单 database、单目标核心 ，不是 v3 快照和独立日志协议。English: V2 recovery。已实现的 v3 多库多目标、可选日志、Web 和消息恢复见 V3 手册 与消息手册。完整设计见 完整平台方案（English）。已确认的多库显式映射、同源多目标及独立恢复设计见 需求与决策（English）； 业务次级 UNIQUE/GSI 转普通索引及接管约束恢复见 Gauss 索引策略（English）。剩余适配器、修复和接管范围见实施状态。 同步服务主备 各进程首次启动幂等创建 v2 元数据；并发目录对象创建冲突单独处理，首个任务的配置和表清单原子插入。 工作前通过条件 UPDATE 获取 owner 和租约。独立心跳线程持续续期，数据/进度事务也校验同一 owner。 每次重新建立工作会话都生成新 owner，防止旧复制连接的回调在新会话中继续提交。 同一任务行的锁将采集、全量提交和增量应用的提交顺序串行化。 租约转移后，旧 owner 的业务事务在任何业务写入前就被拒绝；旧节点也不能替新 owner 暂停任务或释放租约。 节点只是备用时不会连接 binlog，同一任务正常只有一个复制客户端。 GTID 状态 - capture gtid：已经进入持久化队列或不影响业务库的已提交源事务，加上首次基线。 - required gtid：capture gtid 与全量扫描已读取状态所依赖的 GTID 的并集。 - applied sequence：已经写入目标业务表的队列事务序号。 源的物理 UUID 和文件位点只用于诊断、连接后端校验，不用于跨服务器恢复定位。 每个源提交事件先完整持久化，才把该事务 GTID 加入 capture gtid；不使用客户端可能提前更新的内存 GTID 直接覆盖状态。 重复 GTID 在持有任务锁时检查，已经持久化的事务不会重复加入队列。 全量期间也允许安全切主 记录基线 B0 后开始采集 FULL 行镜像，并按主键游标扫描业务表。 每次分块读取之后获取源 GTID 水位；分块数据、最后主键和该依赖水位一起提交到目标。 表发现和初始扫描上界读取的结束水位也保存为初始 required gtid。 若全量读取到了旧主库已提交、但采集器尚未持久化的事务，仅检查 capture gtid 会遗漏这一依赖。 因此切换候选必须包含 required gtid，不能只包含已采集事件。 所有分块完成后取结束 GTID B1，等待 capture gtid 覆盖 B1，再按源提交顺序回放队列。 对 B0 后没有变化的记录，扫描负责导入；有变化的记录，由最后一条完整行镜像或 DELETE 决定最终状态。 主键修改按删除旧键、写入新键处理，游标之前的插入及扫描上界之后的记录也由日志补齐。 全量和早期回放期间目标不是某一个时间点的一致性快照。持续增量阶段，每个源事务（包括跨表）在一个目标事务中应用。 主库发现与切换 1. 逐个检查候选地址，读取 UUID、server id、只读标记、GTID 模式、executed/purged 集合及复制状态。 2. 普通主从仅选择可写且没有活动上游线程或残留复制错误的节点。 3. Group Replication 仅选择 ONLINE、PRIMARY、可写、单主模式的节点。 4. 多个可写主库时等待外部高可用系统完成隔离，不能任选一个节点。 5. 要求 required gtid ⊆ candidate.gtid executed ；不满足则等待追平。 6. 要求 candidate.gtid purged ⊆ capture gtid ；不满足说明还有未采集的必要事务已无日志，任务暂停。 7. 新建复制连接使用持久化 GTID auto-positioning，禁用自动回退到 purged 集合。 JDBC 查询会校验物理 UUID 和可写性；复制连接在处理事件前校验握手查询到的 server id。 这也能发现 Router/VIP 在两种连接之间切换了后端，届时退出本次会话，重新发现而不混用数据。 心跳超时、源连接断开和源角色变化会触发新会话，重新读取持久化 GTID。 候选需要由运维保证全量复制、没有业务数据过滤或伪造 GTID，属于同一逻辑复制拓扑。 GTID 一致不等于能检测所有人工修改数据的情况。数据库自身丢失的异步未复制事务，不能由 CDC 重建。 提交边界 操作 一个目标事务内的内容 --- --- 创建任务 配置指纹、B0、表清单、扫描上界、发现水位 全量分块 业务行、游标、行数、完成状态、读取依赖 GTID 捕获源事务 有序完整行事件、来源、GTID、capture/required 集合 应用源事务 全部行修改、applied sequence、阶段变更、队列删除 记录故障 错误历史、共享 run state、最近错误上下文、释放 owner 提交响应不确定时退出本次会话，不复用旧内存游标或 GTID；新会话读取目标数据库的持久化记录。 数据表、队列和状态表必须作为同一个恢复单元备份和恢复。 SQL 错误与暂停 SQLState 08/40、锁等待和可恢复资源错误退避重试；数据、约束、权限和语法错误暂停。 错误记录保留表、源 GTID、队列事务序号、SQLState 和 vendor code，不记录行载荷或 SQL 字面量。 目标事务失败整体回滚，队列头不删除；采集端可能已把其他事务安全存入队列，这不会使应用越过错误。 PAUSED 是数据库中的共享状态，重启进程或新增备用节点不会绕过它。 修复数据类型、权限或约束后执行 resume，只重试原事务，不跳过、更改 GTID 或清空队列。 源复制 SQL 错误由数据库运维修复；服务不会自动执行 SQL SLAVE SKIP COUNTER、注入空 GTID 或 RESET。 正常主库可用时，故障从库不影响当前采集；故障从库被提升时会拒绝其接管，等待修复。 v1 文件位点任务缺少完整 GTID 和读取依赖，不能直接自动升级；新版本会保留旧状态并明确拒绝同名旧任务。

title: Acceptance matrix
text: SDD acceptance matrix RM-SDD-001 · 2026-11-16 These contracts track implementation acceptance. CP-01 and SE-01/02/03/04/05 accepted; CP-05 is partial and remaining scope stays open. Given a supported profile/authorization,when normal,error or interrupted operations occur,the outcomes below must hold. Include positive,refusal,duplicate and relevant restart/failover scenarios. PASS AC-CP-02 CP-02 A task created/edited through A appears at B with the same global revision;IDs are unique within a cluster;independent sources remain isolated and standalone mode remains usable. PARTIAL · foundations AC-CP-03 CP-03 Any entry controls tasks on B;typed commands cover create/check/lifecycle/retry/validation/repair and carry request ID,revision and owner generation;duplicate delivery is idempotent and acceptance is distinct from execution. title: 验收矩阵
text: SDD验收矩阵 RM-SDD-001 · 2026-11-16 这些合同持续追踪验收状态。CP-01及SE-01/02/03/04/05已验收；CP-05部分完成，其余范围仍待验收。Given=满足规格中的受支持档案及权限；When=执行对应正常、错误或中断操作；Then=满足下列可观察结果。每项至少包含正常、拒绝、重复请求及相关重启/切换场景。 ID 需求 验收合同 证据状态 --- --- --- --- AC-CP-01 CP-01 部署两个节点后，任一管理入口均显示相同节点ID、角色、版本/JDK/架构、容量、心跳时间和任务归属；失联显示过期/未知，不能伪装成健康。 PASS AC-CP-02 CP-02 同一集群中从A创建/修改任务后B读到同一全局修订；全局taskId唯一，独立任务与源配置仍隔离；单机模式保留可运行配置。 PARTIAL · foundations AC-CP-03 CP-03 任一入口可控制B的任务：创建、检查、启停、暂停/恢复、重试、校验/修复；命令含全局请求ID/修订/owner代次，重复投递只生效一次，202仅表示接受，返回已执行/拒绝/未知结果。 PARTIAL · foundations AC-CP-04 CP-04 节点断电/网络分区/旧节点恢复时同一任务无双写；未确认停机可标记未知并隔离；按JDK、连接器、存储可达性和配额调度；排空迁移保留断点。 待验收 AC-CP-05 CP-05 从A撤销权限后B拒绝新命令；同一远端操作可按请求ID/任务/节点/计划追踪；界面不返回密钥，节点仅获得授权任务必需的密钥引用。 PARTIAL · shared-access AC-CP-06 CP-06 界面按节点/任务/目标过滤状态、延迟、积压、日志和错误；注明采集时间及失联范围；远端日志分页/限流且不泄露业务值或凭据。 待验收 AC-CP-07 CP-07 管理实例故障后其他入口可继续查询/控制；接收但未完成的命令可恢复；按明确策略已有Worker可继续安全同步；仅部署多个replica或共享目录不能算通过。 DONE · separated profile AC-SE-01 SE-01 登录后刷新、重新打开同一站点页面可恢复未过期会话和原权限，不需再次输入令牌；过期则回到登录页且不误发操作。 通过：单控制器 AC-SE-02 SE-02 可配置空闲/绝对有效期；退出、账号停用、令牌轮换或权限撤销按策略失效；多标签页一致；浏览器关闭后的持久记住登录为单独可配置策略。 通过：单控制器 AC-SE-03 SE-03
