title: Installation and sign-in
text: Install and sign in Build from the core repository using Java 8/Maven, or build its Docker Compose image locally. The current version is a source-built pre-release; no public container image is assumed. Source and deployment commands · Quick start Prepare the environment Use a reachable MySQL source with GTID, ROW logging and FULL row images, an independent empty target, persistent storage, and database accounts with the privileges required by the pipeline manual. Snapshot initialization requires a brief global read lock and appropriate permissions. Start the console Run the documented commands from the quick start. Open http://127.0.0.1:8080 and sign in with your own RIVOMESH TOKEN . Default local settings are for loopback access. Configure HTTPS, Cookie and Origin policies before remote use. Docker Compose builds from source. Use addresses reachable from the container, and retain the named data volume. Docker Desktop can reach host services through host.docker.internal when appropriate. Before sharing the installation 1. Provide an HTTPS entry point and assign individual accounts. 2. Persist task, controller, journal, configuration and report directories. 3. Verify inserts, updates, deletes and restart recovery on a small test pipeline. 4. For several nodes, read multi-node deployment before sharing any storage. Create a task · Deployment reference · Browser sessions

title: Create a synchronization task
text: Create your first synchronization task This walkthrough uses MySQL → PostgreSQL , a small source and an independent empty target. Additional destinations have their own connector profiles. Prepare connection details For MySQL, collect host, port, databases, credentials and a unique replication client serverId . It must differ from database node IDs and other replication clients. For the target, collect host, port, database/schema, credentials and the intended source-to-target mappings. The source must meet snapshot and replication requirements. Target business tables must be empty and exclusively written by this task. Configure and check 1. Choose Create task and keep the default multi-database, multi-target format. 2. Assign stable task and logical source identities, then enter MySQL details. 3. Add one PostgreSQL target and explicit mappings for each source database. 4. Select a persistent journal. Local storage is suitable for same-host trials; cross-host continuation requires the external journal profile. 5. Save, check connections and objects, then start. A check does not validate every runtime or snapshot privilege. A saved task remains stopped until started. In optional global mode, choose the actual execution node; an accepted command is not evidence that execution has finished. See global control. Validate the first run Watch snapshot, catch-up and target delivery. Insert, update and delete a test row and compare actual destination values. Restart the worker and confirm it continues from its persisted state. Keep task identity, journals and target state for recovery. Monitoring · Troubleshooting · Pipeline reference

title: Progress and daily operations
text: Read progress and operate tasks Check both the synchronization phase and each target's confirmed position. A running process does not mean all destinations are caught up. State Meaning --- --- Snapshot Existing data is being read/prepared or delivered; target data may be incomplete Streaming Incremental changes are being handled; lag can still exist Target paused Inspect that target's error and repair the cause before retrying Shared pipeline paused Standby claims are blocked; inspect target isolation confirmation Local worker stopped Only this machine's process is stopped; inspect shared state separately UNKNOWN in global mode The owner or reliable receipt is unavailable; do not infer success or a stopped process Daily checks Watch phase, backlog trends, per-target acknowledgements, SQL errors, connectivity, disk space and source binlog retention. The slowest destination determines retained journal history; a healthy fast target cannot free another target's unacknowledged events. Stop, pause or recover - Stop local worker stops only the local process. - Pause shared pipeline blocks ordinary standby claims; unreachable targets still need isolation verification. - Resume this target retries that target's original transaction after its error is fixed. - Resume after repair handles the pipeline-level error; it does not silently clear independent target pauses. Optional fixed-owner global mode routes commands to the execution owner. HTTP 202 means accepted, not finished; inspect the original command receipt. An offline STOP waits until the original owner can recover it. Administrators can review configuration history and restore versions according to identity/state restrictions. Configuration revisions · Global control · Backup

title: Troubleshooting
text: Troubleshoot a synchronization task Preserve the error, task identity and persisted state. Fix the cause before retrying; do not reset GTID, checkpoints or queues to bypass an error. Symptom First checks --- --- Console unavailable Service startup logs, bind/port, token/session configuration, HTTPS proxy Source connection fails Container/network address, credentials, GTID, replication privileges and required logs Target SQL pause Exact SQL error, privileges, type mapping, table structure and target identity Backlog grows Slowest target, independent target errors, journal quota and disk headroom Source waits after failover Candidate topology, writable role, required executed/purged GTID history Global command pending/unknown Original request receipt, owner availability, control database and matching private directory/key Temporary connectivity, locking and serialization errors may retry under policy. Deterministic SQL/type/DDL errors need intervention. Recovery retries the original transaction; it does not skip records. If logs or state are lost, restore a coordinated backup or create an explicit rebuild plan. Never delete controller or journal state and reuse a nonempty target as if it were a new task. Recovery rules · Backup and restore · Global control · Report an issue

title: Validate data and review repairs
text: Validate data and review repairs Progress describes how far replication has advanced. Validation compares actual source and target content at a historical common checkpoint; a report does not assert permanent equality afterward. Initial managed row validation and repair acceptance covers MySQL 8.4 / PostgreSQL 17 business targets. Other relational profiles need separate verification. Messaging and analytical targets do not use this workflow. Create a validation report 1. Finish initialization, run the task and allow the chosen target to catch up. 2. An administrator starts row validation from task details, selecting the target and lock/read/staging budgets. 3. Inspect the operation and completed report for source/target row counts, missing, extra and changed rows. 4. Review task state and explicitly resume when appropriate. Validation does not repair data automatically. Establishing the common checkpoint briefly affects source writes. Raw values may contain sensitive business data and require the appropriate permissions. Review and execute a repair Keep the task paused, explicitly select targets/tables, generate a plan, and review its scope and budget before execution. Check per-table results and explicitly resume after completion. Unsupported foreign keys, triggers or dependencies can reject a repair. Canceling cannot roll back tables already committed. After an interrupted operation, recover the original request/report/plan and inspect committed results rather than assuming nothing happened. Optional global mode supports cross-entry workflows within its documented fixed-owner acceptance profile; it is not automatic owner migration. Managed validation · Managed repair · Global maintenance

title: Backup and recovery
text: Preserve state for recovery A recovery plan must retain task configuration and identity, journal events/checkpoints, target business and management state, and the controller's private data. Keep source binlogs long enough for the outage and catch-up window. Back up together - Controller state, account/audit data, configuration history, reports and task-specific keys. - Local journal directories or external journal storage, including snapshot artifacts and unacknowledged events. - Target business tables and their atomic checkpoint/receipt state. - Shared control database and original node directories/keys when shared or global mode is enabled. Choose a coordinated backup/restore plan. Restoring a checkpoint alone cannot reconstruct already removed events, and an old consistent backup can reintroduce old permissions that need review. Rehearse recovery Stop according to the operation plan, preserve directories/volumes, reopen the original identities and verify snapshot/CDC content and target acknowledgements. For global mode, inspect the original command/report receipt and restore the fixed owner's matching directory and key. An empty directory cannot impersonate that owner. Cross-host synchronization continuation uses the external journal profile. Source database promotion, worker journal ownership and global controller relocation are separate concerns. Explicit separated controller/Agent deployment has its own initial acceptance profile. Automatic owner relocation and the full HA matrix remain open. Multi-node guide · Pipeline journal requirements · Recovery reference

title: Accounts and permissions
text: Assign accounts and permissions Use individual identities and grant the least access needed for each role. Role Typical access --- --- VIEWER Read authorized task states and permitted report summaries OPERATOR Perform permitted daily operations within task/node grants ADMIN Manage accounts/configuration and administrative validation/repair workflows The API and UI enforce both roles and task/node scope. If a task or action is absent, inspect grants before changing data or state. Shared access With explicit shared-access configuration, nodes share account authority, sessions and audit. Account changes revoke old sessions. Cookie domains, HTTPS, Origin and session limits still apply across entry points. Optional shared-task mode additionally routes task commands to fixed owners. Shared login alone does not enable global task operations or controller HA. Account management · Task grants · Shared access · Security audit

title: Use cases and evaluation
text: Choose a representative evaluation Begin with a defined business scope and an independent test target, then preserve configuration and measured results for review. Cross-database and heterogeneous integration Replicate MySQL data to supported database targets with explicit database/schema mappings. Review text, NULL values, temporal precision, decimals, JSON, keyless duplicates, generated columns, indexes and constraints. Each product/mode has its own connector profile. Continuously updated analytics Deliver snapshots and changes to ClickHouse, Doris or Hive. Validate update/delete behavior, views and materialization before measuring latency under your workload. These targets do not all use transactional JDBC semantics. Multiple downstream systems Deliver one logical source to independently acknowledged targets. Rehearse a slow or failed destination and plan retained journal capacity. Message consumers must interpret snapshot/transaction boundaries and handle duplicates. Migration and parallel validation Populate an independent environment while preserving the original business database. Review actual values, object differences, restarts and recovery. Application SQL, write cutover, rollback and business constraints require their own plan. For openGauss, DM, KingbaseES, GBase 8c and OceanBase, use the domestic database adaptation guide. Managed row validation/repair has a MySQL/PostgreSQL acceptance profile; do not assume all domestic target profiles support the same maintenance workflow. Performance measurement · Multi-node evaluation · Compatibility boundaries

title: Frequently asked questions
text: Frequently asked questions Where should I start? Read the introduction, then use the quick start with a small MySQL source and an independent empty target. Database administrators should review logging, replication and snapshot privileges. What does V3 in the console mean? It identifies the task configuration format, formatVersion: 3 , for multi-database, multi-target tasks. It is not a database version or a development stage you need to learn. Keep the default for new tasks; changing the number does not migrate an old task's persisted state. Are other capture sources available? MySQL is implemented. PostgreSQL and Oracle sources are planned; the source adapter interface allows other database types to be added with independent log, snapshot and recovery acceptance. Support as a target does not imply source capture support. Can I start with a populated target? First-use target business tables must be empty. Nonempty takeover is a separate migration concern; RivoMesh does not silently clear or merge existing business data. Does recovery skip failed transactions? No. Fix the cause, then retry the original transaction. Reviewed data repair is a separate workflow with a documented target profile. Is global task control available? An optional fixed-owner global mode supports shared task views, durable commands, configuration and read-only queries. Default operation is local. An explicit separated controller/Agent profile has initial acceptance. Automatic owner relocation and the full HA matrix remain open. See multi-node deployment. Does this website collect database credentials? No. It is a static product/documentation site. Your actual console runs in your own deployment. Local search loads a static document index from this site. Feedback and contribution · Known limitations

title: Multi-node deployment
text: Multi-node deployment and recovery RivoMesh separates shared node observation, shared access and synchronization failover. Task operations are local by default. An optional fixed-owner global mode now supports shared task views, durable commands, configuration/history and read-only queries. Explicit controller/Agent separation has an accepted initial profile; automatic cross-Agent relocation and the full HA matrix remain open. Capability Current scope --- --- Node registry Administrators can inspect nodes, runtime versions, resources, leases and task observations through a shared control database Shared accounts, sessions and audit Explicit cluster.sharedAccess: true ; PostgreSQL 17 / MySQL 8.4 two-node acceptance records include cross-node revocation and restart recovery Synchronization failover Eligible standby workers use an external journal, matching logical task and target settings, distinct node IDs, leases and target fencing Global task control Optional fixed-owner mode is integrated into HTTP and the console, with cross-entry maintenance acceptance for MySQL/PostgreSQL targets; full migration, cancellation, fault and capacity profiles remain incomplete Each controller needs its own persistent control, task, configuration, key and report directories. Do not share controller.json , a controller directory or a PVC between controllers. Configure the shared control database with platform-cluster.yml, using a stable, unique node ID per node. The control database and external transaction journal have different responsibilities. A shared control database does not make local synchronization events available on another machine. Cross-host continuation requires the external journal profile in the pipeline manual. One task has one active owner, rather than being split across workers for parallel processing. For shared access, stop all old members normally before migration, back up local directories and the control database, initialize from the selected bootstrap node, review account/node permissions, and then start other nodes. Use consistent session/audit policies and HTTPS. Read the shared access manual before changing an existing installation. Stopping a local worker does not stop every standby. Pausing the shared pipeline prevents ordinary takeover; inspect target isolation results separately. A healthy heartbeat does not prove business synchronization is healthy, and an expired lease does not prove a process has stopped. Helm provides cluster values and shared-access values, with independent releases per node. Real Kubernetes/CSI, automatic cross-Agent relocation and additional HA profiles require separate acceptance. Node registry · Recovery · Global control progress Enable optional fixed-owner global mode In addition to shared access, set cluster.sharedTasks: true and configure the same protected 32-byte Base64 taskKey on all members. Each node needs a stable ID and its original independent persistent directory. See the global profile and global control manual. Initial activation requires task-free directories; old local tasks have no automatic import tool. HTTP 202 means accepted, not finished. An offline owner keeps a command pending/unknown until it provides a reliable receipt. This mode does not automatically move execution to another owner. Separate management and execution The explicit controller/Agent profile has acceptance records for PostgreSQL17/MySQL8.4 control storage, LOCAL/H2 journals, MySQL8.4 capture and PostgreSQL17/MySQL8.4 targets. Existing Workers continue in tested all-controller-loss scenarios; this does not relocate execution to another Agent. Default combined deployment remains coupled. See execution lifecycle for roles, upgrade conditions and exact evidence.

title: Domestic database adaptation
text: Domestic database adaptation RivoMesh can copy existing MySQL data and subsequent changes into an independent domestic database environment for Xinchuang adaptation, parallel validation and migration preparation. Target Current profile --- --- openGauss / GaussDB openGauss 7.0.0-RC3 partially verified; commercial/distributed GaussDB requires separate verification DM Experimental DM8 UTF8 profile with snapshot, CDC and recovery records Kingbase Experimental V9 PG/UTF8 profile with snapshot, CDC and recovery records GBase 8c Experimental PG/UTF8 profile; 8a and 8s remain separately planned OceanBase Experimental MySQL-mode tenant; full mixed recovery acceptance remains incomplete See the connector catalog for product manuals and exact boundaries. These are target adapters, not capture sources or vendor certification. Start with an empty target and representative business tables. Validate Chinese text, NULL/empty strings, temporal precision, decimal values, JSON, keyless duplicates, generated columns and index/constraint conversions. Rehearse outages and restart recovery. Application SQL compatibility, constraints, write cutover and rollback need their own plan. Managed row-level validation and repair currently have a MySQL/PostgreSQL acceptance profile. Source expansion MySQL is the implemented capture source. PostgreSQL and Oracle sources are planned and are not currently runnable. The source adapter interface allows additional database types to be added with their own snapshot, transaction-log and recovery-position semantics. Other products, including domestic database sources, require separate implementation and acceptance; no delivery date is promised. Multi-node deployment · Compatibility · Roadmap · Platform design

title: User guide
text: RivoMesh documentation RivoMesh is a Java-based database synchronization platform. It reads existing MySQL data and binlog changes, delivering them to databases, analytical systems and message brokers with a web console for task management. title: Introduction
text: What is RivoMesh? RivoMesh synchronizes existing MySQL data and subsequent inserts, updates and deletes to supported target systems. It combines snapshots, CDC, persistent journals, independent target acknowledgements and web task management. The implemented capture source is MySQL. Targets include relational databases, analytical systems and messaging systems. Availability depends on the exact product, version and profile; PostgreSQL as a target does not imply PostgreSQL source support. Start with a small test database and an independent empty target. Check actual values, incremental changes and restart recovery before expanding the scope. Quick start · Compatibility · Platform design

title: Quick start
text: Quick start Prepare Java 8, Maven, a MySQL test source and an independent empty PostgreSQL / openGauss target. MySQL needs GTID, ROW/FULL binlog settings and the replication/snapshot privileges described in the pipeline manual. Build the core project Start the console Open http://127.0.0.1:8080 and sign in with the token. Keep credentials out of URLs and Git. Production browser access requires the HTTPS/session deployment settings in the session manual. Create and verify a pipeline Use the default pipeline wizard to configure source identity, databases, an independent target, explicit mappings and a persistent journal. Save, check, and then start. Validate snapshot values, inserts, updates, deletes and Worker restart recovery. Targets require empty business tables on first use. The check operation does not validate every runtime privilege. Default recovery retries the original transaction; it does not skip failed data. Console and deployment · Multi-database pipelines

title: Compatibility
text: Compatibility and capability boundaries The connector catalog is generated from the source capability registry. AVAILABLE, PARTIALLY VERIFIED, EXPERIMENTAL and PLANNED are distinct states, not certification for every version or cluster. MySQL is the implemented capture source. PostgreSQL and Oracle source adapters remain tracked separately in SDD. Historical Java 8/11/17/21/25 SQL/session records do not cover the entire platform and every driver. Multiple targets acknowledge independently and do not form one distributed atomic transaction. Message delivery is confirmed at least once; consumers must handle duplicates according to the protocol. Unsupported DDL or types can block progress. First-use business targets must be empty and exclusively written by the service. Managed COMMON CUT repair has a limited MySQL/PostgreSQL acceptance profile. Shared node observation and shared accounts/sessions/audit have acceptance records. Task operations are local by default. Optional fixed-owner global controls are integrated; an explicit separated controller/Agent profile has initial acceptance, while automatic cross-Agent relocation and the full HA matrix remain open. See multi-node deployment. Domestic database adaptation covers target profiles and source expansion. MySQL is currently the implemented source; PostgreSQL and Oracle sources remain planned. Additional database types require independent source adapters and acceptance. Read implementation status, performance, node registry, shared access and the SDD requirements for exact scope.

title: Connector catalog
text: Sources and targets Check the direction, availability state and exact product profile before selecting a connector. ConnectorCatalog / Relational, analytical and messaging targets have different acknowledgement and recovery protocols. Multiple targets acknowledge independently; messaging consumers still need protocol-level deduplication.
